body.title: [ENG/ESP] The Silverbloggers Chronicles - Prompt # 43/ Cinderella: Favourite Childhood Story
body.body:
My favorite childhood story was, without a doubt, Cinderella. Not only for its fairytale atmosphere and transformations, but also for the values ​​it conveyed, which resonated deeply in my young imagination. At first glance, it seems like a simple princess story, but for me, it was an emotional roadmap for facing adversity.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYoS2rpGsT8fQoifgeNePvZjJpmzFWFg6uk2cmSLvdtGJ/ervnx7lw8aa_76f.jpg)[source](https://x.com/_DNA_L0st/status/1348097774106120192/photo/1)



What captivated me most was Cinderella's resilience. Despite being mistreated by her stepmother and stepsisters, she never became bitter or lost her essential kindness. Every morning, while my toys waited neatly, I thought of her sweeping up the ashes without resentment. That taught me that dignity doesn't depend on how we are treated, but on how we choose to respond. She was a silent heroine, whose strength didn't come from physical power, but from active patience.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWBusUXhCeUnJvP4QPbhhQsx9u3L324E1MYPWERww3Yut/ervnxm_w4ai2daw.jpg)[source](https://x.com/_DNA_L0st/status/1348097768116674565/photo/1)

Another fundamental value was active hope. Cinderella doesn't just sit around weeping passively; she accepts the fairy godmother's help, but she also does her part: she goes to the ball, dances with the prince, and, above all, escapes in time. There's a subtle lesson there: miracles exist, but they require taking the first step. The famous glass slipper symbolizes authenticity for me: you can only be recognized for who you truly are, not for appearances or borrowed clothes.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQy94xU3Lnaitjg6AWsZ5krvAawAbJNiC9AYkFJYDi6CD/ervnxqxxcaawzp0.jpg)[fuente](https://x.com/_DNA_L0st/status/1348097762919911430/photo/1)

Finally, gratitude and kindness without expecting anything in return are the moral core. Cinderella treats the animals well, and they are the ones who help her. This ecological and empathetic principle resonated with me: generosity creates invisible support networks. Furthermore, by forgiving her stepsisters in the end, the story doesn't celebrate revenge, but restorative justice.

Today, as an adult, I understand that Cinderella isn't a letter to Prince Charming, but a manifesto on tenderness as resistance. That's why it was my favorite: because it showed me that even from the ashes, you can dance, and that the greatest magic is not letting the world harden your heart.

Important: The translator is from Google.



ESPAÑOL



Mi cuento favorito de la infancia era, sin duda, Cenicienta. No solo por su atmósfera de hadas y transformaciones, sino por los valores que transmitía, los cuales resonaban profundamente en mi imaginación de niña. A primera vista, parece una simple historia de princesas, pero para mí era un mapa emocional sobre cómo enfrentar la adversidad.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYoS2rpGsT8fQoifgeNePvZjJpmzFWFg6uk2cmSLvdtGJ/ervnx7lw8aa_76f.jpg)[fuente](https://x.com/_DNA_L0st/status/1348097774106120192/photo/1)

Lo que más me cautivaba era la resiliencia de Cenicienta. A pesar de ser maltratada por su madrastra y hermanastras, ella nunca se amargaba ni perdía su bondad esencial. Cada mañana, mientras mis juguetes esperaban ordenados, yo pensaba en ella barriendo las cenizas sin rencor. Eso me enseñó que la dignidad no depende del trato que recibimos, sino de cómo decidimos responder. Era una heroína silenciosa, cuya fortaleza no provenía de la fuerza física, sino de la paciencia activa.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWBusUXhCeUnJvP4QPbhhQsx9u3L324E1MYPWERww3Yut/ervnxm_w4ai2daw.jpg)[fuente](https://x.com/_DNA_L0st/status/1348097768116674565/photo/1)




Otro valor fundamental era la esperanza activa. Cenicienta no se queda llorando pasivamente; acepta la ayuda del hada, pero también pone de su parte: va al baile, baila con el príncipe y, sobre todo, huye a tiempo. Hay una lección sutil ahí: los milagros existen, pero requieren que uno dé el primer paso. El famoso zapato de cristal simboliza para mí la autenticidad: solo puedes ser reconocido por lo que eres realmente, no por las apariencias o los vestidos prestados.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQy94xU3Lnaitjg6AWsZ5krvAawAbJNiC9AYkFJYDi6CD/ervnxqxxcaawzp0.jpg)[fuente](https://x.com/_DNA_L0st/status/1348097762919911430/photo/1)



Por último, la gratitud y la bondad sin esperar recompensa son el eje moral. Cenicienta trata bien a los animalitos, y son ellos quienes la ayudan. Este principio ecológico y empático me marcó: la generosidad crea redes de apoyo invisibles. Además, al perdonar a sus hermanastras al final, el cuento no celebra la venganza, sino la justicia restaurativa.

Hoy, adulta, entiendo que Cenicienta no es una carta al príncipe azul, sino un manifiesto sobre la ternura como resistencia. Por eso fue mi favorito: porque me mostró que incluso desde las cenizas se puede bailar, y que la mayor magia es no dejar que el mundo endurezca tu corazón.


Importante: El traductor es de Google.

body.title: 🇵🇱 Cieszyn 10 km – kontrola, progres i kolejny krok 🏆 /🇬🇧 Cieszyn 10K – control, progress and the next step 🏆 : April 26 2026
body.body:
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/cfcf9887-fe72-445f-b5dd-d642ecdfd8b2.jpg)
Ten start nie był „all-in” na wynik. To był start kontrolny — kolejny element układanki w projekcie SUB40. Cieszyn, 10 km, dobrze znana trasa, ale z małymi zmianami w tym roku. Cel był prosty: pobiec mądrze, utrzymać kontrolę i sprawdzić, gdzie jestem. --- This wasn’t an all-out race. It was a controlled effort — another step in the SUB40 project. Cieszyn, 10K, familiar course with slight changes this year. The goal was simple: run smart, stay in control and see where I am.
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e4555229-47ed-4eb1-be1a-06ccd1e9e498.jpg)
Poranek spokojny, bez nerwów i bez pośpiechu. Lekki posiłek — nic eksperymentalnego, nic ciężkiego. To był jeden z tych dni, gdzie głowa jest czysta: 👉 robisz swoje, bez presji wyniku. Wyjazd ze Szczyrku z zapasem, żeby nie wprowadzać chaosu. Na miejscu byłem około 9:00. Odbiór pakietu na spokojnie, bez kolejek, bez stresu. Czas był po mojej stronie — i to było czuć. --- Calm morning, no rush, no stress. Light breakfast — nothing new, nothing heavy. One of those days where your head is clear: 👉 just do your job, no pressure. Left Szczyrk early to avoid any chaos. Arrived around 9:00. Picked up the race package smoothly. Plenty of time, no stress.
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/8505c85d-449b-43c3-a181-889694527a71.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/a239926f-5630-4613-8296-b99e60f1a892.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/c08e68a6-58f7-420d-89c2-40d4e56d0076.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/b5ef6dfc-c10b-4bea-8637-5033c98a38ff.jpg)
Po odbiorze pakietu zrobiłem spacer — krótki rekonesans. W tym roku trasa była lekko zmieniona przez remont w Czeskim Cieszynie, więc warto było zobaczyć fragmenty „na żywo”. To daje spokój w trakcie biegu: 👉 mniej zaskoczeń = lepsze decyzje. --- After picking up the bib, I went for a short walk. The course had slight changes due to road works in Český Těšín, so it was worth checking it in advance. 👉 fewer surprises = better decisions during the race.
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/91e19387-5aee-4d4a-aa7c-22929794f219.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/1f9f14f2-46a3-4bce-8036-467f3ebe4d82.jpg)
Plan był bardzo konkretny: 👉 0–2 km – wejście w rytm, bez szarpania 👉 2–8 km – stabilna praca progowa 👉 8–10 km – decyzja: czy jest z czego przyspieszyć Priorytet: • kontrola tętna • brak chaosu • zachowanie rezerwy na końcówkę. --- The plan was clear: 👉 0–2 km – settle in 👉 2–8 km – controlled threshold effort 👉 8–10 km – decide and push Priorities: • heart rate control • no surges • save something for the finish

Start (0–2 km) Pierwsze kilometry spokojne, świadomie trzymane. Nie było gonienia tempa ani ludzi. Było pilnowanie własnego rytmu. 👉 to jest moment, gdzie łatwo spalić bieg — tym razem tego nie zrobiłem. Środek biegu (2–8 km) Najważniejszy fragment. Tempo ustabilizowane, oddech pod kontrolą, tętno w zakresie, który znałem z treningów. Nie było walki — była praca. 👉 to był bieg „trzymany”, nie „ratowany” I to jest największa różnica względem wcześniejszych startów. Końcówka (8–10 km) Na 9 km decyzja: dokładam. Tempo w górę, tętno w górę — wchodzę wyżej. Pojawia się charakterystyczny moment: 👉 wydech zaczyna być wymuszony, 👉 pojawia się dźwięk przy każdym oddechu To już jest granica. Ale tym razem: 👉 bez rozpadu 👉 bez ściany 👉 dowiezione do mety --- Start (0–2 km) Controlled from the beginning. No chasing pace, no chasing people. Just holding my rhythm. 👉 this is where races are often ruined — not this time Middle (2–8 km) The key part. Stable pace, controlled breathing, heart rate exactly where expected. No struggle — just work. 👉 this was a “managed” run, not a “survived” one Final part (8–10 km) At 9 km — decision to push. Pace up, HR up. That familiar moment appears: 👉 forced breathing 👉 audible exhale That’s the limit. But this time: 👉 no breakdown 👉 no collapse 👉 strong finish

## 44:42 Złamane 45 minut. Jest życiówka. I co ważniejsze: 👉 pełna kontrola biegu To nie był przypadek — to była świadoma realizacja planu. --- ## 44:42 Sub 45 achieved. New PB. And more importantly: 👉 full control of the race

#### Progres na przestrzeni lat. Ten wynik nie wziął się znikąd. 54:42 → 48:01 → 47:07 → 46:51 → 45:30 → 44:42 👉 5 lat systematycznej pracy Największe skoki są już za mną. Teraz każda minuta to konkretna robota. --- #### Progress over the years This didn’t happen overnight. 54:42 → 48:01 → 47:07 → 46:51 → 45:30 → 44:42 👉 5 years of consistent work Now every minute gained takes real effort.
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/686cd848-f67b-4d73-b20c-04616dcfba50.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/86c50155-41d9-4d90-9538-bccbb3766bf6.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/26aba13c-abc2-49c3-8c68-23e5257486f2.jpg)
### Podsumowanie To był start, który nie miał być spektakularny. Miał być mądry — i taki był. 44 minuty przestają być barierą, zaczynają być standardem. Robota zrobiona. Lecimy dalej 🏃‍♂️🔥 --- ### Conclusion This wasn’t meant to be spectacular. It was meant to be smart — and it was. 44 minutes is no longer a barrier. It’s becoming the baseline. Work done. On to the next one 🏃‍♂️🔥

body.title: Unveiling the Unseen Side of Michael Jackson
body.body:
![f1635e44415b7eb86876ab0d181049b8.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdaHLHc3PB6ZrkTES7rcSWxeD7GAPD2MzjN1MbrZAAhse/f1635e44415b7eb86876ab0d181049b8.jpg)


I can boldly say that Michael Jackson was the first musician I truly knew as a kid. 
, Even though I wasn’t born during the peak of his fame
, I grew up hearing so many stories about him.
Unfortunately, most of what I heard back then were rumors—things that made me dislike him without really knowing the truth. 

There were all kinds of wild claims, and as a kid, I believed them.

But as I grew older, I became curious and decided to find out the truth for myself.

 I started researching his life, reading about his journey, his struggles, and his achievements. The more I learned, the more my perspective changed.
I came to realize that he wasn’t just one of the greatest musicians of all time, but also someone with a genuinely kind and compassionate heart. 

Despite his fame and success, all he seemed to want was love, peace, and to make people happy through his music.


What really stood out to me was his humility. In today’s world, it’s easy to see people become proud or arrogant after gaining just a little success. But Michael Jackson, who was one of the most successful artists in history, carried himself with a level of humility that is rare.

He genuinely cared for children, and all he ever wanted was a better world.
Yet, instead of understanding, he was often met with mockery and judgment about his personality.
If it were ever possible to trade places with any musician just to meet him,
I wouldn’t hesitate—I would do it just to see Michael Jackson face to face.


See you tomorrow wonderful people of hive
Adios amigos ❤️❤️❤️❤️

The days have been going so fast and I fear that one of these days I might not post. Not because I don’t want to or don’t have drawings in stock but just because there are so many things going on simultaneously.

I just got home not quite long ago and I’ve been spending time with my cousins. For some reason they are just pumped up and excited and I don’t want to ruin the fun. So even though I’m stressed and tired, I still have to spend time with them. 
___
And this leads me to today’s sketch. Because I had very little time to draw today, I picked a relatable subject; **The Owl**. When I was younger movies and stories always made this animal mystical and when we saw one near the house we used to chase it away because my Uncles and Aunts used to say it was a bad omen.
As I grew and started reading I discovered that the animal was just misunderstood and that their eyes and rotating neck were not one devilish trait but an evolutionary adaptation.

Another thing that makes me relate with this animal is how well they function at night. I also over the years have become a night person. Owls are amazing creatures and once you get to know them, you see them differently.

# The Ledger of Shadows: A Forensic Exposé on Hive's Super Farm



---

## **BREAKING: The Hive Cartel Unmasked**

There is a particular audacity in continuing the performance after the curtain has fallen.

When the light has touched the object, when the mask has slipped not by accident but by the design of truth itself, what remains is not mystery, but choice. The ledger does not negotiate with denial. The blockchain does not offer the mercy of forgetting. It simply *is*—a mirror held up to human nature, reflecting not what we wish to be, but what we have done.

To keep lying when you have been exposed is not cleverness. It is not strategy. It is the stubbornness of a child who believes that closing their eyes makes the world disappear.

But the world does not disappear.

The truth does not retreat because you refuse to acknowledge it. It waits. It accumulates. It becomes the foundation upon which your next step must be built—whether that step is forward, into integrity, or backward, into the quicksand of self-deception.

You *can* keep lying. The lips are free to shape the falsehood. The keys are free to sign the transaction. But the blockchain will keep recording.

## **II. The Network: A Web of Influence**

**The Connection:**

## **III. The Hashtags: Markers in the Digital Dust**

You point to patterns. You whisper hashtags. You name the accounts.

These are not mere accusations. They are coordinates. They are markers in the digital dust, signaling to those who come after where the path turned toward shadow.

**What the blockchain confirms:**
✓ Systematic downvoting patterns (-0.25% weight, high frequency)
✓ Targeted suppression of specific users and threads
✓ Industrial-scale reward harvesting alongside suppression
✓ Coordination between multiple accounts (voting the same targets)
✓ Delegation networks concentrating voting power
✓ Spam accounts sharing stolen content linked to central farm

**What the blockchain cannot confirm:**
✗ Malicious intent (though the pattern implies it)
✗ Off-line payment agreements
✗ The identity of the operators behind the keys
✗ The motivations, explicit or implicit

**The Gap:**
We see the mechanics. We see the flows. We see the patterns. But we do not see the minds behind the keys. The blockchain is a mirror that reflects actions, not intentions. It shows us *what* happened, but not *why*.

---

## **IV. The Community Impact: A Toxic Environment**

*Based on user reports and platform analytics*

```

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

**The Human Cost:**
Behind every downvoted post is a creator who invested time, thought, and passion. Behind every suppressed voice is a community member who felt unwelcome. Behind every stolen content post is an original artist whose work was taken without permission.

**The Platform Cost:**
When users leave because of toxic behavior, when creators stop posting because their work is suppressed, when the community fractures along lines of power and privilege—what remains of the promise of decentralized social media?

---

## **V. The Call to Action: Accountability and Change**

There is a particular courage in speaking truth to power, even when that power is hidden behind cryptographic keys.

You have pointed to patterns. You have followed the money. You have connected the dots between accounts, between votes, between rewards. You have shown us a system of extraction, a network of influence, a machine that harvests value from the Hive blockchain with industrial efficiency.

But the blockchain, for all its immutability, cannot tell us whether this is abuse or innovation, whether this is scam or strategy, whether this is bullying or business.

That judgment requires something the blockchain does not have: a conscience.

**To Blocktrades:**
We believe that Blocktrades needs to take action to remove their Hive power delegation from Buildawhale and Usainvote. These two accounts have been downvoting good content, driving users away from the platform and creating a toxic environment. We've seen firsthand the damage it can cause, and people are leaving Hive.

**To the Community:**
WE MUST STOP THE @BUILDAWHALE AKA @THEMARKYMARK SCAM FARM DOWNVOTE ABUSE

This is not about silencing dissent. This is about protecting the integrity of the platform. This is about ensuring that Hive remains a place where creators can share their work without fear of systematic suppression.

**To the Whale:**
How can we have a whale downvoting good content, speaking to people in a derogatory manner, and yet still expect to be part of our community? This individual needs help, and they should not be a part of Hive.

---

## **Epilogue: The Unblinking Ledger**

You *can* keep lying.

The vote weight can still be set to `-0.25%`, mechanical and cold, sweeping through the garden like a scythe disguised as a tool. The curation rewards can still be claimed, harvested from the soil of suppressed voices, counted in HP while the community counts the cost.

But the ledger remembers.

It records the rhythm of the downvote farm. It tracks the flow of delegated power. It notes the coordinated cadence of the network, casting hundreds of negative votes in minutes, not against spam, but against specific souls.

It sees the farm. It sees the scam. It sees the mask.

There is a courage in cessation. To stop. To say: *I was wrong. I see now. I will do better.* These are not words of weakness. They are the architecture of redemption.

But if you choose to persist? If you choose to let the hashtags become your epitaph?

Then let them be written clearly. Let the record show not just the lie, but the refusal to cease. Let the tags stand as markers in the digital dust, signaling to those who come after where the path turned toward shadow.

You can keep lying. The blockchain will keep recording.

And in the end, only one of those two things will remain when the noise has faded.

> ## Español Hola a todos! este fin de semana estuve perdida por aquí porque resulta que un viejo amigo (al que tenía más de 7 años sin ver), vino a Polonia a visitarme, se trata de Luis, quien estudió conmigo en la universidad y a quien por supuesto le estaba dedicando mucho tiempo ya que necesitabamos ponernos al día con nuestras vidas y recordar todos esos momentos que vivímos en la universidad y les cuento que la pasamos increíble. Estas fotos son de la primera vez que nos vimos, él llegó el viernes pasado en la noche y decidímos ir a comer al restaurante Pizzeria-Trattoria Stonehenge ubicado en Sosnowiec, Pawel se quedó con Olivia (quien ya estaba dormida) para que yo pudiera ir a disfrutar y hablar con mi amigo, lo cual fue maravilloso porque el tiempo se hizo corto con tanto que teníamos para contarnos, pero debo confesar que me sentía un poco rara ya que era la primera que salía sin Olivia y sin mi esposo a la vez jajaja. Ahora bien, en el restaurante Luis y yo decidimos ordenar una pizza DIAVOLO para compartir, por supuesto era una pizza picante, así que es bueno que a ambos nos gusta este, además ordenamos un par de cervezas que fueron la combinación perfecta para contarnos todo lo que paso en todos estos años, además les cuento que mi mamá y mi hermana estaban muy felices de este encuentro también ya que Luis era muy buen amigo de nosotras y pasamos mucho tiempo juntos en la etapa de la universidad por lo que claro que mi mamá lo conocía. Contar con buenos amigos es genial, y Luis es uno de ellos, ojalá esta visita se vuelva a repetir pronto para que la sigamos pasando increíble, ya que sin duda estos momentos hacen muy bien al alma. ## English Hi everyone! I’ve been MIA this weekend because an old friend (whom I hadn’t seen in over seven years) came to Poland to visit me. His name is Luis; he went to college with me, and of course I spent a lot of time with him since we needed to catch up on our lives and reminisce about all those moments we shared in college. Let me tell you, we had an amazing time. These photos are from the first time we saw each other. He arrived last Friday night, and we decided to go eat at the restaurant Pizzeria-Trattoria Stonehenge in Sosnowiec. Pawel stayed with Olivia (who was already asleep) so I could go enjoy myself and talk with my friend, which was wonderful because time flew by with so much we had to tell each other, but I have to admit I felt a little weird since it was the first time I’d gone out without Olivia and without my husband at the same time, hahaha. Anyway, at the restaurant, Luis and I decided to order a DIAVOLO pizza to share—of course, it was a spicy pizza— so it’s a good thing we both like it. We also ordered a couple of beers, which were the perfect combination for catching up on everything that’s happened over the years. I should also mention that my mom and my sister were very happy about this reunion too, since Luis was a very good friend of ours and we spent a lot of time together in college, so of course my mom knew him. Having good friends is great, and Luis is one of them. I hope we can do this again soon so we can keep having an amazing time, since moments like these are definitely good for the soul.

body.body:
Splinterland's : One of the interesting, reckless battle.
---------------------------------------------------------

I guess, I had already written about the strategy that can be used when we are playing the reckless ruleset, and playing the no attack monster and monster having taunt with good health and in a non-attacking position is one of the good options to be used. Since this is the ranked frontier battle , so options become really limited but still we have \
in frontier card sent and can be used. But along with reckless ruleset has \
that means the card having taunt will suffer double damage. At this point, I decided that I will not be going with the taunt ability.\n\n

/>  
[Source](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_404834f3e1d91610822b08e64b33dcc3)

So I decided to use a melee monster \
in position 5, from where it cannot attack, and \

at the last position, just wondering this dual attack monster to be the last survivor in the battle. If you look closely, the use of Port Guardian is the only difference in the team created, Also my choice of position of \
is also a major change.\n\n

/> [Source](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_404834f3e1d91610822b08e64b33dcc3) We both lost our tank in round 1 and both used the same monster as tank i.e Asel Alagosdil. Actually it is a good choice in frontier battles. With 5 monsters on both sides, the battle looks fairly balanced.

/>  
[Source](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_404834f3e1d91610822b08e64b33dcc3)

What was once looking like a fairly balanced battle in round 2 started looking as easy win for my opponent at the start of round 3 as my opponent has 4 monsters against the 1.

So it is an easy win for my opponent? Actually no, because here starts the thrill of reckless and dual attack, my opponents Water Logged Wizard attacked first and took down its own \
with it. My dual attack took opponents Saltwater Mage and Mystic Scaleweaver. So in the fourth round, it was 1 vs 1.\n\n

/> [Source](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_404834f3e1d91610822b08e64b33dcc3) Since, I attacked first, I won the battle, and if you want to enjoy the battle then here is [Link to battle](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_404834f3e1d91610822b08e64b33dcc3) It is an interesting contest, and based on the position of the monsters the result of battle can swings at anyone favour and actually this aspect of the game does make the game interesting to play.

/>

If you have not played Splinterlands or will be returning player, then I will say let give Splinterlands a try. If you like to read more of my recent Splinterland's post, then please find the link below.

title.title: 🌸 A little shopping at Traki || Unas pequeñas compras en Traki 🌸
title.body: >Hello! Hello! Friends of good taste and elegance, I greet you hoping that you will accompany me in this wonderful shopping post that I made at one of my favorite clothing stores, which has always understood the anatomy of my body, because I think that EVERYTHING it sells fits me 😊.

>These days there was a crazy price reduction in many stores if you paid with a credit app; Traki offered this credit, so if you bought $100, you only paid around $20 that day. That’s why I wanted to go and see what they had for me this time.

>My main goal was to look for some jeans; my mother had told me that the ones I have already look worn out. Certainly, I have looked in other stores, but two things happen: either they don’t fit me well, or they are too expensive; some exceed $40. At Traki, I have always found jeans for under $20, so that was what I was going for.Furthermore, the 'denim fashion' reached its women's department, so I had a higher chance of finding what I wanted.

>Even though I tried on many garments of that material, I only kept a basic pair of jeans. The reason is that I didn't need them; I have been getting rid of a lot of clothes that take up space and have already fulfilled their cycle, but I also don't want to fill myself with clothes that I know I won't use soon.
I prefer to get rid of what I don't wear, wear the clothes I have to make the most of them, and then focus on changing my wardrobe. However, I did come away with the conviction to get a denim shirt, which I feel is missing from my closet:
>

>¡Hola! ¡Hola! Amigas del buen gusto y la elegancia, les saludo esperando que me acompañen en esta maravillosa publicación de compras que realicé en una de mis tiendas favoritas de ropa que siempre ha entendido la anatomía de mi cuerpo, porque pienso que TODO lo que vende se adapta a mí 😊. En estos días hubo una locura de rebaja de precios en muchas tiendas si se compraba con una app de crédito; Traki ofrecía este crédito, así que si comprabas $100, solo cancelabas ese día unos $20. Por eso quise ir a ver qué ofrecía para mí en esta oportunidad.
>

>Mi principal objetivo era buscar unos jeans; mi madre me había dicho que los que tengo ya lucen como desgastados. Ciertamente, he buscado en otras tiendas, pero suceden dos cosas: o no me quedan bien, o son muy costosos; algunos exceden los $40. En Traki siempre he conseguido jeans por debajo de los $20, así que iba por ellos. Además, la \

llegó a su departamento de damas, así que tenía una mayor probabilidad de encontrar lo que quería. Aunque me medí muchas prendas de ese material, solo me quedé con un jeans básico. La razón es que no las necesitaba; he estado sacando mucha ropa que me ocupa espacio y ya cumplió su ciclo, pero tampoco me quiero llenar con ropa que sé que no usaré en un tiempo próximo. Prefiero salir de lo que no me pongo, ponerme mi ropa que tengo para sacarle su máximo provecho y después, enfocarme en cambiar mi guardarropa. Sin embargo, sí quedé con la convicción de ir por una camisa de jeans, que siento su falta en mi armario:
-----

>Another piece of clothing I bought was a palazzo-type pant. It has become one of my favorite styles because of how comfortable, cool, and elegant it looks with almost any shirt. I tried on several, but based on what I told you earlier, I already have about 3, and since brown is in fashion, I decided to get it just because I don't have that color 😇. I will wear it for the first time tomorrow for a trip, and I want to be comfortable but presentable 😉:
\n\n>

>Otra prenda de ropa que compré fue un pantalón tipo palazzo. Se ha vuelto uno de mis estilos favoritos por lo cómodo, fresco y elegante que se ven con casi cualquier camisa. Me medí varios, pero partiendo de lo que les dije anteriormente, ya tengo unos 3 y, como el marrón está de moda, entonces decidí solo porque no tengo ese color 😇. Me lo estrenaré mañana que tengo un viaje y quiero ir cómoda pero presentable 😉:
-----

>One-piece swimsuits OMG! one-piece swimsuits short or long, are a trend that Traki always has for those days when we have all the clothes on the bed and we don't know what to wear, because that's how we are 😊. I tried on two, I liked both, I bought both. Its price was less than $10 each; I already released one and the other I'm waiting for an outing with my J.J. to wear it as it is 😍:
>

>Las bragas, ¡DIOS MÍO! Las bragas, cortas o largas, son una tendencia que siempre tiene Traki para aquellos días donde tenemos toda la ropa sobre la cama y no sabemos qué ponernos, porque así somos 😊. Me probé dos, me gustaron las dos, compré las dos. Su precio fue menos de $10 cada una; una ya me la estrené y la otra estoy esperando una salida con mi J.J. para lucirla como es 😍:
------

>Finally, since I started going to the gym, I need A LOT OF SPORTS CLOTHES and Traki has an entire section dedicated to exercise; unfortunately, I see that it is clothing for paddle or running and not for my body. I took the opportunity and bought some leggings and I hope to go soon to take a better look to expand my sports clothing 😉:
>

>Por último, ya que inicié el gym, necesito MUCHA ROPA DEPORTIVA y Traki tiene toda una sección dedicada al ejercicio; lamentablemente, veo que es ropa como para pádel o correr y no para mi cuerpo. Aproveché y compré una licra y espero ir pronto a revisar mejor para ampliar mi ropa deportiva 😉:
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/florecitamejias/23y8z6Ya7FXvtNsTQ8jgZuZ6HuSB57sqKabXM9ZK2ypuFUgRQJQZuQTWLsMLTPhh6U6Xn.jpeg ---- ![FM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/florecitamejias/23wXSdeCjyWqFNmVJN1CZC5wGmM4zitBAnVVuPtiQs9yubkH9BdzqfuXENZuTAx9Yqzjk.png)

>I left the store very happy and joyful. Checking it out took me about 3 hours and more than 20 items measured; as always, I left a long list of clothes I want to buy, but for now, at least I fulfilled the rule that everything I bought I truly need and am using 😍. The total expense was $70 because I also purchased other products like towels, some household utensils, and some gifts for my friends; everything under control 😎.
_Thank you for reading. The photos are my property. I made the cover, the banner, and the divider in Canva. The translator I used was Traductor Google._
# Until next time 🌸 >

>Yo salí muy contenta y feliz de la tienda. Revisarla me tomó unas 3 horas y más de 20 piezas medidas; como siempre, dejé una gran lista de prendas que quiero comprar, pero por ahora, al menos cumplí con la regla de que todo lo que compré verdaderamente lo necesito y lo estoy usando 😍. El gasto total fue de $70 porque adquirí otros productos como toallas, algunos utensilios para el hogar y unos regalos para mis amigas; todo bajo control 😎. Gracias por tu lectura. Las fotografías son de mi propiedad. La portada, el banner y el separador los hice en Canva. El traductor que usé fue Google Traductor. Hasta una próxima oportunidad 🌸.

body.title: Monday Walk
body.body:
My wife and I are relaxing on the island of Pag on a beautiful sunny day with a temperature of 24°C. This weather is just begging for some kind of activity. At least a walk. So we went for a walk, not far, along the path that leads to the main road around the hill.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmer22nF6Ki3Qv1ENvNfU79CQKTVmwZo3PrkJ7zBd8Hx3Y/mond1a.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYBiyKzMWZt5yUbQyx8iZidTXL7FVnVHVzzXAqhkyC7cu/mond2.jpg)

Actually, my wife wanted to see if the immortelle (Helichrysum italicum, a Mediterranean medicinal plant with yellow flowers that don’t wilt) and sage (Salvia officinalis, used in cooking and teas) were in bloom. 
The island of Pag is known for these. Everything smells wonderful, and we really enjoyed the intoxicating scents along the way.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXrqCVRwyesCQmCKdGJH6JQBTJuk5hZAd6QrJQ9rvb3Xh/mond3.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXJ4a54WiRZpFHSjGMxMUu4ZiMPfUDEunesN27EKB4TTQ/mond4.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNWrSHk6Z2xAcKg8czkEthAeq1R5swEjzipEAAMLg8VFV/mond5.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcEKnwiegYDSNpaevU8f6LE7TiUdbVWWToKgBuZqsK24R/mond5a.jpg)

The skeleton of a bird, most likely a seagull — at least that’s what Grok says.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPt44SC1z8CRZ8jmcj6xDKePdr7bGkw4RuqGubhq4qxRT/mond6.jpg)

<center>📷 😎 📷</center>

Typical stone fences that landowners use to enclose their plots. Just rocks and herbs — you rarely find anything else on this rocky side of the island.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeYvFjUXGtLdVaZ9DnQMJhtnMCD8jsFnuKjpP3rg2X4mH/mond7.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUGqcy4SZotLDU1djy4ixBxQsfDNQaoh8VuX1tSWRBcbt/mond1.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQAb5oRWG8qvLQToM48puZrWCGToDaeWGyuPZjd7BUXfh/mond9.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX4oYzfSisZGVHmrmimvXKQF3AmsaHE4t2dzBXJUMNbMd/mond10.jpg)

<center>📷 😎 📷</center>

We’re now at the top, on the island’s main road; it’s ten kilometers to the town of Novalja to the right and fifteen kilometers to the town of Pag to the left.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZrAZqvJFD65RZyyP9BuH5bfXpeqQYfoXX1V9V76ow1d2/mond11.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfKwGt6hNQm3NgkhCRWS3cBL2AAtYCjihoEFTmMjVF7Y1/mond12.jpg)

Let’s head back down to the coast, but take a different route — the gravel road. There are beautiful views of Pag Bay, with the Velebit Mountains on the mainland in the background.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSzfDYNm6VfqK5HogW6BrNzFw5nE7Hax5gtF2qbAs6emf/mond13.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaN4WRrGxYmahVnAgLApGRGk62i6r4gtjzvgc1i93QG4Y/mond14.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeUzSXs3rSpBfx2tnDwC3jeEC1ptrqPAm2tCYkMR5hzRH/mond15.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeM2ZjTH9gqRNMnnu1GmLazq2a2NzEu55cXnZShTUwEK1/mond16.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYV5VrgXEF4XvzR1EmHzLwxhWeAsXQMm5L94GH3GCYRED/mond16a.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcrbvy7L2iQo4nfvF9h5rW3ZWeRrSq66cm8UnzDw4HKfw/mond17.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXgLnvL8pdD1Hy4iuXNPxH5uJjyy6sjJusvARFMzFarMQ/mond17a.jpg)

<center>📷 😎 📷</center>

Almost back on the coast.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme5JicvNb1viR9aYERM72dpfWfUw1LE4vrVGjHSg5vhA8/mond19.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWA6SbcuujfR6imx4hSqWbw64gZdkKHLUKUMDVBs8E9Bm/mond18.jpg)

And to finish off, a dip in the sea. It’s 16°C — still too cold for swimming — but in a week or two, if the sun keeps shining like this, it’ll be possible.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaqvnXS1eQaf8hzZtGyoKJKqPHNF7hK5FrxQmKfMxmoPA/mond19a.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTMHECweVQgYWGSHxvekeyvwh5weRJWbmbZnsy3QZrPNr/mond20.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcxjQuNGipHhqyM4T1eG8H9RRLkSRp3gySBgkUBuECJjm/mond21.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTfPKRDJJyaH1FMvZxhebboRh16EcMEatzNNvELVHwUta/mond22.jpg)

Thank you for your attention!

body.title: Greenhouse news 2
body.body:
I was writing a garden journal yesterday and I totally forgot to mention the greenhouse. Definitely too many plants :) Of course you can never have enough.
My wife has prepared a lot of flowers that will go in our garden, she has picked them in pots and will then plant them next to the peas, peppers and wherever else they are needed.
Currently there are marigolds and nasturtium.
![20260427_175541.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKScPKDDgf3CgJaMGwoXaRUpnnEnzrAC7HymKfkPtMeW6PF1Atof4jrFiduaiGM.jpg)

![20260427_175606.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKCG4hamqtF5SddLg9UQFL4TP18cbnEcgzEbTWM4Vi1x9ND2A1ss94ZQfqakqCt.jpg)
Night-Scented Stock is currently growing nicely and will soon be ready to transplant. It is a small, unsightly plant but it smells wonderful at night. My wife loves it.
![20260427_175545.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKLsTsccekftw7SQYz7JK1hKqpKpK3s533DoHbGZ3rwuTUHq9SeRVphmCj3SqZo.jpg)
My wife pickled the elephant ear pepper. And we pickled it with willow water, the results are good. We have another type of sweet pepper left, the Macedonian ajvarusha. We will probably pickle it tomorrow.
![20260427_175619.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKtSvSSWRNvqWVs8AHghw4Twm9aefX8qCe8hGCgTdBt1Dwc4A6NXv81Zotz6ewD.jpg)
We grew both types of melons. Pineapple melon and honeydew melon.
![20260427_175633.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKDhCb9FjCib5hFgDD6sNyxqox86GBNbxBNJSiTTTveqTSeFEAD8TpNigMk4e1T.jpg)
As you can see in the picture, the soil dries out quickly, the small greenhouse quickly raises the temperature, since even my fan did not help to lower the temperature. My wife cut the nylon and made another door that did not exist in the factory.
![20260427_175624.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKWv3b9CMWzKGQD8Wv7hDdbNnjEXZuQMCxhmNKEtqXfY8f8kVN97X8XHirUGevQ.jpg)
Although we talked about the fact that we might have to cut the nylon
She cut the nylon wrong. Now we have a little problem closing the greenhouse on that side. Although I'm usually the one who does things like that, she took the title with one stroke of the scalpel :)

The radishes and both types of lettuce have gone wild, they are really full of leaves. The myrtle has also sprouted next to them, and we have also planted cherries in the greenhouse in several places.
![20260427_175555.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKApoHmyKc6AYtMgi6YoZVm24xombKLWeP5XxUxujKqesKMNP5AGkwcnz3sR86t.jpg)


![20260427_175601.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AJpj97iWQ5rCeApXxSEe7wUePZwc2eNnCnack3JQ5Zd9JNAgjzLqGUG6wK4ZEc2.jpg)Strawberries in the greenhouse are excellent![20260427_175611.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AK3eHGvyYQkjRDaNnvZ6qVeAhMZgimAhaJGWG6Lq2Uv9CL2xXrYcPonWzyzyQyw.jpg)A few days before this post I noticed that the lettuce in the greenhouse was missing, half the leaves were torn off, but I didn't know who was to blame.
And then I found the culprit eating fresh lettuce for lunch. It was my son.


![20260418_154707.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKSd3PcmnaQArM2Uu2qHQmiALgDCYCjUtdEumE9NRHFAgbYxQgVC7tuiqaJPdRR.jpg)

---
Thanks for reading.
Until next time.
Stay healthy.
Markone85.
---

body.title: Gesunder Menschenverstand und Arbeitssicherheit
body.body:
Hallo Freunde,

wisst ihr, ich finde es immer wieder lustig das man mehr oder weniger sagen kann, die Arbeitssicherheit lässt sich durch Gesunden Menschenverstand ersetzen. Das Problem ist, die meisten Menschen denken nicht soweit wie es notwendig wäre. Ich meine wer von uns hat sich noch nie gedacht, ich mache mal schnell und dann steht man auf einmal da und ist tief in die Scheiße gestürtzt. Klassiker ist der Sturz vom Drehstuhl. Man soll eine Leiter verwenden, aber am Ende landet man an einem Punkt, wo die halt ein Stockwerk weiter unten ist und schon fliegt man auf die Schnauze, weil man den Stuhl der gerade im Raum ist nutzt und der halt nicht so stabil ist oder sich eben wegbewegen kann. 

Und so ist es bei viele. Vor allem wenn man gerade gestresst ist, vergisst man auch gerne mal drei Meter nach links und rechts zu schauen und schon werden Sachen übersehen. Oder man weiß bestimmte Sachen nicht. Ich meine am Ende muss man z.b. bei Generatoren darauf achten, dass man sie nicht im Betrieb betankt, da die Gase in Kombination mit der Hitze des Generators zu einer Explosion führen können. Oder man vergisst die Zelte zu verankern und schon beginnen sie davon zu fliegen und das bringt einige Probleme mit sich. Ich meine wer will von einem Zelt erschlagen werden? Man unterschätzt dann sehr schnell, welche Kräfte sich dabei entwickeln können. 

Also in dem Sinne, schaut in die Arbeitssicherheit, die Regeln dort sind mit Blut geschrieben, sie entstehen indem man sich anschaut, wo was schief gelaufen ist und wie man das verhindern kann. Also in dem Sinne, gehabt euch wohl.

# The Hive Cartel Exposed: A Forensic Investigation into Systematic Abuse



---



There is a particular audacity in continuing the performance after the curtain has fallen.

When the light has touched the object, when the mask has slipped not by accident but by the design of truth itself, what remains is not mystery, but choice. The ledger does not negotiate with denial. The blockchain does not offer the mercy of forgetting. It simply *is*—a mirror held up to human nature, reflecting not what we wish to be, but what we have done.

To keep lying when you have been exposed is not cleverness. It is not strategy. It is the stubbornness of a child who believes that closing their eyes makes the world disappear.

But the world does not disappear.

The truth does not retreat because you refuse to acknowledge it. It waits. It accumulates. It becomes the foundation upon which your next step must be built—whether that step is forward, into integrity, or backward, into the quicksand of self-deception.

You *can* keep lying. The lips are free to shape the falsehood. The keys are free to sign the transaction. But the blockchain will keep recording.

And in the end, only one of those two things will remain when the noise has faded.

---

## **I. The Evidence: A Mechanical Symphony of Suppression**

*Based on on-chain transaction logs (Pasted_Text_1774476471429.txt)*

### **Figure 1: The Curation Farming Engine (@buildawhale)**

```

Analyst Note: This is not organic curation. This is a machine calibrated to extract value from the reward pool with metronomic precision.
```

**The Implication:**
When curation becomes industrial, when rewards are harvested rather than earned through spontaneous appreciation, what happens to the soul of the platform? The blockchain does not judge. It only records.

### **Figure 2: The Downvote Cartel (Coordinated Suppression)**

While @buildawhale farms, the wider network suppresses. The logs reveal a coordinated effort to mute specific voices while the cartel extracts value.

```

body.title: ¿Arsenal o Manchester City?
body.body:
> The 2026 Premier League title race will be a historic battle between Arsenal and Manchester City: the Gunners lead with 73 points from 34 matches, while City have 70 with one game in hand. The difference is minimal, and every goal could decide the title.

The race is incredibly close. To give you an idea, here's the current situation of both teams in numbers. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV2rh52LmnfAdNcHKdEuKMTW2nZBRxrpXCdKEpZ6VZMz1/675150712_1522252446450648_1890770509112530502_n.jpg)[source](https://www.facebook.com/Apasionadosmex/photos/-impresionante-si-arsenal-y-manchester-city-ganan-todos-los-partidos-que-quedan-/1522252413117318/) Arsenal: 73 points in 34 matches, goal difference +38. Manchester City: 70 points in 33 matches, goal difference +37. Both teams could finish tied on points; the tiebreakers would be goal difference, goals scored, and head-to-head results. Arsenal: Strengths and Weaknesses Strengths: Solid defense: only 26 goals conceded, the best back line in the league. Return of Bukayo Saka: his return from injury revitalizes the attack and boosts team morale. Resilience: Key victory against Newcastle to regain the lead. Weaknesses: Psychological pressure: After losses against City and Bournemouth, confidence wavered. Demanding schedule: In addition to the Premier League, they must play the Champions League semi-finals against Atlético de Madrid. History: They haven't won the league in 22 years, which adds emotional weight. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmduGgifU7EdwTBjWHXcMyfnTzs4grid2TuZVpLS55WmR5/679381733_1511574270330321_8570546217614724681_n.jpg)[source](https://www.facebook.com/AFTVMedia/photos/premier-league-run-in-revealed-arsenal-vs-manchester-city-fixture-battle-compare/1511574266996988/) Manchester City: Strengths and weaknesses Strengths: Devastating attack: 66 goals scored, with Haaland decisive in key matches. Winning experience: Guardiola and his squad know how to manage the end of the season. Favorable schedule: A game in hand against Crystal Palace and mid-table opponents like Burnley, Everton, and Bournemouth. Weaknesses: Less solid defense: 29 goals conceded, slightly worse than Arsenal. Competition load: In addition to the Premier League, they are also playing in the FA Cup final. Haaland dependence: If the Norwegian gets injured or his performance dips, the attack loses its edge. Prediction Arsenal has a slight advantage in points and a more solid defense, but faces greater pressure and a Champions League schedule that could take its toll. Manchester City has a game in hand, more goals scored, and the experience of having won titles in similar situations. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcjM6uGY2qfJ2wxEMhykxvvkAcSaToq93ksrT8mWuunGH/655725276_1399163688922788_5055990926261322025_n.jpg)[source](https://www.facebook.com/ManCityMEN/photos/-arsenal-vs-man-city-live-cup-final-build-up-early-team-news-how-to-watch-for-fr/1399163685589455/) In summary Although Arsenal leads, Manchester City seems to have a better chance of being crowned champion thanks to their schedule, their attacking prowess, and Guardiola's experience in late-season matches. However, the difference is so narrow that a slip-up or a decisive goal could tip the scales in favor of the Gunners. Credits: I used Google Translate.

body.title: Errores silenciosos en Web3: que pueden ponerte en riesgo
body.body:
<center>![1000933426.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliento/23vi1oqh2QzBq19jrEnyYro2B1XcVRHHZfiXcmRoxktdbRE7ShFFcfUT4AUDYJ3uXUeaX.png)</center>

---

<div class=text-justify>

¡Saludos, comunidad!

Cuando pensamos en seguridad digital en Web3, solemos imaginar grandes errores comunes: compartir llaves, caer en estafas o perder el acceso a una cuenta. Pero muchas veces, los mayores riesgos no vienen de lo evidente, sino de lo cotidiano.

Existen pequeñas acciones que repetimos sin pensar, y que poco a poco pueden abrir la puerta a problemas mayores. Estas acciones las realizamos como algo normal, pero realmente nos ponen en riesgo.

<center>![17770716734297748330880250389947.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliento/EoEjFUZhAvvnHRTt412VSgak1mTBn2L3k6ZB41nHxxffMJKuXTRt4AzQunsucX3SMgw.png)</center>

En Web3 existen lo que podemos llamar errores silenciosos: hábitos que parecen inofensivos, pero que afectan directamente nuestra seguridad.

#### Algunos de los errores silenciosos más comunes:

👉🏻 **Dejar sesiones abiertas:**

Esto es algo que se veía más en los tiempos de los cyber café, pero aunque parezca increíble, en la actualidad también puede darse. Usar tu cuenta en un dispositivo compartido o no cerrar sesión puede parecer algo menor, pero deja tu acceso expuesto.

👉🏻 **Guardar información sensible sin protección:**

Anotar llaves, contraseñas o datos importantes en lugares visibles o sin seguridad es más común de lo que parece. Y si cargas estos datos contigo, en caso de una perdida de documentos, puedes estar expuesto.

👉🏻 **Conectarte desde redes poco seguras:**

Usar WiFi público sin precaución puede facilitar que tu información sea interceptada. Esto es un error muy común en la actualidad, ya que a veces decidimos conectarnos a una red pública por \

el Internet como beneficio, sin darnos cuenta que ponemos en riesgo nuestra privacidad e información ante terceros. 👉🏻 **No revisar herramientas o accesos:** Instalar extensiones, usar plataformas nuevas o conectar tu cuenta sin verificar también suma riesgo. Esto también sucede cuando autorizamos aplicaciones en nuestros dispositivos, muchas veces damos permisos que ni siquiera nos tomamos el tiempo de leer para qué son o serán usados.
![17770716734297748330880250389947.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliento/EoEjFUZhAvvnHRTt412VSgak1mTBn2L3k6ZB41nHxxffMJKuXTRt4AzQunsucX3SMgw.png)
#### Pero hay un error silencioso que atraviesa a todos los demás: 👉🏻 **Actuar con prisa:** Responder rápido, hacer clic sin revisar, realizar una transacción a prisa, confiar sin verificar, muchas veces no es por desconocimiento, sino por apuro. La prisa nos hace bajar la atención y puede llevarte incluso a perder tus activos, por hacer una transacción equivocadamente. Y en Web3, eso es suficiente para cometer un error. Mensajes que parecen urgentes, enlaces que “no pueden esperar”, decisiones rápidas, todo eso juega en contra de tu seguridad. Por eso, más que saber mucho, lo importante es detenerse a tiempo.
![17770716734297748330880250389947.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliento/EoEjFUZhAvvnHRTt412VSgak1mTBn2L3k6ZB41nHxxffMJKuXTRt4AzQunsucX3SMgw.png)
En Proyecto Aliento creemos que la seguridad no se trata solo de evitar grandes errores, sino aprender de ellos y prestar atención a los pequeños hábitos del día a día. Porque en Web3, cuidarte no siempre es hacer algo complejo, sino evitar lo que parece insignificante. Tu seguridad también se construye en esos pequeños detalles. --- || |:-:| |

body.title: A magical experience in the Resava cave in Serbia
body.body:
Hello everyone. A few weeks ago I went on a one-day trip to central-eastern Serbia with my family. It was a national holiday and the non-working day. We visited three fascinating spots, and the first one I will write about today is the Resava cave.

![IMG_20260410_162826.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoEoZLZmYqctHWQ6UXYirK8ocPpbzyymq7EsB42KfVSc946NbvrRph853U1kTnuMCQa.jpg)

While we were walking towards the cave, we enjoyed the natural surroundings, winding roads, dense forest, and a sense of calm that grew stronger with every kilometer. When we arrived, the surroundings were peaceful, almost untouched.

![IMG_20260410_152321.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqFsSjK5LiwsZ8Q4UhoT8zrWynZNt435XTgpmTKU2JRsy2onmeTFarhet8zDU4dPJWW.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_152420.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpzyDF4C5p53KVfXXNZtCrcN75huvewU4y2dm7kqydGZbz7U16iMZBwQVi2GLvgaB12.jpg)

There were very few people and only the sounds of nature.

![IMG_20260410_153348.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqDjbKddEWyyHb7MHP96tLcL9pZozBXbcoTbDHt4ZiSgrQpaXs2GcnhQHX9jGkacCis.jpg)

While waiting for our turn to enter, we spent time reading the information boards nearby. They described the fascinating ecosystem inside the cave, tiny bats, insects adapted to complete darkness, and unique microorganisms that survive in conditions we can hardly imagine.

![IMG_20260410_153257.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoCj1axcvvPiaYPksGSKKAPFpKhU7crYiQtEKLJqhfeVvYgYKVepVE1AzadGpn3JMsP.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_153252.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogPoQn1VQPrcbuBR2nAXWwf2fKWzVAVLdhaJ2CpeTBjoNX8G6NR9Cs7as4QEqe5TcX.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_153302.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoCj1aZcbpZRL6ibhmif8TyL1MFFvmF1xN5A7mAL8X6YqeeHuuu7HiUJYGaHh8XWzMK.jpg)

It made the anticipation even stronger, knowing that this wasn't just a tourist spot, but a living, breathing natural wonder. Finally, it was the turn of our tour. People from the previous group left full of impressions. And my kids couldn't wait to go in. My daughter said she is not afraid of insects and would like to see a bat. 😊 

![IMG_20260410_153241.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoAag7WT2qT1hPLvhG9daqht4M4g6z9eMPqMim3UiLVqhQq9NDbuVtPh1Pjo8WC2H7G.jpg)

Stepping inside the cave was like entering another dimension. The temperature dropped, the light softened, and everything became still.

![IMG_20260410_164803.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoAYJpwaKbJuPe2TEjnmsv9PTgv3QQ76TvqTiM1YVWUy6rJrdQFmf6Eba2DvwdfGQfg.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_161214.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo6JS5aFZDXn8pgnivzaTPduEfRVBbcH7KiKqemTKfrtyzifdFhJUu13gnyHGW8sK7v.jpg)

The formations were breathtaking, stalactites and stalagmites shaped over thousands of years, creating natural sculptures that looked almost unreal.

![IMG_20260410_161528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoEo9xRmX6XgCfn4HyUaprX85Tfbpt3z8WbvxpLuMrTPS6YGnwMvXkdBrD1BN6XCaGu.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_161427.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoiTEP6un76dWf8ZR7XPWgwda1X8d9v6imvaQYAoDB7TjZNp3n5hWpZfsrxRbP62toK.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_161128.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep5kHF8bNLfRuaTam8exPfubLiinGm15L1ys3QmiWhufga6MrsyUGsa9GrB6BUHYX2x.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_161550.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogLs2i3Z9ntSjgSmnTdxAmdC1BZKh6u2XZvsD8QAtL8ARNtfS4AJQCmGHjwMPnHpb5.jpg)

Each chamber had its own character, with textures and colors that changed subtly as we moved deeper inside. We were fascinated.

![IMG_20260410_161611.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep5mgw4Swm3SnAPYqbBDEybAESmRVSbNuBm8CTjjn67eCKRwnu2ABycwgi3ACo6Uve5.jpg)

The last time I was there was as a 9-year-old child on a school excursion, but then I looked at it with different eyes. Now I was completely enchanted. And my kids were amazed, curious, and full of questions. For them, it felt like an adventure, like discovering a secret underground kingdom.

![IMG_20260410_161921.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoJz7SmmBuCe1mw4i2e1cnXS5NjPYqAxbbUiTMQqYERCEUc2JSuPFYdj84xfy1LjDN4.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_162222.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EokbA9QZPwwjGdR4CEeNHqqokYBgvhpxbfpb3U3TmXSmLNPAnXHgndbnCnxGddFaNe5.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_161848.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo6HXXzc4DgyPASXh54dGhxdc9AdxqnMo5j147FuFLYXh89kfM4VCX6bXrGPdrgMHfe.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_162116.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGwSpL22Cu4h4T1nk8umw2qC5pFiWy1EA2EFWT5HdYCJTK5GtbzpAgQo39GiWXGEdc.jpg)

Their excitement made us slow down and appreciate every detail even more.

![IMG_20260410_162612.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo8Qrijo4n8v4hgfdz6aL7EKMA9ydhrJ19MrBQ9qL6Pe6NXmb1AunxL47DxNmoehVxo.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_162353.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo8RqGojZPBpMeTpHTPgESFkoJd7tCjzRoDn2wBzLjRW5qR5APd3dt73HWxvPEuAv5L.jpg)

![IMG_20260410_162602.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep1WSMYtaGAqNvGQU5XDVPZVLJZjgz3Mqy4zZqwKekyxBMH5acS7MMMcB3DufibYJpM.jpg)

We descended 80 meters underground and visited 8 fascinating halls, each of which has its own story and unique sculptures.

# Learn Zig Series (#31) - Memory-Mapped I/O and Files

## Solutions to Episode 30 Exercises

**Exercise 1** - Thread pool with 4 workers, task queue, submit and shutdown:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{});
}
```

The key insight is the shutdown protocol: the main thread waits until both the queue is empty AND no tasks are active. Then it sets the shutdown flag and broadcasts on the condition to wake any waiting workers. The atomic `active_tasks` counter ensures we never see more than 4 active tasks simultaneously -- the thread pool itself enforces this since there are exactly 4 worker threads.

**Exercise 2** - Read-write lock with readers/writers:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{mapped[0..@min(80, mapped.len)]});
}
```

Let me walk through the parameters:

- **`null`** -- we don't care where in our address space the mapping goes. The OS picks a suitable address. You CAN pass a specific address as a hint but there's rarely a reason to.
- **`file_size`** -- how many bytes to map. This gets rounded up to the nearest page boundary internally. If your file is 5000 bytes on a system with 4096-byte pages, the mapping will actually be 8192 bytes, but only the first 5000 bytes correspond to file data. Accessing the padding bytes between file_size and the page boundary gives you zeros; they're not written back to disk.
- **`posix.PROT.READ`** -- protection flags. `READ` for read-only, `READ | WRITE` for read-write. If you open the file read-only but request write protection, you get a permission error.
- **`.{ .TYPE = .SHARED }`** -- mapping type. `SHARED` means changes are visible to other processes mapping the same file and get written back to disk. `PRIVATE` means you get a copy-on-write mapping -- writes modify your in-memory copy only.
- **`file.handle`** -- the file descriptor. Just the `.handle` field from the opened file.
- **`0`** -- byte offset into the file where the mapping starts. Must be page-aligned.

The return type is `[]align(std.mem.page_size) u8` -- a byte slice aligned to the page size. You use it like any other slice. And the `defer posix.munmap(mapped)` at line 21 ensures we clean up when we're done. We talked about `defer` for memory cleanup back in [episode 7](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-7-memory-management-and-allocators) -- same principle applies here. Mapped memory is a resource, and failing to unmap it is a resource leak just like failing to free an allocation.

## Reading large files efficiently

The real power of mmap shows when you're processing large files. Instead of reading chunks into a buffer and processing them, you just iterate over the mapped slice:

```zig
const std = @import(\

interface needed.\n\nFor performance, the OS handles read-ahead behind the scenes. When you touch page N, the kernel often prefetches pages N+1, N+2, etc., anticipating sequential access. On Linux you can hint the access pattern with `posix.madvise` -- `.sequential` tells the kernel \

, and `.willneed` asks the kernel to preload specific pages. For a file scanner like this, `madvise(.sequential)` can improve throughput on spinning disks quite a bit. On SSDs the difference is smaller since random access is cheap anyway.

## Modifying files through memory mappings

To write through a mapping, open the file with write access and add `PROT.WRITE` to the protection flags:

```zig
const std = @import(\

but shared still shows original data
}
```

The shared mapping still sees the original file data because the private mapping's writes went to a private copy of those pages. This is the same copy-on-write mechanism the OS uses for `fork()` -- the child process gets private copies of the parent's memory pages, and actual copying only happens when either side writes.

## Anonymous mappings for large allocations

You can create a mapping without a file backing it -- that's an **anonymous mapping**. It gives you zero-filled memory directly from the OS, bypassing the allocator entirely:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{size / 1024 / 1024});
}
```

Why would you use this instead of a regular allocator? A few reasons:

1. **Guaranteed page-aligned.** Allocators may or may not give you page-aligned memory. mmap always does.
2. **Guaranteed zero-filled.** The OS zeros anonymous pages for security (so you can't read another process's data). With `page_allocator` you get this too, but general-purpose allocators may return uninitialized memory.
3. **Large allocations.** If you need hundreds of megabytes or gigabytes, mmap is what `page_allocator` uses under the hood anyway. Going direct cuts out the middleman.
4. **Memory protection.** After filling your buffer, you can call `mprotect` to mark it read-only, catching accidental writes at the hardware level.

Having said that, for most allocations you should stick with Zig's allocator interface ([episode 7](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-7-memory-management-and-allocators)). Anonymous mmap is for special cases where you need OS-level control over the memory's properties.

## Unmapping and the importance of `defer`

Every `mmap` must be paired with `munmap`. If you forget to unmap, the mapping persists until the process exits. That's a resource leak -- the virtual address space is consumed, and the kernel keeps the file's page cache entries pinned.

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{result});
}
```

The pattern is always the same: map, `defer` unmap, do your work. Same as `file.close()`, same as allocator `.free()`. Zig's `defer` makes resource management deterministic and hard to get wrong. In C you'd need to remember to call `munmap` on every exit path -- every error check, every early return. Forget one and you've got a leak that only shows up in long-running processes. With `defer` it's one line, right after the mmap call, and you never think about it again.

One subtlety: `munmap` can't fail in practice (the POSIX spec says it can return `EINVAL` for bad arguments, but if your arguments came from a succesful `mmap` call, `munmap` won't fail). That's why Zig's `posix.munmap` returns `void`, not an error union. Safe to call in `defer` without worrying about error handling.

## Practical example: fast byte frequency counter

Let's put it all together with a practical tool. We'll build a byte frequency counter that mmaps a file and counts the occurrence of every byte value (0-255). This is useful for file analysis, detecting binary vs text files, finding encoding issues, or just being curious about a file's contents:

```zig
const std = @import(\

,
    });
}
```

Run this on a source code file and you'll see that space (0x20) and newline (0x0A) dominate, followed by common ASCII letters. Run it on a compiled binary and you'll see a much more uniform distribution with null bytes (0x00) near the top. Run it on a compressed file and the distribution is nearly flat across all 256 values -- that's actually one way to detect encryption or compression: high entropy means evenly distributed byte values.

The mmap approach here is clean: open file, map it, pass the slice to `countFrequencies`, print results. No buffered reader, no chunk management, no file position tracking. For a file that fits in RAM (which is practically everything on a modern system with 16+ GB), this is the simplest and fastest way to scan the contents.

## Wat we geleerd hebben

- **Memory-mapped files** let the OS map file contents directly into your address space. Reading the file becomes reading memory -- no explicit `read()` calls, no buffer management.
- **`std.posix.mmap`** takes an address hint, length, protection flags, mapping type, file descriptor, and offset. Returns a page-aligned `[]u8` slice.
- **Demand paging** means only pages you actually access get loaded from disk. Map a huge file, touch one page, and only 4 KB gets read.
- **`PROT.READ | PROT.WRITE`** enables write access. With `.SHARED` mappings, writes go back to disk. With `.PRIVATE` mappings, writes trigger copy-on-write and only affect your process.
- **Anonymous mappings** (`ANONYMOUS = true`, fd = -1) give you zero-filled OS pages without a file. Good for large aligned allocations with guaranteed zeroing.
- **Always `defer posix.munmap`** right after a successful mmap. Same resource management discipline as allocators and file handles.
- **mmap shines for sequential scans** of large files, read-only access patterns, and sharing data between processes. It's less ideal for small random writes (every modification dirties a full page) or files that change size frequently.

The patterns we covered today -- mapping files for reading, modifying through writable mappings, using anonymous mappings for large allocations -- these are foundational for systems programming. Database engines, text editors, log processors, and virtual memory allocators all use mmap extensively. When your data is already a file and you need to process it in memory, reaching for mmap instead of buffered I/O is often simpler AND faster. How those mapped memory regions interact with Zig's comptime type introspection system opens up some very interesting possibilities for building type-safe file format parsers ;-)

## Exercises

1. Write a program that memory-maps two files and compares them byte-by-byte, printing the offset and differing bytes for the first 10 differences found (or \

if they match). Handle the case where the files have different sizes. Think about what happens at the boundary -- if file A is 1000 bytes and file B is 2000 bytes, you should compare the first 1000 bytes and then report \

2. Build a simple file patcher using mmap: the program takes a filename, a hex offset, and a hex byte value, then writes that byte at the specified offset in the file using a writable shared mapping. Verify the write by re-reading the file with a separate mapping (or regular `read`) and printing the byte before and after. Make sure to validate that the offset is within the file's bounds.

3. Create a program that uses an anonymous mapping to allocate a large buffer (say 64 MB), fills it with a pattern, then uses `std.posix.mprotect` to mark the region read-only. Attempt a write after the protection change and observe what happens (the program should crash with a segfault -- catch this by wrapping the write attempt in a comment that explains the expected behavior, and print a message BEFORE the write attempt so the user knows what's about to happen). This demonstrates hardware-enforced memory protection.

Thanks for reading!

body.title: Be Still: Finding Direction in Quiet Moments
body.body:
Taking a time out or engaging in quiet time is a very good thing and an avenue for us to shut out the busy and noisy world, so we can use that moment to have an uninterrupted reflection about our lives and help us think about ways to better our lives. Many of us find it difficult to take quiet time because our world is a busy one filled with loads of activities that could get us engaged and distracted from having deep thoughts to reflect on our lives, and that's why it's important that at least once in a while we find ways to engage in it. Am I engaging in quiet time? If yes, when last did I do that? Find out my response to those questions and several others relating to the subject matter below. ![1000357471.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickoly/242hcof3oetUWBDsHMYow2s28RT7QTkUCMP3e3EHWk8Qjz8izfpnXMqvaVQNq9sKYGEwV.jpg) To be honest, prior to this year I hardly engaged in quiet time on a regular basis; it just comes with the flow of time and situations of things. However, since the beginning of this year there has been a positive turnaround in that aspect, because now a week hardly goes by without me finding time to just distance myself from the drama of my society and just take out time to reflect on my life. Talk sense to myself, evaluate my life, point out what I'm doing right and wrong, and also reflect on possible solutions and things I can engage in to better my life situation, family, and all that concerns me. Since I've started indulging myself in constant quiet time, I've come to become more intentional about my life, the actions I take, and more. It has helped me take proactive steps and calculated risks, which keeps me safe from the dangers that follow rash and hasty actions and decisions. Although there is still room for improvement, I must say that seeing the changes I've experienced in the past few months, I can't help but somewhat regret how I didn't start indulging in quiet time long before now. But then that's in the past and behind me; the best way forward is to make sure I do it more frequently and make sure it's worth the time by producing results that make my today and future better than my yesterday. Talking about when last I took a time out to listen to my own thoughts and reflect without distractions of this world, it's quite close because this past Friday was the last time I engaged in such quiet time that gave me an opportunity to critically think about my life, scrutinize different possibilities that might follow action I'm proposing if taken, and several other things. Also, it was during that reflection that I got to further understand the importance of good health, especially when it comes to every part of our body and how a simple injury to one part can put the entire body in chaos. This helps me appreciate good health more, especially given the injury I sustained last week. ![1000583640.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickoly/242NghtaQPXUFUL7zW6u4TRXqUVLjmkhm2dUeK15JiPgWHYbyoxim7drkaafBRnuWwk2Z.jpg) Talking about its benefits to my life and the changes it has brought, like I stated above, it's been a blessing to me to the point where I wish I had indulged in it all my life. But then it's all good, because I'm now aware of its benefits and would certainly indulge in it more often so that I can take proactive calculated steps and reflect on my life, both past, present, and future actions. *** All photos are mine. ***

body.title: How to run Folding at Home on powerful Virtual Machine in 5 minutes via Vast.ai?
body.body:
This is tutorial step-by-step how to buy computing power and run Folding at Home to help cancer/Alzheimer etc. research easily and effectively. The instruction works for Linux and macOS, I assume noone running Windows would be determined enough to perform it anyway.

Open the terminal and type:_**ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/Documents/ASI/key\_name**_ 

(You can use different directory, but is elegant to have separate catalog specifially for one task). You will be asked to choose the passphrase for the key, choose wisely as there will be no \

option. There will be two keys created: the private one and the public one. Create the catalogue before You create ssh key in it :).


Register on vast.ai and add funds. Feel free to use my reflink:

Vast.ai: https://cloud.vast.ai/?ref\_id=513344

I have used also ASI:Cloud, which works nicely but is more expensive in general. ASI Cloud: https://asicloud.cudos.org/?referrer=xfclRp0489inOH8t7CiJJ
Go to Console (or type cloud.vast.ai in the browser bar). ![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSgFiBqadECmJavydhiE8mAtLpQiEBqmStwXihhRkPVMu/Wklejony%20obraz%20(2).png)

Click Select Template and choose NVIDIA CUDA (for AMD and Intel GPUs there might be different one, but currently there are none on vast so I cannot check).

Browse through available machines and select the one You want. If you focus on energy efficiency, I recommend choosing RTX PRO Blackwell or RTX Ada GPUs. The amount of memory and its bandwidth is not crucial in Folding at Home. H200 or B200 GPUs will be also very effective, but they will be much more expensive and the difference is not worth the price for that goal (for the same money, You will get better results by running PRO Blackwell or Ada cards for longer, than H100/H200/B200 for shorter). Avoid using gaming machines, if You decide however, I think it is better to choose a few weaker ones than like one RTX 4090 or 5090. If You care about environment, You can also focus on choosing the location with high usage of nuclear or renewable energy, like France, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, California.

When You decide, click Rent. So far I have been using cheaper \
machines but was never interrupted so far:). And even so, the Folding at Home saves the results often, so I recommend choosing these machines.\n\nNow go to \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWtzFET2dkNW7MqgYqwyFM8SsdWPirXvXumUZQmMzKWFg/image.png)

Click Key button

Add PUBLIC SSH key and confirm

![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmahGrop6bJ1EbEq93k1aa5BGJUXrLiH3MNf9ja5DQoW6Q/image.png)


In Terminal on Your PC, write chmod +600 PATH\_TO\_YOUR\_PRIVATE\_KEY

Then type:

![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSkz4iLrcTGi1xqLiHbKZNXfdAgrDRLLK41ygEWq67tKN/image.png)

(the command written here does not work directly, as it does not contain path to the private key)

Then type the passphrase.

You are connected :)

![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTbHUX7LYmc4q6ahS1oXJZGwTZAfmhaZHsZpto2ab9jut/image.png)

Then type consecutively:

_**wget https://download.foldingathome.org/releases/public/fah-client/debian-10-64bit/release/fah-client\_8.5.5-64bit-release.tar.bz2**_

_**apt install bzip2 -y**_

_**tar -xjvf fah-client\_8.5.5-64bit-release.tar.bz2**_

_**cd fah-client\_8.5.5-64bit-release**_

_**nohup ./fah-client --account-token=Your\_token > fah.log 2>&1 &**_

Note: in the future when Folding at Home will get newer version, replace 8.5.5 with the newer one, You can always go here: https://foldingathome.org/start-folding/

and copy path to the proper link:

![ \

one.

The _**nohup**_ command makes the FAH run in the background even when the ssh connections ends.

Replace the token with Your Folding at Home account token. You can find it here:

![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPkAQpQtjPy1weMu1Z2AWRL55FwpG4m7VTwa1Sz5yhdWU/image.png)

I recommend leaving at least as many CPU cores free as You have GPUs, their work is marginal comparing to GPUs anyway and if enabling all cores will slow GPUs for at least 1%, it is not worth, and if they have a lot of cores, like 64 in that case, difference between 62 and 64 is marginal also.

Save the changes and click Start Folding button.

Congratulations, You have just created Your first Virtual Machine running Folding at ~~Home~~ Server.

You can also connect to the machine in the second terminal window, and type _**nvtop**_ or _**nvidia-smi dmon**_ command, and You will see specifically how GPUs work.
For CPU, type _**htop**_.

If GPUs don't run on full power, try different provider next time, maybe he has set some limits. 

Last but not least: create Your own instruction in the .txt file, os You can start action faster than checking each time on my blog.

If You have some questions, feel free to ask. 

RTX PRO 6000 are beasts.

body.title: Hausmeister findet Goldbarren / caretaker finds gold bars
body.body:
Beim Mähen an einem Wasserreservoir im sächsischen Bannewitz machte ein Gemeinde-Mitarbeiter im Oktober einen spektakulären Fund: Acht kleine Goldbarren kamen unter dem frisch gemähten Gras zum Vorschein. Wie der MDR berichtete, tauchten kurz darauf noch zwei weitere auf. Insgesamt wiegt das Gold rund 280 Gramm und wird auf etwa 40.000 Euro geschätzt.


![52991.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZWJzhX6HgZTBdvfoXMeQGF9wT5V33ZF4d7CTU7NET3Hp/52991.png)


Ermittler prüfen zwei letzte Hinweise, bevor das Gold an die Gemeinde geht
Nach deutschem Recht hat ein unbekannter Eigentümer sechs Monate Zeit, seinen Anspruch zu belegen, wie der MDR schreibt. In der Gemeinde, die südwestlich von Dresden liegt, meldeten sich zwar mehrere Personen, doch niemand konnte seinen Anspruch auf das Gold überzeugend nachweisen. Damit darf die Gemeinde den Fund nun offiziell behalten.

**Zu viel Bürokratie: Bürgermeister will Goldbarren lokalen Vereinen aushändigen**

Ganz ungelegen kommt das dem parteilosen Bürgermeister Heiko Wersig und seiner Gemeinde nicht – es soll nun den lokalen Vereinen zugutekommen. Am 28. April will der Gemeinderat entscheiden, welche Vereine vom Fund profitieren. „Es wäre schön, wenn dann das Gold in einem Zug an diese geht“, sagte Wersig zu „Tag24“.

Zehn der 52 örtlichen Vereine sollen je einen Goldbarren erhalten, den sie selbst verkaufen können. Aus Sicherheitsgründen möchte Wersig die Barren nicht im Rathaus lagern, ein Verkauf durch die Gemeinde wäre zu bürokratisch. Vor Bekanntgabe erklärte der Bürgermeister bereits die Richtung der Vereine, die profitieren sollen: 

*„Alle, die mit Kinder- und Jugendarbeit zu tun haben. Und die, die sonst nichts bekommen.“**

Ich zitierte aus folgendem Artikel...

https://www.focus.de/panorama/gaertner-findet-gold-beim-maehen-deutsche-gemeinde-darf-40-000-euro-behalten_4e0c478c-7bab-47bc-8841-2845150be9c4.html

Mein persönliches Fazit:

Solch einen Fund habe ich leider noch nicht gemacht. Ich bin mir allerdings sicher um positive Karmapunkte zu sammeln hätte ich diesen Fund auch gemeldet. 😉

Wie hättest du denn gehandelt?

---

English 

While mowing grass near a reservoir in Bannewitz, Saxony, a municipal employee made a spectacular discovery in October: eight small gold bars were unearthed beneath the freshly cut grass. As reported by MDR, two more appeared shortly afterward. The gold weighs a total of approximately 280 grams and is estimated to be worth around €40,000.

Investigators are examining two final leads before the gold is handed over to the municipality.

According to German law, an unknown owner has six months to prove their claim, as MDR reports. Although several people in the municipality, located southwest of Dresden, came forward, no one could convincingly prove their claim to the gold. Therefore, the municipality is now officially allowed to keep the find.

**Too much bureaucracy: Mayor wants to hand over gold bars to local clubs**

This comes at a convenient time for the independent mayor, Heiko Wersig, and his municipality – the gold is intended to benefit local clubs. The municipal council will decide on April 28 which clubs will profit from the find.  “It would be wonderful if the gold went to them all at once,” Wersig told Tag24.

Ten of the 52 local clubs are to receive a gold bar each, which they can then sell themselves. For security reasons, Wersig doesn't want to store the bars in the town hall; selling them through the municipality would be too bureaucratic. Before the announcement, the mayor explained which clubs would benefit:

*“All those involved in children's and youth work. And those that otherwise receive nothing.”**

I quoted from the following article...

https://www.focus.de/panorama/gaertner-findet-gold-beim-maehen-deutsche-gemeinde-darf-40-000-euro-behalten_4e0c478c-7bab-47bc-8841-2845150be9c4.html

My personal conclusion:

Unfortunately, I haven't made such a find myself.  I'm sure I would have reported this find to gain some positive karma points. 😉

How would you have handled it?
