### 1/🧵   The Noise I Had to Outrun to Find Myself



A lot of people will not say it out loud, but deep down, they are afraid of silence. And I am not talking about the usual late-night silence or when the environment is silent. But the deeper kind of silent. The silence when someone purposely decides to lock in and hear their own thoughts out loud, like when you can hear the sound of a ticking clock. At some point, I ran away from this too. All my free moments used to be filled with one distraction or another. From music to scrolling to watching movies to chatting, or anything that can just distract me. But when I looked at the past, my take was that I was running. Not from anything external in particular. But from what is sitting inside of me quietly.

body.title: Beneath the Quiet Tree
body.body:
/>Two months ago, I found myself sat at the foot of a tree, away from any noise, distraction and rush of life. At my feet lay a large warm stone, upon which I remained for over two hours; there was no phone, there were no conversations. Simply the whisper of the wind rustling through leaves, and the gentle trills of birds in the trees above me.

I was surrounded by palm trees standing tall and serene; seemingly without a care in the world.  
I wasn’t there just to find some calm, though. On the day I found myself beneath that tree my life seemed to be falling apart. I felt like everything around me had fallen into an incomprehensible and messy chaos and I was just treading water to stay afloat.

Problems seemed to keep arising, and I constantly felt like I was battling against something – I didn’t know what, and I didn't know why; because just recently life seemed to make sense, it wasn’t a lot but it felt stable; I never worried so much and I didn't feel like I was dragging an invisible weight behind me, that comfort however, somewhere along the line, turned into something that felt almost unbearable.  
Sitting at the base of that tree, however, I was forced to confront my own inner demons. I had no distraction so there was no escape; it was initially discomforting, replaying mistakes over and over and beating myself up over what I wished I could have done differently.

It seemed part of the chaotic nature I was experiencing stemmed from a tendency to run away from these thoughts. I was too busy sorting out the life I was living that I wasn't taking any time out to check if I was okay inside and just like magic that tranquil moment turned into a catalyst for change.

Instead of blaming the entire world for my problems, I started looking inward, at the specific things that had put me in the position I was in; I thought about the decisions that had been made and the choices that I had been faced with, and I started asking myself questions like, \

.

Those weren't easy questions to answer and I certainly never found them easy, but for the first time in a long while I didn't have to. The more I questioned myself, the calmer I felt, the actual state of my surroundings hadn’t changed – I knew I was still facing the same set of problems- but my attitude towards them did.

I realized that happiness doesn’t necessarily entail having a 'perfect' life and sometimes is simply about a clear understanding of oneself regardless of the circumstances that one is surrounded by.

That day was not an instant fix, but it was a stepping stone, giving me perspective to understand that change doesn’t necessarily have to involve grand gestures; it can simply involve a willingness to take that first step, and that I still had control over where my path would lead.

Even though I haven't returned to that exact spot I remember that a moments pause can actually be more productive than continuing to blindly rush through life.

I certainly plan on carrying that with me as there was something so peaceful about those silent moments and the clear understanding it brought me and that is something I think every person needs to try to find within themselves every now and then, just for some added clarity and peace; and from there, who knows?

body.title: Thinning the Mongol Patrol.
body.body:
> > The contest themes of @gamingphoto helps us seeing things in a video game that we normally ignore. After a failed standoff against an armored guard, I fought a brutal melee to secure the final Shashimono banner from a watchtower. I eliminated an archer and engaged the ground patrol, but the noise drew the war camp general and another heavy guard into a difficult confrontation.
[Gaming Photography Weekly Contest.](https://peakd.com/hive-185676/@gamingphoto/gaming-photography-weekly-contest)
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWpTVJHispLTcnrFZSawiXxznAZ94b5gniPL2N9hHbLAP/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc6yhfC9ZkCU1wWs4wxPPmjZUyRcvUeCRaBnZQ46vQqBK/screenshot_2_.png) I still had to recover one last Shashimono banner and eliminate the war camp general to fully liberate the area. I found a heavy guard with massive armor standing watch close to where the general was positioned. I decided to challenge him to a standoff to end it quickly, but I failed my timing as he moved with unexpected speed. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYpa1QA5sNbi9Nvw31RriAVPYqwdg5VW38WRLDwwdEn67/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmea9tvEiwscmbnrf93dnQPfrksrKSVee6M8Tr9jbhaS35/screenshot_4_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPbsr2MN15V7zpDFjeXmvDF4MrBY4QCnBsJaFuRzDZVmV/screenshot_5_.png) That guard was really fast for his size and somehow dodged my standoff attack before I could land the strike. I had to take care of him next in a brutal melee fight, where I used my heavy stance to break through his defenses. After fighting for a moment and dodging his massive swings, I finally took him down. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmayqvXkbRNoMU6JG8V2UQnvHoeJBJomxZ84h5Kt33FXH3/screenshot_6_.png) I found the last Shashimono banner on a tall tower near the center of the camp. While I was climbing up to claim it, I noticed there were several Mongol guards below patrolling the area in tight circles. They were unaware of my presence for the moment, allowing me to plan my next move from a position of height. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPLWN7qRe46kLd6MNLYqzUk1Wtjp1JFkk7MGn1BFGeurw/screenshot_7_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTMUnHQgjbrrR6GGc6FpvV38ZnbKiCikokLvEnun6QGtV/screenshot_8_.png) An archer from a nearby tower somehow noticed me while I was reaching for the banner. He started shooting me with arrows while I was in cover, forcing me to pull out my own bow to retaliate. I took him down later, and surprisingly, when the guards on the ground below didn't have any idea about this arrow war. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbnY4T1WnxerfU7b3um9oFQaqDnrioA4nsyfQRZkbwgnT/screenshot_9_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRNRnkS4hKWrZ2o5T5dH3RAaaZEvvemG6fvqff5d4j8h2/screenshot_10_.png) After shooting down one of the guards below with arrows to thin the group, I jumped down to finish the rest. I tried to assassinate the next target, but I failed to get the drop on him and had to engage in a messy melee attack. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma8VWZ4rS1KXP5rk2pyoKmnwrqXS2r31htTn2AZPHUQcT/screenshot_11_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQQ9pe3NPs21W9CcBJRLaXFRy1znZYLb5VR9u2HWrmNKA/screenshot_12_.png) There came two more Mongol guards to look around as they found the dead body of their comrade I had just left behind. I stayed hidden above them. Once the opportunity felt right, I tried an aerial assassination on one of them, dropping like a stone to end him. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbigkzbRmXCxkJZGwmsCJFztSFpAfa7R3bzAvuayhZGt3/screenshot_13_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQz95ZJvV2XgYwK8RfjAYsNPyUDhviimbU7EiTVkMVJe5/screenshot_14_.png) I noticed the war camp general was running towards me as he heard the noise and the screams around his post. I was still in the process of taking down that Mongol guard when the general appeared around the corner. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTsGgkQsH5qWKPqcPJ5Bm4BixfdzMMzGsj3RJWnHsCeZE/screenshot_15_.png) Right when the war camp general reached me to begin our duel, there came another heavy guard with thick armor from the opposite side. This reinforcement made the situation even harder for me to take care of as I was now trapped between two powerful enemies. I had to think fast to survive this sudden and deadly escalation. --- If you like the post, feel free to like, comment & share. I will soon come with another post. --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=naeemulnepun/8d40fbf5)

## 1) Seit 2016 im Zeitalter der Zerrüttung

### 1.1 Wie sogar EXCEL den Zeitgeist spiegelt

#- KLAR?

#- EXCEL IDEALERWEISE EIN MODELL FÜR SYSTEMISCHE ORDNUNG

**WARUM WAR EXCEL FRÜHER** (Excel 97–2010) benutzerbezogen PROBLEMLOS?
- relative Pfade wurden immer bevorzugt
- absolute Pfade wurden automatisch aktualisiert
- Ordner umorganisieren war problemlos

**Heute** (Excel 2016–365): ***Schwer nachvollziehbar bis die vom Benutzer gewollte programmierte Ordnung vom System eigendynamisch zerrüttet wird:*** 
- OneDrive‑Integration
- Auto-Recover
- Sync‑Metadaten
- Cloud‑Pfade
- interne Caches
→ **Excel aktualisiert absolute Pfade nicht mehr zuverlässig erstrebenswert**!
- <u>Das ist ein **Designfehler mit Systemeigendynamik wider den Bediener**</u>

![Copilot_20260424_101746.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/option2-e/23vi2AUiJpiKxzwEQAVWKqtq9TUcqoKXRUakG9fzGoA5X4LmFB98uPckSrAEbCkALbn3H.png)

> **Abb. 1** Das Bild macht den technischen Strukturfehler von Excel sichtbar:
>- **Links:** der alte, absolute Pfad „C:\Old\Missing\File.xlsx“ – bröckelnd, rot markiert, mit Warnsymbolen und Fehlermeldung „LINK ERROR!“.
>- **Rechts:** der korrekte relative Pfad „A‑APS\03‑APS\03a_APS‑iso.xlsm“ – klar, grün leuchtend, verbunden mit geordneten Ordnern und einem stabilen Excel‑Symbol.
Zwischen beiden Seiten verläuft ein Lichtbogen, der den Übergang von Chaos zu Ordnung markiert.
>- **Die Darstellung zeigt**, wie Excel an alten Pfaden festhält und dadurch Stress erzeugt – und wie die bewusste Korrektur zur Wiederherstellung der Ordnung führt.
Das Bild ist eine technische Konkretisierung des existenziellen Prinzips aus Abb. 1.

### 1.1 Technisches Verhalten mit großer Wirkung

Excel speichert bei Datei‑Verknüpfungen zwei Pfade:
- einen relativen (korrekt)
- einen absoluten (veraltet)

Wenn Dateien neu organisiert werden, aktualisiert Excel den absoluten Pfad nicht.  
Das führt dazu, dass Excel an einem Ort sucht, der nicht mehr existiert.

Die Folge:
- Fehlermeldungen
- Stress
- Datenverlust
- unnötige Reparaturarbeit
- Vertrauensverlust in die Struktur

Dieses Verhalten ist dokumentiert, aber nicht korrigiert.

### 1.2 Warum das existenziell relevant ist

Dieses Muster ist nicht nur technisch.  
Es ist strukturell:

**Ein System hält an alten Pfaden fest, obwohl die Realität längst weiter ist.**

Das erzeugt:
- Reibung
- Blockaden
- Eskalationen
- unnötige Komplexität

Excel zeigt im Kleinen, was in großen Systemen geschieht:
Wenn die Struktur nicht aktualisiert wird, entsteht destruktiver Stress.

### 1.3 Die Chance für Microsoft

Microsoft hat die Möglichkeit, hier ein Zeichen zu setzen:

- durch klare Pfad‑Aktualisierung  
- durch Priorisierung relativer Verknüpfungen  
- durch automatische Korrektur veralteter absoluter Pfade  
- durch Transparenz im Verknüpfungsdialog  
- durch eine Option „Verknüpfungen auf relative Struktur zurücksetzen“  

Das wäre nicht nur eine technische Verbesserung.  
Es wäre ein Beitrag zur **systemischen Klarheit**.

### 1.4 Warum das wichtig ist

Millionen Menschen arbeiten täglich mit Excel.  
Wenn ein System alte Pfade konserviert, erzeugt es Stress, der vermeidbar wäre.

Eine Korrektur würde:
- Stabilität erhöhen  
- Fehlermeldungen reduzieren  
- Vertrauen stärken  
- Komplexität senken  
- die Ordnung wiederherstellen

body.title: The Noise I Had to Outrun to Find Myself
body.body:
A lot of people will not say it out loud, but deep down, they are afraid of silence. And I am not talking about the usual late-night silence or when the environment is silent. But the deeper kind of silent. The silence when someone purposely decides to lock in and hear their own thoughts out loud, like when you can hear the sound of a ticking clock. At some point, I ran away from this too. All my free moments used to be filled with one distraction or another. From music to scrolling to watching movies to chatting, or anything that can just distract me. But when I looked at the past, my take was that I was running. Not from anything external in particular. But from what is sitting inside of me quietly. ![217328.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenproject/23yTwwe5oRpAgh1Wto8ATyzom33g9CpRoJLZju7bM42UHHuY778trjpu3Kcah3mcEyPHH.png) After watching similar podcasts back to back. The funny thing was that my YouTube kept bringing related videos to me, and then I decided to try it one day. I sat alone, but I was not really feeling anything. I was physically present, but I had another distraction, and this time it was an inward one because my mind was just wandering all over the place. From thinking of what I will do next to another thing. Though I set an alarm before I started and after my time elapsed, I reached out again to my phone. This happened a few years ago anyway. But now, things have changed because my continuous practice is giving me results. Now I do it just as my spirit directs me, especially when I need to take a deep self-reflection on myself about some unresolved things in me. The major thing I will say led to this was because I got tired at some point. Not tired of life actually, but just doing a lot of things with an unsettled mind. That can be so frustrating. But I needed to understand life better than just reacting casually to what is going on around me. Tired of doing things in a circle or in someone else's shadow. The morning quiet became the one place where I could finally find out what was real for me. ![217333.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenproject/217333.png) There used to be some days when nothing profound happened in my morning. I just wake up, sit, continue my day, and move on with my life. While some days, the first thing that will come to my mind even before I pray is this thing I have ignored for days, and it's just there, in front of me, until I deal with it carefully. And to me, assuming I was rushing, I wouldn't have seen that type of clarity. Because it usually comes when I stay long enough to stop pretending that everything is okay. A lot of pressure, man, future questions, how to make better decisions, money pressure too, a lot of contemplation if I am doing the right thing, especially in the right way. All these things will never go away during a quiet time, they just become more visible. And to be honest, they helped my decision making because I noticed that mornings when I have a very deep and quiet time, I don't usually panic in making my decisions, unlike other mornings. Some other habits like that in me have already earned their place slowly and quietly. But this quiet time has earned it completely. ----- ##### 🔗 Apps which I recommend built by sagarkothari88 | | | | |---|---|---| | 各位小伙伴们好！友哥今天又来分享一集，探店美食。今天这个店，开在燕山大学附近，价格亲民，味道很好，所以很火爆！欢迎继续阅读了解！

友哥打卡秦皇岛博物馆，中午饭得想法解决一下呢。友哥从网上搜索了一下，就找到了评分较高的烤鱼店。在大学附近的，能持续开多年，那么味道一定差不了，不会踩坑。

body.title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians (2023) [ENG/ESP]
body.body:
>Since I really enjoyed both Percy Jackson movies and everything related to the Greek gods, I obviously didn't want to miss the series that Disney+ released. It follows the same story as the books, although, as always, it changes significant details or includes some forced additions. But since I haven't read the books, only summaries and reviews, I decided to give it a chance and see what this series version had to offer. So, here are my impressions. ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_074910_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/23uQfxXheuqyG1GbFZyqiH5fLLmZQ8VAAhMEiwzfBSVwqfgMU4WkceGdLpAw1UebtQHYg.png) [Source](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm1663258113/?ref_=ttmi_mi_157_1) ---
> # Percy Jackson and the Olympians …. ---

>Premiered in 2023, it is an American fantasy television series created by Rick Riordan and Jonathan E., based on the books of the same name by Riordan. It is an adventure, comedy-drama, and fantasy series, starring Walker Scobell, Leah Sava Jeffries, Aryan Simhadri, among others, and currently has 2 seasons, with 8 episodes each. ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_074938_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/EoGxSUP2Wsdf7ZNbQEyXV4NuWpCBBA8p594US6pbX1pUSoduwGHm1wybNPa6WDRL4QD.png) [Source](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm1425923330/?ref_=ttmi_mi_63_2) ---

>If you've already seen the movies, well, in retrospect, it's almost the same, but with different ages, more characters, and quite significant details in the ending, which, of course, aren't shown or aren't faithfully covered in the two-hour version. Even so, here's what this series brings us: The story follows the life of a 12-year-old boy, Percy Jackson, who, after a series of inexplicable events and learning difficulties (such as ADHD and dyslexia), actually reveals himself to be a demigod, the son of a human and a Greek god. He is taken to Camp Half-Blood, a refuge for young people with divine lineage, where he learns that he is the son of none other than Poseidon, one of the \

>His arrival coincides with a crisis on Olympus: Zeus's Master Bolt has been stolen, and Percy is the prime suspect due to an old rivalry between his father and the king of the gods. To clear his name, prevent a new war between the gods, and rescue his mother from the clutches of the Underworld, Percy, along with Annabeth, a clever girl and daughter of Athena, and Grover, his loyal satyr protector, embarks on an epic journey across the United States. Will he manage to save his mother and prevent chaos in the world? Who is really behind the theft of the bolt? ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_075036_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/241tT6bGbEp6Xrk1WYJzEdTTNPfSZBAiwr9in9miyeNovHkJ4hme8MfUqf6LB7QAFeXqL.png) [Source](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm740391681/?ref_=ttmi_mi_111_2) ---

>First and foremost, the main characters bothered me. I was used to the others, and I understand that both Percy and Annabeth do have their differences compared to the books, especially the girl, since she's supposed to be described as blonde with blue eyes, as well as Alexandra Daddario, who dyed her hair in the second season, making her look more like her character. The problem was their ages, since they were older than the original story indicated. Anyway, that's forgivable because the script has tonal coherence. It tells us that, from the beginning, it's a \

and doesn't try to force an artificial maturity, so the pacing is appropriate. It takes its time to explore the lore and the psychology of the characters; however, in several episodes, the characters explain the danger before we see it, which sometimes breaks the tension and ends up being discouraging. ---

>Now, regarding the acting, since I haven't read the books, I don't know if they portray the characters well, but without a doubt, these kids know how to convey what they're going through, and it comes naturally to them. For example, the actor playing Percy manages to convey the feeling of a child who feels \

by his dyslexia and ADHD, but who has a huge heart. Similarly, the actress playing Annabeth clearly shows her pride and strategic nature; these are details that are appreciated. Finally, as for the entire set design, I loved it. They were very meticulous in immersing us in that classic style mixed with modern elements; you can tell they're building their world. ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_075249_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/242DDrZ3rTEYrdCntGRHLjZDtaxis8ERbW71Ne2AQUFjL4TuqcdDKGGZfoHtG35ff94sR.png) [Source](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm4150372098/?ref_=ttmi_mi_103_1) ---

>

- Based on the reviews I've read, the story stays true to the original format, successfully balancing youthful humor with profound themes like parental abandonment, the search for identity, and a critique of power hierarchies.
- The acting is good, effectively capturing the essence of their characters.
- Production Design and CGI: The integration of mythology into the modern world is excellent. Camp Half-Blood and the creatures (like the Minotaur and the Chimera) boast high-quality artistic design that moves beyond generic fantasy clichés.
- Villain Development: Here, we see greater depth in the villains. They aren't simply evil for the sake of it; no, they are humanized. They are figures with complex motivations that invite the viewer to question who the \

> - Excessive dialogue and a tendency to anticipate events before they actually happen. - Pacing and Episode Length: Some episodes feel short (around 30-35 minutes of actual runtime), causing certain important scenes to feel rushed, while other conversations drag on unnecessarily. ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_075343_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/23tvVvw2Eh9UiB34LRewMCVm2GUtJTeUjEPTkBNNTMQ6BfkY4D26Dwkpwp2qBMP4raiY3.png) [Source](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm3869298690/?ref_=ttmi_mi_41_2) ---
>8/10 Story │ 8.5/10 Acting │ 8.5/10 Sound │ 9.5/10 Stage Design │ 8.5/10 Overall ---

>The series is a triumph of characterization, but it suffers from narrative pacing issues. It's a solid production that prioritizes building a coherent, long-term universe over empty spectacle. Personally, if you enjoy Greek culture as much as I do, it's interesting, and well, we won't be left wondering what happened next, in reference to the films. ---

> # Percy Jackson and the Olympians …. ---

>Estrenado para el año 2023, es una serie de televisión estadounidense de fantasía creada por Rick Riordan y Jonathan E, basados en los libros homónimos del mismo Riordan y es de genero aventuras, comedia dramática y fantasía, protagonizada por Walker Scobell, Leah Sava Jeffries, Aryan Simhadri, entre otros y, hasta el momento tiene 2 temporadas, de 8 episodios cada una. ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_074938_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/EoGxSUP2Wsdf7ZNbQEyXV4NuWpCBBA8p594US6pbX1pUSoduwGHm1wybNPa6WDRL4QD.png) [Fuente](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm1425923330/?ref_=ttmi_mi_63_2) ---

>Si ya vieron las películas, pues en retrospectiva, es casi lo mismo, pero en otras edades y con más personajes y detalles bastantes significativos en el desenlace, que, por supuesto, en la versión de dos horas no se muestran o no logran abarcar fielmente, aun así, aquí les dejo lo que nos trae esta serie: La historia sigue la vida de un joven de 12 años, Percy Jackson, quien, tras una serie de eventos inexplicables y dificultades de aprendizajes (como el TDAH y la dislexia) son en realidad señales de que es un semidiós, hijo de una humana y del dios griego. Es llevado a un campamento mestizo un refugio para jóvenes con linaje divino, enterándose que es hijo de nada más de Poseidón, uno de los “Tres grandes dioses”. ---

>Su llegada coincide con una crisis en el Olimpo: el Rayo Maestro de Zeus ha sido robado, y Percy es el principal sospechoso debido a una antigua rivalidad entre su padre y el rey de los dioses. Para limpiar su nombre, evitar una nueva guerra entre dioses y rescatar a su madre de las garras del inframundo, junto Annabeth, una inteligente chica, hija de Atenea, y Grover, su leal protector sátiro, Percy se embarca en una travesía épica a través de los Estados Unidos ¿Logrará salvar a su madre y el caos en el mundo? ¿Quién estará realmente detrás del robo del rayo? ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_075036_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/241tT6bGbEp6Xrk1WYJzEdTTNPfSZBAiwr9in9miyeNovHkJ4hme8MfUqf6LB7QAFeXqL.png) [Fuente](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm740391681/?ref_=ttmi_mi_111_2) ---

>Primero y principal, pues me choco los personajes principales, tenia la costumbre de los otros y, tengo entendido que, tanto Percy como Annabeth si tienen sus diferencias en contrastes a los libros, sobre todo la chica, ya que se supone que la describen catira con ojos azules, así como Alexandra Daddario, que en la segunda entrega se pintó el cabello, asemejándose más, el inconveniente era la edad de los mismos, ya que estaban más grandes de lo que la historia original indicaba. En fin, se deja pasar eso, debido a que, aquí el guion tiene coherencia tonal, nos indica que, al principio es una \

y no intenta forzar una madurez artificial, por lo que el ritmo es adecuado, se toma su tiempo para explorar el lore y la psicología de los personajes; no obstante, en varios episodios, los personajes explican el peligro antes de que lo veamos, lo que a veces rompe la tensión, por lo que termina desanimándote. ---

>Ahora de las actuaciones, como no he leído los libros, no sé si personifican bien, pero sin duda, estos chicos saben transmitir los que les pasa y les sale natural, por ejemplo, el que hace de Percy, logra transmitir esa sensación de un niño que se siente \

por su dislexia y TDAH, pero que tiene un corazón enorme o como la que interpreta a Annabeth, se denota la soberbia y lo estratega que es; son detalles que se aprecian. Ahora bien, para ir finalizando, pues en cuando a toda la escenografía, a mi me encanto, fueron bastantes minuciosos en adentrarnos a ese estilo clásico mezclado con la modernidad, se nota que están construyendo su mundo. ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_075249_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/242DDrZ3rTEYrdCntGRHLjZDtaxis8ERbW71Ne2AQUFjL4TuqcdDKGGZfoHtG35ff94sR.png) [Fuente](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm4150372098/?ref_=ttmi_mi_103_1) ---

>

- Con los comentarios que he leído, la historia se mantiene fiel al formato original, logrando equilibrar el humor juvenil con temas profundos como el abandono parental, la búsqueda de identidad y la crítica a las jerarquías de poder.
- Las actuaciones están bien, logrando capturar a sus personajes en cuestión.
- Diseño de Producción y CGI: La integración de la mitología en el mundo moderno es excelente. El Campamento Mestizo y las criaturas (como el Minotauro o la Quimera) tienen un diseño artístico de alta calidad que se aleja de los clichés genéricos de la fantasía.
- Desarrollo de los villanos: Aquí notamos más profundidad en los mismos, no son malos porque si, porque te lo pinto así y listo, no, aquí los humaniza, son figuras con motivaciones complejas que invitan al espectador a cuestionar quiénes son realmente los \

> - Exceso de diálogos y antepone los sucesos ante de que ocurran. - Ritmo y Duración de los Episodios: Algunos episodios se sienten cortos (alrededor de 30-35 minutos efectivos), lo que provoca que ciertas escenas importantes se sientan apresuradas, mientras que otras conversaciones se alargan innecesariamente. ---
![Opera Instantánea_2026-04-27_075343_www.imdb.com.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yaslenysofia/23tvVvw2Eh9UiB34LRewMCVm2GUtJTeUjEPTkBNNTMQ6BfkY4D26Dwkpwp2qBMP4raiY3.png) [Fuente](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt12324366/mediaviewer/rm3869298690/?ref_=ttmi_mi_41_2) ---
>8/10 Historia │ 8.5/10 Actuaciones │ 8.5/10 Sonido │ 9.5/10 Escenario │ 8.5/10 General ---

>La serie es un triunfo de caracterización, pero tiene problemas de ritmo narrativo. Es un producto sólido que prioriza la construcción de un universo coherente a largo plazo por encima de la espectacularidad vacía. En lo personal, pues si te gusta los temas de la cultura griega como a mí, resulta interesante y que, bueno, no nos quedaremos con las ganas de que paso después, en referencia a las películas. ---

body.title: [ESP/ENG] Oklahoma City Thunder en modo campeón de la NBA. Opinión
body.body:
Una introducción necesaria 

Oklahoma City ha mostrado una superioridad contundente en estos Playoffs 2026, impulsada por el dominio de Shai Gilgeous-Alexander y la profundidad de su plantilla. Con tres juegos desarrollados los actuales campeones de la Asociación Nacional de Baloncesto de los Estados Unidos (NBA) por sus siglas en inglés ha demostrado que viene con la clara intención de revalidar su título algo que no ocurre desde hace varios años.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme5BSGqMmDbk4Y4j4X7vYULA97Cz7LgZzaTGkgABJa4YK/1777290953322.jpg)[fuente](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048161261863436660?t=5QZ1JRdF0y-MI7pazw2prQ&s=19)




Oklahoma City Thunder en modo imbatible

La actuación del Thunder ha sido, hasta ahora, una demostración de autoridad propia de un equipo que terminó la temporada regular con el mejor récord del Oeste y que defiende su título de la temporada anterior. Oklahoma City lidera su serie 3-0 ante Phoenix, mostrando un baloncesto maduro, agresivo y sostenido. 

 
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaEVZVZvZRm3FqnaisPKe4C9NSxeB4P7yXXt7jArMcoKy/1777291115538.jpg)[fuente](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048407377704087869?t=eiw9A84uf52EJQBWhigrqg&s=19)


Elementos positivos

- Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (SGA) en modo MVP, con actuaciones de más de 30 puntos por partido y un tope de 42 puntos en el juego 3 que han marcado la diferencia con sus rivales. Su dominio en el terreno de juego y su capacidad para forzar faltas han sido imparables.   
- Chet Holmgren como ancla defensiva, aportando rebotes, intimidación y eficiencia ofensiva. Su presencia ha sido clave para controlar la pintura y buscar la estabilidad entre ataque y defensa.  
- Profundidad del banquillo, que ha sostenido ventajas y aportado energía constante. El equipo luce fresco, disciplinado y con roles bien definidos, algo que para un deporte de equipo tan dinámico es esencialmente imprescindible para alcanzar objetivos dorados.
- Control del ritmo, imponiendo su estilo desde el primer cuarto y obligando a Phoenix a jugar desde atrás en todos los partidos.   


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRYcVrSnzTXGXJKXuqis6PAHBTTYuBk8MdK2HJTmQHpao/1777292085531.jpg)[fuente](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048199769034498088?t=MSEm7ySWrXEyr6JuGk64GQ&s=19)

 Limitaciones del equipo

- Dependencia alta de SGA: aunque el equipo es profundo, el peso ofensivo recae demasiado en su estrella. Una mala noche o una defensa muy física podría.  
- Lesión de Jalen Williams, quien salió con molestias en el tendón de la corva. Su ausencia prolongada afectaría la versatilidad ofensiva y defensiva del equipo.   
- Tendencia a relajarse con grandes ventajas, algo que Phoenix aprovechó parcialmente en el tercer cuarto del Juego 2 y que puede pasarle factura ante equipos de mayor calidad.

Otros elementos de interés

- Oklahoma City está jugando con la confianza de un campeón y con la madurez de un equipo que sabe cerrar partidos.  
- Su defensa perimetral ha sido una de las mejores del torneo, limitando a Booker y obligando a Phoenix a depender de tiros forzados.  


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbSFJFAci2sL4UYdD8vvdpcGq2MnHtiquiXdtFJn7Xy2z/1777291685278.jpg)[fuente](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048401712071803216?t=_vlthITW4oIur3qb_SG_GA&s=19)



Un comentario final

Para este autor, será muy difícil que este equipo no esté en la discusión del anillo de la NBA. Es cierto que en la división hay equipos como los Lakers, Denver o Minessota, pero la manera en la que este equipo ha jugado durante toda la temporada ha sido sencillamente espectacular.

Veremos quién puede frenar el baile de SGA y su equipo.


¿Qué piensa usted?

Nota: He utilizado el traductor DeepL Translate.




ENGLISH 



[ESP/ENG] NB Champion Dominance



A Necessary Introduction 

Oklahoma City has shown a resounding superiority in these 2026 Playoffs, driven by the dominance of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the depth of its roster. With three games played, the reigning champions of the United States National Basketball Association (NBA) have shown that they come with the clear intention of revalidating their title, something that has not happened for several years. 


! [](https://images.ecency.com/DQme5BSGqMmDbk4Y4j4X7vYULA97Cz7LgZzaTGkgABJa4YK/1777290953322.jpg)[source](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048161261863436660?t=5QZ1JRdF0y-MI7pazw2prQ&s=19)




Oklahoma City Thunder in unbeatable mode

The Thunder's performance has been, so far, a demonstration of authority from a team that finished the regular season with the best record in the West and is defending its title from the previous season. Oklahoma City leads its series 3-0 against Phoenix, showing mature, aggressive and sustained basketball.  

 
! [](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaEVZVZvZRm3FqnaisPKe4C9NSxeB4P7yXXt7jArMcoKy/1777291115538.jpg)[source](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048407377704087869?t=eiw9A84uf52EJQBWhigrqg&s=19)


Positive elements

- Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (SGA) in MVP mode, with performances of more than 30 points per game and a game 3 cap of 42 points that have made the difference with their opponents. His dominance on the court and his ability to force fouls have been unstoppable.    
- Chet Holmgren as a defensive anchor, providing rebounds, intimidation and offensive efficiency. His presence has been key to controlling the paint and looking for stability between offense and defense.   
- Depth of the bench, which has sustained advantages and provided constant energy. The team looks fresh, disciplined and with well-defined roles, something that for such a dynamic team sport is essentially essential to achieve golden objectives. 
- Control of the rhythm, imposing his style from the first quarter and forcing Phoenix to play from the back in all games.    


! [](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRYcVrSnzTXGXJKXuqis6PAHBTTYuBk8MdK2HJTmQHpao/1777292085531.jpg)[source](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048199769034498088?t=MSEm7ySWrXEyr6JuGk64GQ&s=19)

 Equipment limitations

- High dependence on SGA: although the team is deep, the offensive weight falls too much on their star. A bad night or a very physical defense could.   
- Jalen Williams is injured, who left with hamstring discomfort. His prolonged absence would affect the team's offensive and defensive versatility.    
- Tendency to relax with big leads, something Phoenix partially took advantage of in the third quarter of Game 2 and can take its toll against higher-quality teams. 

Other items of interest

- Oklahoma City is playing with the confidence of a champion and with the maturity of a team that knows how to close games.   
- Their perimeter defense has been one of the best in the tournament, limiting Booker and forcing Phoenix to rely on force shots.   


! [](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbSFJFAci2sL4UYdD8vvdpcGq2MnHtiquiXdtFJn7Xy2z/1777291685278.jpg)[source](https://twitter.com/okcthunder/status/2048401712071803216?t=_vlthITW4oIur3qb_SG_GA&s=19)



A final comment

For this author, it will be very difficult for this team not to be in the discussion of the NBA ring. It is true that in the division there are teams like the Lakers, Denver or Minnesota, but the way in which this team has played throughout the season has been simply spectacular. 

We will see who can stop the dance of SGA and his team. 


What do you think?

body.title: Meeting people while hiking [ENG/ESP]
body.body:
<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQpVesjtDJx2CNYyPeaF3dzXwG4D9AfNXf9hXMBKUBbfH/1777290936370.heic)</center>

Hey everyone! I hope you're all doing great. This week we went hiking up a pretty steep mountain; we covered about 6 or 7 km and spent around 2 hours walking.

>Hola hivers! Espero se encuentren genial, esta semana tocó ir a una montaña bastante inclinada, recorrimos aproximadamente unos 6 o 7km y duramos como unas 2 horas caminando.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWVPDjLT6FUzvWb6zXU32akjo4PXPv7gpQXZGjCjrv78i/1777290937107.heic)</center>

Even though it was quite tall, there wasn't really a viewpoint from which you could see the city; instead, there were lots of trees all around and quite a few flower beds.

>A pesar de que era bastante alto no había un mirador como tal en el que pudieras observar la ciudad, lo que habían eran muchos árboles rodeando todo y bastante platas de siembra.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdfmHi8t6Pq7rKKHLuEaxrzz2pvz7WKBRgQkBAqWDtGW6/1777290937730.heic)</center>

We stopped by a few of the farms in the area; people saw us and waved, offering us things like fruits and vegetables from their crops. Generally speaking, people who work on farms tend to be friendly—I know this because you could say I grew up on one (long story)

>Enteamos a algunas de las fincas de por ahí, la gente nos veía y saludaba, nos ofrecían cosas como frutas y verduras de sus cosechas, en general la gente que trabaja en fincas suele ser amable, lo sé porque se podría decir que crecí en una (larga historia)

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbT37ncrWtAo117jt3EiyMy7k4xG6keAN12a3BeTYoqCc/1777290938407.heic)</center>

All in all, it was a really nice and unique trip; we’d never seen so many people while hiking before.

>En fin, un viaje bastante agradable y diferente, jamás habíamos visto a tantas personas mientras hacíamos senderismo.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZYR3BTrTsKnvt3siGHdrLunpUjGkz2N8iySUDc772eEn/1777290939096.heic)</center>

body.title: 我的三餐组合局…😉
body.body:
![MTXX\_20260421\_160518639.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/annepink/AKGbfRzbnxktRwDMAxreryzmdfhv7buckWGLYdLjnuxiFdp6hV6rinZg8dF3UfF.jpg)

![MTXX\_20260421\_160713122.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/annepink/AKCHyCBJDCo4Wk8ES1tHPZNA5nMgcQ9ZxZ89o5noqkCmmuaXnWYjjmuNy6Uv6mY.jpg)

不知从何时起… 看着父母渐渐老去，身体大不如前不由得心生忧虑…😔 再加上近来身边总能听闻各种各样的健康问题… 我心里也不由得绷紧了弦！开始格外在意起自己的身体状况了！

毕竟很多时候，身体表面看似无恙，并不代表内里就毫无问题！人到了一定年纪，终究要学会为自己的健康负责，生怕哪天身体垮了，无人照料，想想都觉得心酸啊！
 
也正是这份顾虑，让自己醒悟了… 从前的我比较敷衍度日的生活！现在该是注重一点自己的养生日常咯！比如一日三餐不能太随意了，得把自己的日子过得尽心一点尽力一点…
 
回想起从前，早餐对我来说总是可有可无的！要么干脆不吃，要么拖到很晚才随便对付一下！就算偶尔吃，也只是一个鸡蛋，一杯热水，再搭配一两个馒头，牛奶几乎都没吃过只买给儿子吃！就这样简单将就得糊弄一下…

以前孩子还小，满心满眼都是照顾他，还会跟着孩子一起好好吃点！可一旦孩子不在家的时候，自己就彻底懈怠，怎么省事怎么来了🤦🏻‍♀️
 
如今不一样了，即便只有我一个人，我也坚持好好吃早餐了！这不，清晨的第一餐吃得营养又精致有木有呵呵～我现在的早餐标配… 一杯鲜奶，搭配一碗暴走工坊的燕窝银耳燕麦片，里面我还放了好几颗原味核桃仁！以前从没吃过这些啊！😅 

这款麦片是偶然在刷短剧的广告里看到的，价格一般，口感也还行！作为我这种懒人营养早餐再合适不过了！偶尔我还会配份水果… 以前不搞这些讲究的！😅 今次一盘脐橙，给简单的早餐增添一丝果香味嘿嘿～水果不是天天那么勤快有，这次我用心地对待自己，早已胜过从前的随意将就哈～
 
还把这份丰盛的早餐随手拍给熊孩纸了！就是对他小小炫耀一下，让他夸夸我哈哈哈哈🤣🤣🤣 要知道从前的我，从不会如此认真对待早餐，如今慢慢做出改变，不再一味凑活，连自己都觉得变勤快了不是嘛！

从前的早餐，我常年是单一的面条或是米粉吃的最多！现在时常换换心情花式早餐安排下！这样会给自己提供不少情绪价值嘿嘿～

![MTXX\_20260206\_225024108.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/annepink/AKcgLkf4ct1CvzvXhMCNTAbZgJ85X944TX7ctJnTQd2yFao96YYwUip3VaYVhH1.jpg)

![MTXX\_20260206\_225000223.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/annepink/AKRCUMr3zRXQ4E8SSfm1fEPfZef2WrMKJsAnsqicyEtRmhdr1ZpgH53GFJZD6EE.jpg)

另外，这一份午餐看着简单但很好吃哦！这是一碗自制拌面🍜 简单用盐、麻油、生抽、老抽调味… 撒上一小把美妈种的小香葱！再来一勺灵魂老干妈，看似普通的一碗拌面，味道绝杀啊！😋😋😋😋😋😋 重点是面条的口感筋道十足，好吃到停不下来！！！！弱弱说一下这款面条，是在拼夕夕入手的，不是啥大品牌，却胜在真材实料，价格实惠哈！我每次吃都觉得格外满足感！关键煮起来一点不糊不坨！真心好！本来收货后我还看不上呢！没想到吃起来太惊喜啦！还安利给我熊孩纸尝鲜了！他更是爱吃的不得了啊哈哈哈哈～😎
 
![IMG20260105222457.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/annepink/EoK6HtWWtKsZi1JUeUsxZBMwJjHL3iwG5PwV2K7gsqqG1gcHSPj8JzthcY53re64Kjq.jpg)

![MTXX\_20260126\_202615478.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/annepink/AKCGwT2LkBj6uz4d64Z8WmK1xm3LkTMZKFVP4rkqejuzT5LcsrSbBGCdpFGHuur.jpg)

这是我某一天晚上的晚餐！一碗热气腾腾的糙米粥！简简单单煮上一人份量，丢了几颗红枣一起煮！软糯香甜… 暖胃又养生哈！最爱这样简单方便的食材就能尝得到的美味… 朴素却格外治愈！
 
我的三餐还是简单，却是对自己来说不一样的用心了！很享受这样的独处时光… 一个人吃饭，一个人感受岁月静好，这种慢悠悠的惬意感是独属于自己的美好！一年四季朝朝暮暮… 都能轻松拥有的自在！
 
然而，也会感叹年华早已悄然流逝，不胜唏嘘… 但更多的是感恩岁月的温柔，庆幸自己依旧平安健康！不知不觉中时光虽在身上留下痕迹… 却也让我懂得用心感受三餐四季，生活点滴的温柔与美好！

如今孩子已然长大，有了自己的诸多主见！即便身为父母，心中依旧免不了操心！但终究要学会慢慢放手，不必再事事过度操劳！往后余生，照顾好我自己才是最要紧的事！守护自身健康，才能游刃有余地陪伴好父母…❤️❤️❤️

body.title: War Between the Sexes: Abundance Year Episode 1949 (audio noxsoma.substack.com)
body.body:
Full Metal Ox Day 1884
Monday 27, April 2026
Abundance Year Episode 1949
Noxsoma Life Camp:  
War Between the Sexes

![1949.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTgduTQCY5ML5qKfWe2i3EAc45RAqMsGfd4YNNTPvhUQj/1949.png)

Efficiency
All is Maya 
Dharma Collection Long Play, now available on all channels.                      
 
Today's Episode:   https://odysee.com/@Noxsoma:2/1884_full_4-27-26_1949_sexwars:4?r=47k2ScJsm9Uex9eETqgCCA8q1fukdST9  
Channels: go to noxsoma.substack.com and subscribe. 

We have a piece in today’s Ox Drop about the growing and ugly divide between males & females. We are intentionally reducing these critters to a diminutive and vague reference because the behavior in question does not reflect that of what our Atman would recognize as “men” & “women”, let alone ladies and gentle (meaning “well-born”) men. It was commonly said in the before times, that “the cream rises to the top.” But, notes the cynic, “so does the scum.” 

In the waning days of white-supremacy-powered American hegemony, it’s not surprising that the “War between the Sexes” has escalated to a level that spotlights the word, “misandry.” This word, apologetically coined in 1881, is the welding of the Greek, “miso” meaning hate, and “andros” meaning “male human” (as opposed to women, or gods.) This time, our word does not come from the hallowed halls of psychology, but from one, Frances Power Cobbe, an Irish feminist  nigh-instantly  flipping misogyny to “misandry” to make a point. 

The word and the concept was incubated within the Womens Rights movement and wielded by both sides of the battle lines. 

(1970s-90s). Second-wave feminism & backlash.  As feminism critiqued patriarchy and male privilege, critics began to claim that some feminist rhetoric expressed hatred of all men, not just patriarchal structures. They adopted misandry as a counter-accusation to misogyny. 

(1990s-2000s). Men's rights movement. This movement made misandry a central term in its lexicon, arguing that society systematically discriminates against men (e.g., in family courts, domestic violence shelters, education). They positioned misandry as the overlooked mirror image of misogyny. 

(2000s-present).  Internet and social media  Online forums, Reddit, Twitter, and YouTube amplified the term enormously. It became a staple of \
discourse, often used to label feminist statements, dating norms, or media portrayals (e.g., \

sitcom tropes) as hateful toward men.    

Conversely, the word, “misogyny” goes back to antiquity. A deep dive into history suggests that men have always hated women. In general that is. It literally goes back to Genesis. Imagine Adam and Eve, as “1984” characters Winston and Julia. Winston gets busted, with apple in hand, still chewing, and immediately flips on Eve. 

“Twernt me Lord, spect-it was Eve.” 

It’s been downhill for women ever since. There’s not a history book ever read by your humble observer where there wasn’t some horrible fate leveled against women of any era, on either side of the common era, simply for being women. Unfaithful? Death. Barren? Death. Not pretty anymore? Death. Born female? Death. It’s a wonder there are any females left on the planet. That they exist is a testament to their resilience. 

What was that line? “Can’t live with’em, can’t live without’em.” 

But back to the scum rising to the top. The scum of maleness seems to have risen to the very top of the social media popularity pyramid. But it hasn’t stopped there. The Epstein apocalypse has confirmed what many have suspected, (and some have enjoyed, downstream) for decades.  Yours truly has been blissfully ignorant of the current wave of this phenomenon for many years. It’s only when the likes of blowhards like Voldemort, and his virulent ilk rise to the level of my awareness do I have a clue that this attitude and behavior is, or seems to be, perpetuating throughout the simulation.   
It’s never not been this way through time. (Although it has not been this way for your boy. The past was active, varied, daring and experimental at times, but deny decadence, and sexploitation.) The stories of matriarchal societies, are Utopian fantasies. But that’s a debate for another time. 

Have you ever heard of the “Witches Hammer?” Aka the “Malleus Maleficarum.” It’s this crazy treatise on the prosecution of witches, published in the German (that anti-human region) city of Speyer, in 1486. It was written by the German Catholic clergyman Heinrich Kramer. It’s been characterized the compendium of preexisting demonological literature of the 15th century. 

Here’s one of my favorite, but crude, recollections from the book.  In my own rendition. 

Heinz is coming home from wherever he was. Gertrude returning from the grocer’s with dinner. Heinz has a natural thought about Gertrude, gets a hard-on, and because he’s a 15th Century Catholic German, he doesn’t know what to do. So he runs to the church and tells the vicar. Of course the clergyman immediately diagnosis the problem. “Witchcraft!” Heinz mentions seeing Gertrude. “She’s a witch!” Gertrude is burned at the stake. Or drowned, or, what they call, “Pressed.” This is where the “melleus” kicks in, it means “to crush.”     

Anyway, all these words later, back to the word that started this whole trip, “misandry.” It seems to have flipped from a defensive term, to an offensive one. It’s not like     
It’s not like men don’t have this vitriol coming. After an entirety of institutionally, academically, theologically, politically, sexually and violently hating women, men should forever sleep with one eye open. But for real. “We” (still a man, afterall), won’t have to. The final irony, and maybe it’s a tragedy, and maybe it’s just nature – is nature her self. (If it’s not demons.) Females, of all species, (confidently speculating), have those annoying chemicals that make reproduction, an instinct, rather than a choice. Even if they manage to overcome the urge to reproduce that nature is still there. (I got stories.) 

The War Between the Sexes isn’t new, it’s perpetual. What changes is the technology and the artificial “laws” that are supposed to, but always fail to protect women from the nature of the beast.

body.title: Film Review: Thor: Ragnarok (2017)
body.body:
![(source: tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/xxtTTSMtApYD0ZY2n4SkgcFprfb.jpg)

The Marvel Cinematic Universe can boast with the reputation of the most commercially successful series in film history, but it's still hard to shake the impression that it's built on shaky foundations. Or, to put it more precisely, many of its parts function only as part of a larger whole, while on their own they fall far short of the quality expected of Hollywood's biggest golden goose. Perhaps the best example of this might be Thor, who could be described as the most popular and likeable of all Marvel's Avengers, but whose first two standalone films in the series have relatively quickly faded from the memory of audiences who aren't among the most passionate fans of Marvel comics or Chris Hemsworth. The third film, titled Thor: Ragnarok, was entrusted to Taika Waititi, a New Zealand director who had won over critics and cinephiles with the wacky low-budget vampire comedy *What We Do in the Shadows*.

In Norse mythology, Ragnarok signifies the destruction of the world, or at least of Thor's homeland Asgard. Such a catastrophe is supposed to be brought about by the fire demon Surtur, whom Thor manages to defeat, but it turns out that Asgard is still in danger. The reason for this is the death of Thor's father, the god Odin (Anthony Hopkins), after which there is no one left to keep a check on his millennia-imprisoned sister Hela (Cate Blanchett), the goddess of death. Against her, even Thor with his hammer Mjolnir stands no chance, and she arrives in Asgard, seizes power and gains the ability to threaten all Nine Realms, including Earth. In an attempt to oppose her, Thor ends up on the planet Sakaar, where he is captured and sold to the Grandmaster (Jeff Goldblum), the local ruler who entertains his people with spectacular gladiatorial games. Thor could become one of the stars of the arena, provided he survives a clash with the Grandmaster's top star, who turns out to be none other than the Hulk. Thor must not only win, but also try to awaken in the Hulk his true character as Dr Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo), so that together with Valkyrie (Tessa Thompson) they can try to save Asgard.

The screenwriters of Ragnarok still adhere to the formula used in most Marvel films, so the main hero still has to confront a demonic supervillain threatening to destroy one or more universes, naturally accompanied by a heap of apocalyptic destruction aided by CGI. On the other hand, although they have kept this basic framework, they have allowed themselves a little more creative freedom, both in playing with the comic book source material – so characters and locations that one would expect to survive until the end credits disappear – and in the film's structure itself. Ragnarok thus seems like two films: a routine 'Marvel-esque' and 'serious' epic about saving the universe, into which, somewhere in the middle, a far wackier space adventure is inserted that more closely resembles *[Flash Gordon](https://peakd.com/aaa/@drax/retro-film-review-flash-gordon-1980)* or *[The Fifth Element](https://hive.blog/film/@drax/retro-film-review-the-fifth-element-1997)*. Fortunately, this 'wacky' part takes up most of the film, and some of that wackiness lingers on towards the end, where in the obligatory climactic showdown there is room for some unexpected humour.

This time the screenwriters have also been quite generous towards Thor, giving his character some exceptionally good one-liners, and Hemsworth even manages to overshadow Tom Hiddleston in the role of Thor's mischievous brother Loki, who is fun in Ragnarok but ultimately not that important to the film. The choice of Jeff Goldblum as the Grandmaster also proved excellent; his character – a bumbling yet charismatic villain – manages to quite overshadow Cate Blanchett and her role as the evil goddess. The music by Mark Mothersbaugh, former keyboardist of the band Devo, also makes a rather good impression; his techno sounds provide a refreshing touch and help the 'offbeat' atmosphere considerably. On the other hand, some characters are underused, most notably the Asgardian warrior Skurge, from whom the unrecognisable Karl Urban only manages to get something out of at the end. The same can be said for Idris Elba, who turns in a routine performance as Heimdall. Ragnarok is essentially a good and mostly entertaining film, but the mini-cliffhanger ending, which tells us that the real challenges for Thor and the rest of the Avengers lie in the future, clearly points to the main drawback of films that don't mean much without the wider context of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

RATING: 6/10 (++)

*(Note: The text in the original Croatian version is available [here](https://draxblog.com/2020/05/24/recenzija-thor-ragnarok-2017/).)*

body.title: Título: Cuando el Diablo se pasea por Moscú y un escritor arde en preguntas
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRWQvgSBkJWhJjEXBYHKYd5nfhWfxvUm7hMj1ygREUFos/1777290941486.jpg)

Imaginen que un miércoles cualquiera, en un parque de Moscú, el mismísimo Satán se sienta a tu lado y te suelta: «Somos viejos conocidos». Eso es, más o menos, lo que le ocurre a Berlioz, editor ateo y confiado, antes de que un tranvía le quite la cabeza con una pulcritud macabra. Así arranca El maestro y Margarita, un libro que parece un chiste mal contado, pero termina siendo una de las novelas más profundas (y chifladas) del siglo XX.

Mijaíl Bulgakov escribió esta joya a escondidas, sabiendo que jamás la vería publicada. Y eso se nota: cada página es un acto de rebeldía. Pero lo que hace única a esta obra es ese duende imposible que logra —mezclar a Poncio Pilatos con un gato negro gigante que dispara una máuser y cobra en el metro. Sí, leyeron bien.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNsSry3z14Ez6Hn7t2rZSMckiPJoXMmPskRprjtmpa2Lq/1777290909066.jpg)

Lo que más me fascina es cómo Bulgakov juega con los planos. Por un lado, tenemos la Moscú de los años treinta, llena de burócratas, poetas mediocres y vecinos chismosos, que recibe a Woland (el diablo) y su séquito. Pero por otro, viajamos a la Jerusalén antigua, donde un procurador atormentado dialoga con un filósofo pobre llamado Yeshua. Y entonces cae el otro: ambos mundos se comunican. La traición, el miedo, el perdón y el poder no cambian tanto en dos mil años.

El personaje de Margarita es otro volcán. Cuando aparece, el libro se viste de noche y magia negra. Ella no es la típica amante sufrida: vuela desnuda sobre Moscú, se convierte en bruja, destroza la casa de un crítico literario miserable y se juega el infierno por rescatar a su amado —el desquiciado Maestro, ese escritor quemado por dentro que terminó en un manicomio tras escribir su novela sobre Pilatos.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR2xPHYGhJMdhBrabN8KhL6mg25gGUdAvyJuqUBsjsztU/1777290909297.jpg)

Y aquí va mi confesión: al principio, El maestro y Margarita me desconcertó. No sabía si reírme con los trucos del gato Behemot o estremecerme con la soledad de Pilatos. Pero luego entendí que de eso va la cosa. De aprender a mirar de reojo, de aceptar que lo real y lo fantástico se toman el mismo vodka. Bulgakov nos dice que la verdad no está en los informes ni en las normas, sino en la lealtad, en la palabra dicha al filo de la noche y, sobre todo, en la misericordia.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPYdirjktEMbD5jMb7xXRLM7zuEsUHrxosqQeURqoXoSc/1777290909728.jpg)
Si aún no se han asomado a esta locura, háganlo con calma. Y si ya la leyeron, cuéntenme: ¿Con quién se quedan, con el gato pícaro o con el procurador que llora en la roca?

Nos leemos en los comentarios.



Title: When the Devil Walks into Moscow and a Writer Burns with Questions

Imagine it's a random Wednesday in a Moscow park. You're minding your own business when Satan himself sits next to you and says, \

That's roughly what happens to Berlioz, a smug, atheist editor, moments before a tram neatly removes his head. And just like that, The Master and Margarita kicks off—a novel that feels like a bad joke at first but ends up being one of the deepest (and maddest) books of the 20th century.

Mikhail Bulgakov wrote this masterpiece in secret, knowing it would never see the light of day in his lifetime. You can feel it on every page: this is an act of rebellion. But what makes the novel truly unique is its impossible charm—it somehow mixes Pontius Pilate with a giant black cat who fires a pistol and rides the metro on its hind legs. Yes, you read that right.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdgoYEauAeMrGYihBaMjcV3bUX8rJkMdYwDVgqS8s9NjK/1777290909519.jpg)

What fascinates me most is how Bulgakov juggles dimensions. On one hand, we have 1930s Moscow, packed with petty bureaucrats, mediocre poets, and nosy neighbors, all getting a visit from Woland (the devil) and his absurdly terrifying crew. On the other, we travel to ancient Jerusalem, where a tormented procurator debates with a ragged philosopher named Yeshua. Then the punch lands: both worlds speak to each other. Betrayal, fear, power, forgiveness—they haven't changed much in two thousand years.

And then there's Margarita. When she enters the scene, the book puts on a black dress and flies. She's no passive lover: she rides naked over Moscow, turns into a witch, trashes the apartment of a miserable literary critic, and strikes a deal with hell itself to rescue her beloved—the tormented Master, a writer burned by his own brilliance, locked away in an asylum after finishing his novel about Pilate.

Here's my honest confession: the first time I read The Master and Margarita, I didn't know whether to laugh at Behemoth the cat's tricks or cry at Pilate's loneliness. But eventually, I got it. That's the whole point. Learning to look sideways. Accepting that reality and fantasy share the same cheap vodka. Bulgakov whispers to us: truth isn't in reports or regulations. It's in loyalty. In words spoken at the edge of night. And above all, in mercy.

If you haven't stepped into this beautiful chaos yet, do it slowly. And if you have—tell me: are you team Behemoth, or team the weeping procurator on his stone?

Drop your thoughts below.

body.title: 3LOOK Explained: What It Is And How It Works?
body.body:
When the old InfoFi big names closed the shop or had to revamp, new projects and protocols tried to fill the gap. [3Look](https://3look.io/?ref=pvmihalache&src=invfr) was one of the new kids on the block that tried to make a move! 

[3Look](https://3look.io/?ref=pvmihalache&src=invfr) it may look like a fashion-focused social platform where people share outfits, discover style content, and sometimes take part in brand campaigns or drops but is not! 

They are mixing the feel of social media with a kind of gamified focus on social media! Instead of just scrolling you’re engaging  to earn recognition and rewards from campaigns.

The creator score matters on [3Look](https://3look.io/?ref=pvmihalache&src=invfr) and the activity on social media helped users to get their tiers. I got a Bronze Tier with my creator score, and now looking to grow!


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX9jufscU3YgwNQSm5DWA1fBjCRvJyc73BcstBcPjn3CJ/image.png)


The way it works is pretty straightforward. You post “looks”  and interact with other [3Look](https://3look.io/?ref=pvmihalache&src=invfr) users’ content, or in some cases join the challenges to share a slice of the campaign's pool.

As you stay active, the platform tracks your participation and uses that to unlock different kinds of status or rewards. The [3Look](https://3look.io/?ref=pvmihalache&src=invfr) Loop campaign was about spreading the word! 

They also had a fast-paced campaign that shared daily a part of the $USDC prize pool, but I wasn't selected for that. Instead of early users they went for KOLs and big names! 

That was a move that left me with a sour taste and a bit disappointed, considering I was an OG member. However, the game goes on and it's cool to see my 606th rank is improving. 


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPondfi3BcmUEnLyNqL2hJC52wXDKCSagNgsF7DjJyzVk/image.png)


Yes anon... I was an OG on [3Look](https://3look.io/?ref=pvmihalache&src=invfr)! I have badges to prove it! The OG badges and Early badges are really about timing. You got it if you joined extremely early, between the platform’s launch or very first user wave.

It’s a status marker that shows I there at the beginning. Early badges are similar but not as cool as the OG one! This was given to people who joined shortly after the OG claim was closed.

Both are basically ways of recognizing early adopters, and they come with a bit of prestige and hopefully sometimes access perks depending on how the platform will set up.

[3Look](https://3look.io/?ref=pvmihalache&src=invfr) said in some messages and communications that badge holders will have early access to campaigns, or maybe multipliers. Let's see if this gets implemented soon! 


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVsAFcuv3WCvQjaD1MAbBTLCPdjftjSJ84wEvkhx8DEX7/image.png)

body.title: Sitting With My Thoughts.
body.body: > ## Hello, everyone. I welcome you to my blog and another wonderful edition of the Hive Learner's featured post. Lately one thing that has become very difficult to do is to take time to reflect or have the time to observe some quiet time where you can comfortably collect your thoughts, compare them and also reflect to see if you are making actual progress or it is the other way around. The world has become so noisy to the point where silence is a treasure hard to come by; the saying 'silence is golden' was not taken seriously until now; it is very difficult to actually come by these days. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcm3gHRBT97zngEZS9CoHFBvouvLADcDKnFJ6G6eHDVVm/1777290930438.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/grayscale-photography-of-man-sitting-down-on-metal-bench-ZW03J8-zpKY) Observing some quiet time for yourself has become nearly impossible to do because we are all so busy; you leave the house in the morning and come back late in the evening, and at that point what you need is rest, not quiet time, because at that time your thoughts are already chaotic due to the day's stress, and you cannot even think straight. How busy we are and how noisy the world that we live in is have made observing a quiet time difficult and reflecting a thing that we do once in a while. A lot of things are also competing for our attention: our phones, social media, and entertainment platforms. Sometimes when we get a break from life's struggles, instead of collecting our thoughts and reflecting, we opt to spend time on social media, and after that, getting back to life's struggles, we spend time chatting on social media, scrolling through social media, and moving from one social media application to another with zero reflection in mind. The truth is reflecting and spending some quiet time with yourself is no doubt one of the best times to realise and discover where you are lagging. Before I graduated college, I will say it's been a year or more than a year since I last sat down with my thoughts, reflected and tried to align back with goals and aspirations. Now I have graduated, and the life I imagined I would live after graduation is completely different from the life I am currently living. It was at this point that I realised how noisy the world was, as there is nowhere to stay and actually think and try to pinpoint where you went wrong and what to do next to help you get back on track. Currently working in a school, lately I do a lot of reflecting. Whenever school dismisses, I go to one of the empty classes, which is my only way of observing some quiet time because back home I have my uncles' kids making noise like there are a dozen of them, whereas there are just 4 of them. Then, during school hours, there are students everywhere and fellow teachers gossiping and gisting, and the only time I have to observe a quiet time is after school when the students have gone home and just a few teachers are left. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRnUowuBafoXbx29wU5cmceaZjEEJSjdngmWhegZhFRCJ/1777290930387.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/man-sitting-on-bench-M_ajTtNalSA) This quiet time and my recent reflections have helped me calm down. I realised I was putting so much pressure on myself and comparing myself a lot with people who did not start from the same starting point but want to be at the same level as them. I realised I was comparing myself with people getting way more support than they talk about and way more than I am getting, and all of that has helped me ease the pressure I was actually putting myself under. Quiet times are when you pinpoint errors and mistakes made and then try to correct them. Lately I observe quiet times more than I can actually count, and that is the only thing that has helped me stay sane.
