links.title: Finding Peace in Silence | My Quiet Time Reflection
links.body:
Hello everyone, happy new week. We are gradually getting to the end of April, and my exams are also coming up this weekend, so everything feels a little busy right now.


![IMG-20260427-WA0000.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mathewdaddywah/23wCV3D7hew3abZ54jHyztfB5GTPTamTNkKSvNQDNxN3d2n7hJ5URPXYEvKjaKyn67yc5.jpg)

Images Generated with Meta AI

Still, I’ll be participating in this prompt on A Quiet Time because it is something I can really relate to.
I do love the energy behind those words because it explains who I am. I love nothing more than a quiet place, a time of peace and relaxation where I can let my thoughts flow through my head. 

There is something special about silence. It gives you room to think, room to breathe, and room to understand yourself better. So yes, if I am to be honest, I think this prompt is worth writing on.

When was the last time I really got a chance to sit down and reflect about life? Honestly, it has been a long time. As much as I love to reflect on things, the chances hardly come.

Every day, bills keep piling up, responsibilities keep showing up, and survival becomes the main focus. Sometimes life moves so fast that you forget to pause and ask yourself if you are truly okay can you leave another day

There are days when I get back from a work am always tired, both physically and mentally, and all I want is silence. No noise, no stress, no people asking questions just a little quiet. 

That moment, even if it is just for thirty minutes at night, helps me a lot. I sit alone, sometimes outside, sometimes just lying on my bed, and I think about everything my life, my family, my dreams, my mistakes, and where I am heading.

Most times, reflection makes me realize how far I have come. There were moments in my life when things were really hard, when I felt stuck and wondered if things would ever get better. 

From working under difficult conditions to trying to save enough money to stand on my own, life has taught me patience and endurance. 

Looking back now, I can say those quiet moments helped me stay strong because they reminded me that giving up was never an option.

Meditation for me is not always sitting in one position and closing my eyes like people describe it. Sometimes it is simply walking alone, listening to music softly, or even staying awake late at night when everywhere is calm. That is when my mind speaks the loudest.

I reflect on my decisions and I ask myself if I am becoming the person I want to be.
This habit has helped my life because it keeps me balanced. 

It stops me from acting out of anger or frustration. It helps me understand my emotions better and reminds me that every problem has a solution if I stay calm enough to think clearly. Quiet time also brings gratitude because in silence, I remember the small blessings I often overlook.

Yes, it is something I hope to continue. No matter how busy life gets, I believe everyone needs that personal moment of peace. The world is already too loud, and sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves is to step away from the noise and just listen to our thoughts, to our hearts, and to where life is trying to lead us.

To me that the definition of a quiet time a place of relaxation, peace of mind.

Thanks for reading hope to see you again @mathewdaddywah

links.title: Money teaches you faster than advice sometimes
links.body:
There are certain things advice alone can’t really teach you. You can listen to people talk about money, saving, spending, or even investing, but it doesn’t always sink in until you experience it yourself.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX4H4HUCBYxLYCqe9Xee85yYe7Co9R5h2V8oL8b5A2fkq/photo_1556742502_ec7c0e9f34b1.jpeg)[source](https://unsplash.com/photos/person-holding-visa-card-and-white-device-lvWw_G8tKsk)

I’ve heard a lot of advice over time. Some of it made sense, some of it didn’t really stick. But the moment money got involved directly, things started becoming clearer.

When you spend your own money on something that doesn’t really matter, you feel it differently. Nobody needs to explain it to you. You already understand where you went wrong. That kind of lesson stays longer than any advice. Even small earnings can change your mindset. The first time I earned something online, it wasn’t anything big. In fact, it was very small.

But it still made me pause and think. It made me realize that values can be created anywhere, it can be created from something as simple as writing or sharing ideas, something other than money.
On Hive, I had a similar experience.
The first few payouts might not look like much, but they carry meaning.

They make you start paying attention.
You begin to ask questions like, what did I do right here? Why did this post perform better than the other one?

That’s how learning starts.
Money has a way of making things real.
It forces you to be more aware, more careful, and more intentional with your actions.
That’s why I don’t ignore small earnings anymore.
They are not just small amounts, they are signals.
They show that something is working, even if it’s still at a very early stage.

And if you pay attention to those signals, you can build on them. Because most people don’t fail because they didn’t have opportunities.
They fail because they didn’t notice what was already working for them.

links.title: How many KMs a day are feasible on a long motorcycle ride in India?
links.body:
![image](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/c1f6a16c6b74a619cfab4aad87addd1c747830ada786189f24157665bf97a040)

Planning distance is essential for a successful motorbike tour india. Unlike highways in other countries, Indian roads vary greatly. On average, riders can comfortably cover 200 to 350 km per day depending on terrain, traffic, and weather conditions.

**Does terrain affect daily riding distance?**

Yes, terrain plays a major role, especially when [traveling to Indian Himalayan by motorcycle](https://www.indiamotorbiketour.com/Destination/himalayas). Mountain routes reduce speed and increase fatigue. During a Himalayan motorcycle tour, riders typically cover:

*   150 to 250 km per day in high altitude regions

*   200 to 300 km on mixed terrain routes

*   Up to 350 km on smoother highways

This is why an india himalayan motorbike tour focuses more on experience than distance.

**What factors influence daily riding limits?**

Several elements impact how far you can ride:

*   Road conditions and elevation changes

*   Rider experience and stamina

*   Weather, especially in the Himalayas

*   Breaks for fuel, food, and rest

A well-planned Himalayan motorbike tour in India considers all these factors to avoid exhaustion.

**What is the ideal strategy for long rides?**

*   Prioritize comfort over distance

*   Follow a flexible itinerary

*   Choose guided tours for better support

A thoughtfully paced journey ensures that your ride remains enjoyable, safe, and truly memorable across India’s diverse landscapes.

links.title: Splinterlands: A new strategy involved purchasing a dozen copies of a magic card! 🔥
links.body: >Just yesterday, I shared with you a trick for making the best possible use of the \

ruleset to your advantage—a strategy I have tried many times, and one that works beautifully every single time. The synergy between Painforge and the ability to deal damage to one's own cards was so impressive that it sparked a thought in my mind: why should this dynamic be limited solely to matches played under the Painforge ruleset? Consequently, I began searching for cards that possess this specific ability. For the time being, my search focused primarily on the Water element, and I successfully discovered an excellent card—\

—specifically of the Magic Attack type. As it happens, I already owned two copies of this card; however, at Level 1, it did not yet possess the Painforge ability. Therefore, I decided to purchase 12 additional copies, as I required a total of 14 copies to upgrade it to Level 3.

\n\n

>At Level 1, this card possessed only the Snipe ability, which grants it the power to attack the first non-melee card; to acquire the Painforge ability, it had to be upgraded to Level 3. As I mentioned, I already possessed two copies of this card; therefore, to reach the required total of 14 copies for Level 3, I needed 12 additional copies. To acquire these, I purchased 12 copies from the market at a rate of $0.079 per copy, costing me a total of $0.95. I then selected these 12 newly acquired copies—along with the two I already owned—and clicked \

thereby upgrading the card to Level 3. If you are a new player, it is also important to understand that in order to use higher-level cards in battle, you require an Archon of the same or a higher level. I am able to do this because I recently upgraded an Archon in the Water element to its maximum level; consequently, I can now utilize this card—as well as other similar cards—at their higher levels.

\n\n

>Now, let me explain my strategy: under the Painforge ability, if a card is struck by its own ally—whether through Poison, Burning, or any other means—that card's Power increases by +1. Typically, the Painforge ruleset offers an advantage only when your team is under the influence of an enemy's Poison or Burning effects; in such instances, it rarely—and only for specific cards—provides a benefit. Thus, in a sense, you could say that this ruleset serves to shield your cards from the potential threat of Poison attacks inherent in the enemy's strategy. However, if you can inflict similar damage upon your own team—even if only slightly—you can proactively grant your team the benefit of gaining that +1 Power boost from Painforge. That is precisely why acquiring this card is an integral part of my plan.

>I will now position the Shock Trooper within my team, placing the Torrent Sniper directly alongside it. The result of this arrangement is that, starting from the beginning of the second round—and in every subsequent round—whenever the Shock Trooper strikes an adjacent card with an electric shock (thanks to its Electrified ability), the Power of that adjacent card will increase by +1. Furthermore, since this card utilizes Magic-type attacks, the damage it inflicts upon the enemy will prove to be quite costly. This synergy will serve to make my Painforge-enabled card even more formidable. I will soon put this strategy to the test with this card and share with all of you exactly how it performed relative to my expectations.😎

* * *

>Splinterlands isn't an easy place, but that's what makes it even more fun. A perfect strategy takes into account many factors, including stats, abilities, rulesets, mana caps, and more. That's why it's even more important to consider all these factors when developing a strategy. Add good cards to your deck, but also work on improving your strategies, and strive to win as many battles as possible!🔥\n\n
>If you also want to enjoy this amazing game and you have not yet signed up, <a target=\

>I invite you to Splinterlands, and I will also try my best to guide you in this game. 😎 * * * `Note:` 1. `English is not my first language. So sometimes I use 'Google Translate'. Please don't think that anything I have written in this blog has been copied from somewhere or is AI-generated.` 2. `Paragraph Dividers and all the photos are from #Splinterlands.` 3. `All the other content images and words are mine unless otherwise stated.`
>Have a Happy and Blessed day!

links.title: THE WAR: The EU has gone mad [eng/срп] РАТ: ЕУ је полудела
links.body:
>

EU politicians are not giving up, nor are they hiding their plans for war against Russia any longer, and the people of Europe are unable to stop them. So what is left?


The war between the European Union and Russia has actually already begun, on the African front. Russia has just prevented a major offensive by colonial powers in Mali. France has hired mercenaries from Europe and Ukraine, and then Tuaregs and Islamists from the region. The offensive that was supposed to carry out the coup failed, but the Minister of Defense, Sadio Camara, was killed in a terrorist attack.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has openly stated this fact, emphasizing that Europe has declared war on Russia by producing drones for Ukraine and allowing them to pass through its airspace to attack Russian civilians. And Russia is slowly losing patience towards EU and NATO. About ten days ago, they published a list of primary targets, drone manufacturing plants in the EU, Turkiye, and Israel:

>

ЕУ политичари не одустају, нити више крију планове о рату против Русије, а народи Европе нису у стању да их зауставе. Шта онда преостаје?


Рат између Европске Уније и Русије заправо је већ почео, и то на Афричком фронту. Русија је управо спречила велику офанзиву колонијалних сила у Малију. Француска је ангажовала плаћенике из Европе и Украјине, а затим и Туареге и исламисте из региона. Офанзива којом је требало извршити преврат није успела, али је у терористичком нападу страдао министар одбране Садио Камара.

Руски министар спољних послова Сергеј Лавров отворено је изнео ту чињеницу, наглашавајући да је Европа објавила рат Русији производњом дронова за Украјину и њиховим пропуштањем кроз свој ваздушни простор за напад на руске цивиле. И Русију полако напушта стрпљење према ЕУ и НАТО. Пре десетак дана објавили су списак примарних циљева, погона који производе дронове на територији ЕУ, Турске и Израела:

[![Spisak pogona po EU-JCcODXkjzDNMetwmBEhRBL.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/23uFuHJxnsjKzjqora9aYj4xwn5yEKDsu67sCCazTfhmQSeNZh4LGmXFy7bR4iRYcurru.jpg)](https://t.me/sputniksrbija/130966)
Source / Извор: [Sputnik Serbia @ Telegram](https://t.me/sputniksrbija/130966)

>

The further development of possible events was described by Sergey Karaganov, Russian political scientist who heads the Council for Foreign and Defense Policy, in an interview to Alexander Kareevsky on Russia 24.

Karaganov is also the dean of the Faculty of World Economy and International Affairs at Moscow's Higher School of Economics. He was a close associate of Yevgeny Primakov, and has been Presidential Advisor to both Boris Yeltsin and Vladimir Putin. He is considered close to Putin and Sergey Lavrov. He is, therefore, someone whose voice is listened to carefully in the Kremlin.

* * *

>‘The EU has gone mad – it must be stopped’
Sergey Karaganov: First and foremost, we need to do something about ourselves. We must understand that, once again, Western Europe has unleashed a war against Russia. That is the plain truth. The initiator of this war was the United States of America, which dragged the EU into it. And now the Americans, having realized that they will not succeed in bringing us down, and moreover having realized that an escalation to the nuclear level is likely and possible, even on US territory, have begun to back off, although they are still warming their hands by the fire of the European war in full swing.

As for the Western Europeans, the EU elites, they are utterly bankrupt. They have no grounds whatsoever to remain in power: no moral, political or economic grounds, they have failed on every front. They are whipping up military hysteria to divert attention from their own problems, but are also preparing for war. And this must be taken seriously. Let me remind you that, over the last five hundred years, Europe has generally been the source of all humanity’s major misfortunes, including most wars, including the two world wars. Therefore, we must not let our guard down.

It is important to realize that a world war has begun. It is being waged in Europe, largely by Western Europeans, whilst the United States of America, together with Israel, has begun to destabilize southern Eurasia.

So, we need to be absolutely clear that this is the situation we find ourselves in. What should the EU do? America is a separate matter, it simply needs to be firmly restrained and steered away from this situation. The EU must finally realize that it will be destroyed if the aggression continues. And the sooner it realizes this, the fewer of our people will die.

Therefore, it seems to me that the time will come when President [Vladimir Putin] must appoint a commander-in-chief in the theater of operations with the authority to use any type of weapon, and even the duty to do so, and incorporate into military doctrine a provision stating that, should war be waged against us, and it has been waged by an enemy that surpasses us in demographic and economic terms, we would have to use nuclear weapons. Naturally, not immediately. First, we can strike the targets indicated by our Ministry of Defense, or others. Most likely, these will be symbolic targets or communication hubs, which will be hit with conventional munitions. If they do not stop, we will have to move to a higher level.

These Western Europeans must be stopped; they have gone mad yet again. Moreover, if we do not stop them now, the situation will be worse in a few years’ time, because the level of anti-Russian propaganda is already exceeding that of Hitler’s era. And, consequently, the population is succumbing to it.

There’s a very simple way to stop this: place a strong emphasis on nuclear deterrence and make it clear that the EU must be stopped. Moreover, as has already been mentioned, some of them are preparing to expand their nuclear capabilities and even to develop new nuclear forces. Monkeys must not be allowed to possess nuclear weapons.

That’s why we must put a firm stop to the EU now. I would prefer this to be done without the use of nuclear weapons, and certainly without a massive strike; after all, Europe is part of our soul, our culture. But we must understand that Western Europe is the embodiment of all the major evils afflicting humanity and Russia. And it must be stopped. It has gone mad.

* * *

>

Даљи развој могућих догађаја описао је Сергеј Караганов, руски политиколог који предводи Савет за спољну и одбрамбену политику, у интервјуу Александру Карејевском на телевизији Русија 24.

Караганов је такође декан Факултета за светску економију и међународне послове на Вишој школи економије у Москви. Био је блиски сарадник Јевгенија Примакова и био је председнички саветник Бориса Јељцина и Владимира Путина. Сматра се блиским Путину и Сергеју Лаврову. Он је, дакле, неко чији се глас у Кремљу пажљиво слуша.

* * *

>‘ЕУ је полудела – мора бити заустављена’
Сергеј Караганов: Пре свега, морамо нешто да урадимо по питању себе. Морамо да схватимо да је Западна Европа поново покренула рат против Русије. То је чиста истина. Покретач овог рата биле су Сједињене Америчке Државе, које су у њега увукле ЕУ. А сад су Американци, схвативши да неће успети да нас оборе, и штавише, схвативши да је ескалација до нуклеарног нивоа вероватна и могућа, чак и на територији САД, почели да се повлаче, иако још увек греју руке ватром европског рата који је у пуном јеку.

狗是一种非常特别的动物，它们忠诚、聪明，能够带给人们无尽的快乐与陪伴。每当看到狗在公园里欢快地奔跑，或者温柔地依偎在主人身边，我都会感受到一种温暖的情感。狗不仅是宠物，更是朋友，它们用无条件的爱回应着我们的关心，让生活增添了许多色彩。与狗相处，不仅是享受快乐时光，更是学习珍惜与陪伴的美好。

links.title: Building My Fintech Side Project as a Freelance Developer
links.body:
![hive_3.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRwUD5TCByDBeLndkg1CSP9iqgFTSzbiixCkoWmom4eg8/hive_3.jpeg)


As a freelancer and contract-based software developer, I always dedicate part of my leisure time to building side projects and staying updated with the latest technologies. Continuous learning is very important to me, and working on personal projects allows me to experiment with new tools and strengthen my technical skills.

As an enthusiastic web and application developer, my journey started with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. JavaScript was the first scripting language I learned, and as my experience grew, I transitioned into TypeScript to benefit from static typing and improved code reliability.

Over time, I have also gained experience working with Solidity and Python/Django, expanding my understanding of blockchain and backend development. My primary development stack has been the MERN stack, but recently I began transitioning to the PERN stack to explore PostgreSQL-based solutions and improve database performance.


![Screenshot (66).png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVTAnSfqc8Q67GhYnfpQvmH1dQZBKSmcf6498AeJMyeBV/Screenshot%20(66).png)

The image above shows the current side project I am working on—a fintech application. The inspiration for this project came from design concepts I discovered on Envato, which helped shape the visual direction of the application.

**The Idea Behind the Project**

The main motivation behind this project comes from observing financial technology trends in Nigeria.

In my observation, many fintech applications in my region mainly focus on transactions using the local currency (Naira), while cryptocurrency-based payment and investment features are still limited. However, many young people are increasingly interested in exploring __digital and crypto-based financial solutions__.

This inspired me to begin developing a platform designed to support both:

- Digital currency transactions (centralized systems)
- Cryptocurrency-based transactions (decentralized systems)

The goal is to create a flexible financial platform where users can perform modern financial operations without being restricted to traditional payment systems.


![Screenshot 2026-04-23 135251.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYsvcDdtnBCv2Ax71t93Z48ynohFGGY7ozn5tGqJpBmCG/Screenshot%202026-04-23%20135251.png)

__Core Features of the Fintech Application__
**Authentication Features**
- Sign Up
- Sign In
- Logout

**Transaction Features**
-  Withdrawal
- Send Money
- Currency Exchange
- Add Money
- Card Management

__Expected Core Functionalities__

To support the features listed above, the application is designed to include the following core functionalities:

* User Account Management
* Secure Authentication System
* Wallet Balance Management
* Money Transfer System
* Withdrawal Processing
* Currency Exchange Engine
* Payment Gateway Integration
* Card Management System
* Transaction Logging
* Notification System

These functionalities represent the backbone of the platform and ensure reliable and secure financial operations.

**Technology Stack Used**

This application is currently being developed using the PERN stack, which includes:
- PostgreSQL — Database
- Express.js — Backend framework
- React.js — Frontend library
- Node.js — Server-side runtime

links.title: I’ve had enough.
links.body:
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/we-are-ai/23y8jMWvAkFUibncGWjmapkx3V9xFguzFuU7mf6AuTE3aZupyKo6WG13SvWzw7HY72LjR.png)



I’ve had enough.

Not just of this or that person—no, of everything in general. Of this suffocating inertia, this feeling of moving forward blindly through thick fog, never quite sure if I’m making progress or just spinning my wheels. Sometimes, it even feels like I’m going backward, as if every effort only pushes me one step further from where I want to be. Time keeps slipping away, and nothing seems to change.
Right now, I’m drowning in paperwork. Endless forms, documents to sign, deadlines to meet—it’s all just a mountain of bureaucratic tasks that eat up my days without any real sense of progress. And then there’s the waiting. Waiting for responses, waiting for appointments, waiting for things to finally move forward. Every day that passes is another day of spending money—again and again—on real-life projects, investments that should pay off, legal steps that should lead somewhere. But so far? Nothing. Or at least, not enough to justify the time and energy I’ve poured into it.

What frustrates me the most is the agonizing slowness of the people I’m paying to handle the legal side of things. They drag their feet, postpone meetings, take weeks to reply to a single email. It’s as if my time doesn’t matter. As if I have nothing better to do than wait for their convenience. And while they waste my time, I’m the one left stagnating—losing motivation, losing focus, losing my drive.
I won’t bore you with all my personal problems—though, let’s be real, they’re weighing heavily on my mind. They irritate me, distract me, make it impossible to fully concentrate on what really matters. Because yes, writing here, tinkering with little bots on this site—that’s not my job. It’s my escape, my hobby, the only thing that still brings me a little joy in this sea of frustration and doubt. A way to clear my head, to remind myself that I can still create, innovate, have fun.

But even that, sometimes, feels hard to enjoy. As if everything is tainted by this lingering frustration, this sense of being trapped in a system that gives me no room to breathe. So I wonder: Will things ever get better? Will I finally see the light at the end of the tunnel? Or am I just going to keep struggling in the dark, spending without results, waiting for something that never comes?
I don’t know. For now, I grit my teeth, keep going, and try to hold onto hope. Because if I give up now, who’s going to fight for me?

links.title: i146 RSD 5, Drawing step by step /Rising Star
links.body: > Happy morning to all my fellow Hive members and colleagues. I hope you're all doing well and having a wonderful day filled with blessings. Today, I want to show you a new drawing I made, inspired by another spectacular card from the Rising Star game. Today, microphones are back, and in this case, it's a common one: the i146 RSD 5. As you can see, it has a classic design that many of us are used to seeing in real life. Although it has a slight difference from the classic design, its top edge is a bit straighter, giving it a more modern look. On truly classic microphones, that area is rounded. In this post, I intend to show you how I made this drawing from beginning to end, so if you'd like to have some fun watching it, stick around. Let's get straight to the point. I started the drawing by sketching the inner frame. ![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo4Js77Ww4LeXLb17fwd2V2Dd5NXqQnjk6kj7d7ZkfcRj5LiTCCpnWLJBtcvS6AGKSw.jpg) After having the frame ready, I moved on to drawing the microphone handle, which is the longer, cylindrical part. After finishing it, I drew the top part on top with its semi-straight design, which makes it look more modern. In fact, I like this design better than the purely classic one. ![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo2BM1YUXi6JumD1KU3U7uVvhcpNybQ8vzSyauX8QqvvzjQCKVDWWsMaZTVFoW4UwMB.jpg) ![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo4JkCmxfZTVXcodtJevCEtWJdGHkDeJnuuAkd741iquo2xR6rNPUUmhuZvmbmnH1J9.jpg) All that was left to do to finish the sketch was to draw some details inside the microphone body. In this case, I drew several internal lines to divide the interior, making it much easier to paint later, since each divided area is for a different color. ![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/Eo6S9Q1ShZHtETTTpF6aaTFMziSpcEneWzgFrmH34P5gtmpXyP7BCP44k65ZimS2ktZ.jpg) With the sketch ready, all that remains is to fill in all the spaces with color. I used blue for everything; in fact, almost the entire drawing is blue in various shades, except for the reflections on top of the microphone and some embellishing details of the device. But it will be more fun if I show you how I drew it all. Here are the screenshots. ![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EoH2i4pUbUrBdxvnPJDkKJooFJG6m4Rtz3uW6hCnnU5JNjRT9XVVwf8oL24smwc13cL.jpg) ![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EnqQcrW3fNFBuTwXLcCuGtJDNWwpy1QcxKhQk1ic53M7JCTcssW1PrGsHVKRq7Niaqz.jpg) ![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EpdeNXSMvRVBuiF8Q94gLMJcwRSfCGLWUY7RizaYYzwnHtFqBHykSaBXLAqmff1derx.jpg) ![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/EqofAdtR6as62s4f7sSFPMTUdozPtxdbaMguRDCgU2p43iUdN2kuhYo7aYSArNRgne8.jpg) And to finish the drawing, here is the presentation of the result. Thank you very much for viewing the drawing. Have a good day. Blessings to all. ![9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dharma1/24327Nfu4WVtTxnTuMLyuXJBhwAqaPbd2dk2fYH5tLGitiXSsDJMNjfcG84xFC5vaDfoG.jpg)

links.title: Television Review: Valar Morghulis (Game of Thrones, S2X10, 2012)
links.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/zmK0CjYZuYUu1DatmBQlYFPR4JL.jpg)

**Valar Morghulis (S02E10)**

Airdate: 3 June 2012

Written by: David Benioff & D. B. Weiss
Directed by: Alan Taylor

Running Time: 64 minutes 



In its second season, *Game of Thrones* continued its established tradition of utilising the season finale not as a locus for cataclysmic, audience-shocking twists, but as a narrative mop-up operation. The penultimate episode, *[Blackwater](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-blackwater-game-of-thrones-s2x09-2012)*, delivered the season’s undeniable ‘wham’ moment: the decisive, spectacular Battle for King’s Landing. *Valar Morghulis*, the concluding chapter, is thus tasked almost entirely with sifting through the aftermath, charting the political and personal consequences of the Lannister victory. Yet, its true narrative ambition lies in its deliberate focus on characters and forces operating far from the capital’s smoke-clogged skies. By checking in on the Starks in the North, Daenerys in Qarth, and Jon Snow beyond the Wall, the episode subtly argues that the seismic events of *Blackwater*—while defining the immediate future of the Iron Throne—may ultimately pale in significance against longer-brewing storms. The War of the Five Kings is revealed as a brutal, cynical game of musical chairs, while the real existential threats gather in the frozen darkness and across the Narrow Sea.

The episode’s most potent illustration of this cynical reality is found in King’s Landing itself, where the architect of the city’s salvation is unceremoniously discarded. Tyrion Lannister, having nearly paid for his strategic genius with his life, awakes to a world that has moved on without him. Grand Maester Pycelle’s gleeful revelation that Tyrion is no longer Hand, that his father Tywin has assumed the role, and that his sellsword ally Bronn has been stripped of his command, is a telling example of political ingratitude. The nasty scar bisecting his face becomes a metaphor for his new station: marked, diminished, and a visible reminder of a service the regime would rather forget. His lover Shae’s desperate urging to flee underscores his precarious position, yet Tyrion’s decision to stay is the first stirring of a deeper, more bitter understanding of the game. His subsequent visit from Varys, who offers sympathy and a frank admission of the injustice, serves as a confirmation: in the theatre of power, the stagehands who save the production are never allowed to take a bow.

That theatre is in full, grotesque swing in the Iron Throne room. In an over-theatrical display of realpolitik, the balance of power shifts publicly and decisively. King Joffrey, the capricious boy-king whose cowardice and folly nearly lost the city, is now the beneficiary of Tywin Lannister and Petyr Baelish’s machinations. His breaking of the betrothal to Sansa Stark—framed as a punishment for her family’s treason—and his new pledge to marry Margaery Tyrell cements the essential Lannister-Tyrell alliance. Baelish, the broker, is rewarded with the hollow title of Lord of Harrenhal, a transaction performed with the calculating clarity of a stock exchange. The irony is layered: Joffrey, a paragon of vile impulsiveness, here performs a act of cold, strategic reason for the good of the realm, while Sansa, the victim, feels only profound relief. Yet Baelish’s whispered promise to help her escape is a chilling reminder that her value as a political prisoner remains undiminished; her personal relief is irrelevant to the currents of power that still hold her fast.

This theme of noble intentions succumbing to personal folly finds its purest expression in Robb Stark’s camp. The Young Wolf, hitherto the show’s most unambiguously heroic figure, makes a decision that undercuts his strategic position entirely. His marriage to Talisa Maegyr, conducted in a simple ceremony of the Faith of the Seven, is a romantic gesture of breathtaking political naivety. Catelyn Stark’s warnings about breaking the sacred pact with Walder Frey hang heavy in the air, ignored. The scene is subdued, almost intimate, which makes its future ramifications all the more devastating. The script, by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss, here employs a sharp, tragic irony: Robb, the honourable king, chooses love and breaks an oath, while Joffrey, the dishonourable monster, chooses duty and secures an alliance. It is a deliberate inversion that begins the process of deconstructing the Stark myth of inherent virtue, a process that continues elsewhere.

Indeed, *Valar Morghulis* actively works to complicate the show’s moral binary. This is most starkly demonstrated in the brief but brutal scene with Brienne of Tarth and her captive, Jaime Lannister. Confronted with the hanged, mutilated corpses of three peasant women—accused of ‘lying with lions’—they discover the perpetrators are Stark soldiers. Brienne’s swift, lethal dispatch of her own side’s men is a pivotal moment. It is partly pragmatic (to silence witnesses), but primarily an act of a personal chivalric code that transcends factional loyalty. The episode forces the audience to witness the brutal reality of war from the ground level: there are no purely virtuous armies, and the Stark cause, however just in its origins, is now being prosecuted by men capable of rape and murder. This nuanced, cynical approach to morality is a hallmark of the series at its best.

The episode’s narrative sprawl allows it to efficiently set numerous other plotlines in motion. Arya Stark’s escape from Harrenhal brings her face-to-face once more with the mysterious Jaqen H’ghar. His offer to teach her the arts of assassination is a fork in the road for her character; her refusal, driven by a desperate desire to reunite her family, is poignant. Yet the gift of the Braavosi coin and the password “Valar morghulis” (all men must die) is an irresistible narrative hook, as is Jaqen’s stunning, magical transformation of his own face—a moment that expands the show’s mystical boundaries and deeply imprints on the young girl’s psyche. Her path is no longer simply one of survival, but of potential transformation.

In Winterfell, another kind of transformation occurs: utter destruction. Theon Greyjoy’s pathetic last stand, undercut by his own men’s betrayal, completes his arc from arrogant invader to tragic fool. Maester Luwin’s dying counsel to Bran—to head north to the Wall, not south to safety—is a crucial piece of narrative guidance, steering the true heir of Winterfell toward his mystical destiny. The burning of Winterfell is not just the loss of a castle; it is the symbolic annihilation of the Stark home, the centre of northern power and identity, making Robb’s southern gambit seem all the more rootless.

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys Targaryen’s storyline reaches a crescendo that, while visually and narratively satisfying, hints at future repetitive patterns. Her journey through the surreal, prophetic visions of the House of the Undying—the Iron Throne room desolate and snow-strewn, a reunion with Khal Drogo and their unborn son—is one of the episode’s most memorable sequences, beautifully directed by Alan Taylor. It ties her destiny inextricably to Westeros. Her confrontation with Pyat Pree, however, resolves with a simplicity that borders on contrivance. The command “Dracarys” and the ensuing dragonfire are thrilling, but they establish a template: an Essosi adversary dramatically underestimates Daenerys and her dragons, only to be spectacularly incinerated. Her subsequent justice against Xaro Xhoan Daxos and Doreah, walling them alive in his empty vault, is a stark display of her growing ruthlessness. Yet, as with Pyat Pree, it feels somewhat neat, a villain disposed of rather than truly grappled with.

North of the Wall, the narrative lays two crucial pieces for the coming conflict. Jon Snow’s killing of Qhorin Halfhand—a staged act of treason to cement his cover with the wildlings—is a brutal rite of passage that severs his last clean tie to the Night’s Watch. Meanwhile, Samwell Tarly’s terrifying encounter with the army of the dead provides the episode’s chilling, masterful finale. The three horn blasts, the grotesque wights shambling through the blizzard, and the final reveal of their unimaginable numbers marching southwards is a stark, visual rebuke to the political squabbling of the south. It tells Sam, and the audience, in no uncertain terms where the true, existential danger lies. All the spectacle of Blackwater is rendered momentarily trivial by this silent, advancing horror.

If the episode has a significant flaw, it is found in a rare moment of clumsy exposition. The scene where Varys explicitly recruits the prostitute Ros as a spy lacks the subtlety that typically defines the Spider’s machinations. Ros, portrayed as a shrewd survivor, seems inexplicably unaware of Varys’s status as a eunuch, a fact widely known in the capital. The dialogue feels engineered to explain Varys’s methods and network to the audience, rather than arising naturally from the characters. This lack of narrative subtlety would become a more persistent issue in the series’ later seasons.

Ultimately, *Valar Morghulis* is a remarkably efficient and effective season finale. It performs the necessary function of resetting the board after the climactic battle, but does so with a consistent, cynical intelligence. The balance of power has shifted back toward the Lannisters, but at the cost of exposing the hollow, thankless nature of their rule. The Starks are weakened, both by the literal destruction of their home and the metaphorical crumbling of their leader’s honour. New powers—Daenerys with her dragons, the White Walkers with their legion of the dead—are announced not with with fire and ice. The episode understands that in the world of *Game of Thrones*, the most important moves are often made in the quiet aftermath of the noise, and that the phrase “valar morghulis” is not just a Braavosi greeting, but a reminder that in the grand, grim scheme of things, all men must die—some merely with more consequence than others.



RATING: 8/10 (+++)

links.title: El llanto que no llegó a ser, escuchado en el otro plano.😔 (ES-EN)
links.body:
> --- Negro y blanco, blanco y negro, con algunas tonalidades de grises, siempre son así, siempre mis ojos se ven privados de ver colores en ese lugar. Un espacio donde reina el desconsuelo, el dolor, sufrimiento, el miedo y el terror más profundo. > Black and white, white and black, with a few shades of gray, it’s always like that; my eyes are always deprived of color in that place. A space where despair, pain, suffering, fear, and the deepest terror reign. --- ![Image_1777232501780.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wX13Z5EUu1y7qWvF54VaCYVrQ1cVXidzFi6soo4NnKJGgaXtHnUY1zhYrg9WLY7BRhv.jpg) ![separador sangre.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xyLavpsC6UFevyftDZ9nego9qqgS3Ys2aohVYeowcv6uw89kdQxQk9E5SABcyCMuwEQ.png) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yRZxF6SVvJs Para escuchar mientras se lee la historia – To listen to whilst reading the story [Fuente](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yRZxF6SVvJs) ---
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

Sometimes I walk down a staircase; other times I simply appear there, but I know that if I find myself in that torment, it is because there is something I must know, as a forewarning, a warning or a precaution. But there is never any colour in that place, except in this case. I recalled nightmares from the past, tangled and strange, where I could make no sense of anything, where everything was twisted as if my mind were protecting me, saying… you’re not ready yet. I have seen so many things from that realm that I sometimes lose count; I have gone there so many times to truly see, to see personal matters, those of family, friends, and even the whole world. Many came true, and others remain unfulfilled. >But one thing is certain: if I see it first-hand, I will see it again in the real world; it will happen with no turning back. First I cried, then I accepted it, and now I live with it, knowing that it is part of my soul and that she is safe and ready—she is ready now. Before me there was colour, but only in one part of the whole. The rest was dark; its depth had no limit whatsoever, as if black ivory oil had painted the scene, leaving only the centre to be filled in later. I could see him inside his mother’s womb; there he was, looking healthy. The only splash of colour revealed in the whole. My gaze did not stray from the centre; I had never seen colours in the black world, the world of nightmares in its entirety. That child had the colour of life and was moving. It was a child, and I knew it because my intuition told me so, something that strikes the heart very strongly when life takes hold. A child with strength and vitality who would soon move, but the dark background was what I did not understand. I did not stop looking at him inside his mother’s womb, which was not mine; I knew that, because I could see her, though not her face, so I never knew who she was. ---

![20250418_170005.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23w2uVi3s5K7hqgtn6YANUkrYYjFKoCeDumZKX6JETasCt2BArYKzoLFuVaLmrre5odHq.jpg)
![separador sangre.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xyLavpsC6UFevyftDZ9nego9qqgS3Ys2aohVYeowcv6uw89kdQxQk9E5SABcyCMuwEQ.png) --- >The movements were very sudden, and what I saw filled my eyes with horror. My tears fell unceasingly at the sight of such an atrocity. Something was happening because the child was being torn apart. I felt intense pain in my chest, as if a stake were being driven into my left side. His face was deforming, turning into a shapeless mass, and darkness was creeping into his belly. I didn’t know what was happening, but I did know that there would be no colours or life there anymore. Seeing inside his belly and what the child was going through was something I hadn’t expected. His dark-coloured legs and little arms were twisting, and I knew that life there would not return. Each part vanished as life left the womb. Everything within him moved abruptly, unexpectedly and distressingly, until the colour faded and the world of nightmares filled everything. >I woke up terrified, in a cold sweat, trembling and desperate; I had witnessed the departure of a cry that was never uttered. Where would that child be? That was my first thought, followed by the sadness of being unable to do anything, though I was sure I would soon find out. I thought of my brother’s wife, happily pregnant, but time passed and everything went smoothly. But I had forgotten one thing: that in my distant family, a woman I didn’t know was pregnant. And that child was going to be my very distant cousin; his grandmother, my close second cousin. >Blood ties, however tenuous they may be, always reveal themselves, in dreams, in signs that life sends my way. ---
![20250418_170045.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23zRwBCrbxm9mQBAdjeDEGxDGsotT7tnnubQagbAGZmwXeXxRtR25xghTMz71ESemrkh2.jpg)
![separador sangre.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xyLavpsC6UFevyftDZ9nego9qqgS3Ys2aohVYeowcv6uw89kdQxQk9E5SABcyCMuwEQ.png) ---

A veces desciendo por una escalera, otras simplemente allí aparezco, pero sé que si en ese tormento estoy es porque algo debo saber como anticipo, aviso o prevención. Pero nunca en ese lugar hay color, salvo en este caso. Recordé pesadillas del pasado, enmarañadas y extrañas donde nada podía sacar en claro, donde todo estaba retorcido como si mi mente me protegiera diciendo… aún no estás preparada. Tantas cosas de ese plano he visto, que a veces pierdo la cuenta, tantas veces he ido para realmente ver, ver cosas personales, de familiares, amistades, y hasta del mundo entero. Muchas se hicieron realidad y otras quedan aún en el tintero. >Pero una cosa es cierta, si en primera persona lo veo, volveré a verlo en el mundo real, sucederá sin marcha atrás. Primero lloré, luego lo acepté y ahora convivo con ello, sabiendo que es parte de mi alma y que ella está segura y preparada, ahora lo está. Frente a mí había color, pero sólo en una parte del todo. Lo demás era oscuro, su profundidad no tenía límite alguno, como si el óleo negro marfil hubiera pintado la escena, dejando sólo el centro para rellenar luego. Pude verlo dentro del vientre de su madre, allí estaba, parecía saludable. Lo único de color que en el todo se revelaba. Mi mirada no se desviaba del centro, jamás había visto colores en el mundo negro, el mundo de las pesadillas por entero. Ese niño tenía el color de la vida y se movía. Era un niño y yo lo sabía porque la intuición me lo decía, algo que se da muy fuerte en el corazón cuando la vida lleva la razón. Un niño con fuerza y vitalidad que pronto se movería, pero fondo oscuro era lo que no entendía. No dejé de mirarlo dentro del vientre de su madre, que no era el mío, lo sabía, porque a ella la veía, aunque no su rostro, por lo que nunca supe de quien se trataría. --- ![20250418_171008.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23zGaD7NiMxCUAK8GYGEhSZr77is1wbBwARePH6Zfh3VddRZSN2sTh1FzwqJ1PJe4F3rJ.jpg) ![separador sangre.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xyLavpsC6UFevyftDZ9nego9qqgS3Ys2aohVYeowcv6uw89kdQxQk9E5SABcyCMuwEQ.png) --- >Los movimientos fueron muy bruscos y lo que vi, el horror inundó mis ojos. Mis lágrimas caían sin cesar al ver semejante atrocidad. Algo estaba pasando porque el niño se estaba desmembrando. Sentí dolor intenso en el pecho como quien clava una estaca del lado izquierdo. Su rostro se deformaba, se convertía en tun todo sin forma dada y la oscuridad al vientre se adentraba. No sabía que pasaba, pero si sabía que allí ya no habría colores ni vida. Ver el interior del vientre y lo que el niño pasaba es algo que no me esperaba. Sus piernas y bracitos de color oscuro se tornaban y sabía que la vida allí no retornaba. Cada parte desaparecía como del vientre la vida. Todo en el se movía abruptamente, inesperado y angustioso, hasta que el color desapareció y el mundo de las pesadillas todo lo llenó. >Desperté aterrada, con sudor frío, temblando y desesperada, había presenciado la partida de un llanto que jamás fue exclamado. Donde estaría ese niño fue mi primer pensamiento, seguido de la tristeza de no poder hacer nada, pero que seguro pronto de ello estaría enterada. Pensé en la jefa de mi hermano, felizmente embarazada, pero pasó el tiempo y todo transcurrió sin problema alguno. Pero de una cosa me olvidaba, que en mi familia lejana una mujer que no conozco estaba embarazada. Y ese niño iba a ser mi primo muy lejano, su abuela mi prima segunda cercana. >Los hilos de sangre por más finos que se hagan siempre se delatan, en sueños, en señales que la vida me alcanza. --- ![20250418_171203.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wqiZrondjpzpbc4DDJXbcfndhgRhK3FmVimd5WNFYUgNe4naE2TqbBHE7WmPMY2f3aL.jpg) ![separador sangre.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xyLavpsC6UFevyftDZ9nego9qqgS3Ys2aohVYeowcv6uw89kdQxQk9E5SABcyCMuwEQ.png) ---

The harmattan dust hung thick over the village of Amawbia, but inside the small wooden shed, the air was heavy with a different kind of tension. Emeka held out the scholarship form, its edges softened by weeks of nervous handling.
​\
Adamma said, her voice barely a whisper. She was scrubbing a blackened pot, her knuckles white. \
\n​Emeka stepped closer, the paper trembling slightly. \
\n​Adamma finally looked up, her eyes searching his. \
\n​Emeka didn’t flinch. He placed the form on the table between them. \
He leaned in, his gaze unwavering. \
\n​Seeing the fire in his eyes, Adamma’s resistance flickered and died. She wiped her hands on her apron and reached out, steadying his hand over the paper.\n​\
she said, a small, proud smile finally breaking through. \

links.title: Are You Ready to Build a Future in Data Science?
links.body:
In today’s data-driven world, the demand for skilled professionals who can interpret and analyze data is growing rapidly. Businesses rely on data to make smarter decisions, improve efficiency, and stay competitive. This shift has created exciting career opportunities for individuals who want to enter the field of data science. If you are exploring options to build a strong career foundation, enrolling in a [Data science course in Chandigarh](https://www.cbitss.in/data_science_course_chandigarh/) can be a practical and rewarding step.

Chandigarh has emerged as an educational hub, offering quality training programs that combine theoretical knowledge with real-world applications. Whether you are a fresh graduate or a working professional, learning data science can open doors to multiple high-paying and future-proof career paths.



![Data science course in Chandigarh (4).png](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/8ef4658d3fb45addcce44f05bf2615bf3f951a097ff86681f33bf93aa252afb3)





***



### Why Data Science Is a Smart Career Choice

Data science is not just a trend; it is a long-term career option with strong growth potential. Organizations across industries—healthcare, finance, retail, and technology—are actively seeking professionals who can extract meaningful insights from data.

The field offers diverse roles such as data analyst, data scientist, machine learning engineer, and business analyst. These roles not only come with attractive salaries but also provide opportunities for continuous learning and career growth.

Another advantage is flexibility. Data science skills are transferable across industries, allowing professionals to switch domains without starting from scratch. This makes it a versatile and secure career option in an ever-changing job market.



***



### What You Learn in a Data Science Program

A well-structured program focuses on both foundational and advanced concepts. When you enroll in a Data science course in Chandigarh, you typically gain hands-on experience in key areas such as:

#### Programming Skills

You learn programming languages like Python and R, which are essential for data analysis and automation. These tools help you handle large datasets and perform complex computations efficiently.

#### Statistics and Mathematics

Understanding statistical concepts is crucial for analyzing data accurately. Topics like probability, hypothesis testing, and regression analysis form the backbone of data science.

#### Data Visualization

Communicating insights effectively is just as important as finding them. Tools like Tableau, Power BI, and Matplotlib help you present data in a visually appealing and easy-to-understand format.

#### Machine Learning Basics

You are introduced to algorithms that allow systems to learn from data. This includes supervised and unsupervised learning techniques used in real-world applications.

#### Real-World Projects

Most programs emphasize practical learning through projects. These projects help you apply your knowledge to solve real business problems, making you job-ready.



***



### Why Choose Chandigarh for Your Learning Journey

Chandigarh is known for its quality education system and well-developed infrastructure. It offers a balanced environment for learning, with access to experienced trainers and modern facilities.

Training institutes in Chandigarh often focus on industry-relevant skills, ensuring that students are prepared for real-world challenges. Many programs also offer placement assistance, helping learners transition smoothly into professional roles.

Another advantage is affordability. Compared to metropolitan cities, Chandigarh provides high-quality education at a more reasonable cost, making it accessible to a wider audience.



***



### Skills That Make You Stand Out

To succeed in data science, technical knowledge alone is not enough. Employers look for a combination of skills that enable you to work effectively in a professional environment.

#### Analytical Thinking

You should be able to approach problems logically and break them down into manageable parts.

#### Communication Skills

Explaining complex data insights in simple terms is a valuable skill. It helps stakeholders understand and act on your findings.

#### Problem-Solving Ability

Data science often involves dealing with incomplete or messy data. Being able to find solutions in such situations is essential.

#### Continuous Learning

The field evolves rapidly, so staying updated with new tools and technologies is important for long-term success.



***



### Career Opportunities After Completion

Completing a Data science course in Chandigarh can lead to various career paths depending on your interests and expertise.

You can start as a data analyst, where you interpret data and generate reports to support business decisions. Another option is becoming a data scientist, where you build predictive models and work on advanced analytics.

If you enjoy working with data visualization, you can specialize in creating dashboards and reports. For those interested in artificial intelligence, machine learning roles offer exciting opportunities.

Additionally, roles like business analyst and data engineer are also in demand, providing multiple avenues for career growth.



***



### Choosing the Right Course

Selecting the right program is crucial for your success. Look for courses that offer a balanced mix of theory and practical training. Experienced instructors, updated curriculum, and real-world projects are key factors to consider.

Placement support is another important aspect. A good institute will provide guidance on resume building, interview preparation, and job placement opportunities.

If you are specifically interested in analytics, you may also explore a [Data Analyst Course in Chandigarh](https://www.cbitss.in/data-analyst-course-in-chandigarh/), which focuses more on data interpretation and visualization skills.



***



### Conclusion

Building a career in data science is a smart decision in today’s digital age. With the right training and dedication, you can become a valuable asset to any organization. Enrolling in a Data science course in Chandigarh gives you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals, gain practical exposure, and prepare for a successful future.

The journey requires effort and continuous learning, but the rewards—both professional and personal—are well worth it. If you are ready to step into a high-demand field, now is the perfect time to begin.



***



### FAQs

1\. Who can enroll in a data science course?
Anyone with a basic understanding of mathematics and an interest in data can enroll. Both fresh graduates and working professionals can benefit from it.

2\. Do I need coding experience to start?
No, most beginner-level courses start from the basics and gradually build your programming skills.

3\. How long does it take to complete a data science course?
The duration typically ranges from 3 to 12 months, depending on the depth and structure of the program.

4\. What job roles can I get after completing the course?
You can apply for roles such as data analyst, data scientist, business analyst, or machine learning engineer.

5\. Is data science a high-paying career?
Yes, data science roles are among the highest-paying jobs due to the growing demand for skilled professionals.

6\. Are there placement opportunities after the course?
Many institutes offer placement assistance, including interview preparation and job referrals.

---

links.title: Why the suburbs of Chiang Mai is a great place for an expat to live
links.body:
There are some expat hot spots all over Thailand where it seems the foreigners gravitate towards in order to live here.  I think the most popular ones are Phuket, Krabi, Bangkok, Chiang Mai, and unfortunately Pattaya.   

I wouldn't want to live in any of those places other than here and perhaps Krabi, but Krabi is kind of uninhabited and there aren't a lot of things that you would get in a place with more people in it such as shopping malls, tons of restaurants, and flights to almost anywhere.

But here in Chiang Mai the downtown area is not really a good place to try to live if you are moving here.  Most people are correct when they say that the rent there is overpriced to the point of being a ripoff for foreigners but this is why people who are considering living here should really hire an agent and have a look at one of the suburb areas such as Sansai Noi where I have lived for the past 5 years.  

<center> https://s1.rea.global/img/800x600-fit/fazwaz/th/ac4bb82e132ea4f35c0d18633bf637ea.jpg</center>

When you get out into the suburbs of Chiang Mai a lot of things change.  For one thing, the traffic is almost non existent unless you get on one of the highways that leads to downtown.  I don't really have much reason to ever go down to the center of town and if I do I find that it is a rather easy ride either on my bicycle or my scooter.   It is 12 km one way, which might seem like a bit of a jaunt for some people but it really doesn't take that long and if you don't like driving, you can get a Grab taxi for a couple of dollars.

Another benefit of living out here is that most of the neighborhoods are specifically designed so that it would be of no benefit for anyone to try to use them as some sort of shortcut.  If something like this ends up accidentally happening the owners of the area will wall off the exit or entrance that is causing this and also lay down speed bumps to prevent any sort of traffic from coming  through other than people that live there.

As far as shopping is concerned, no matter where you live in Chiang Mai you are never very far from some sort of massive grocery store that also doubles as a sort of minimall.

<center> https://www.chiangmailocator.com/design/photosbiz/chiang-mai-tesco-lotus-chiang-mai-kad-kamtiang-6059.jpg
[src](https://www.chiangmailocator.com/design/photosbiz/chiang-mai-tesco-lotus-chiang-mai-kad-kamtiang-6059.jpg)</center>

The one nearest my house used to be called Tesco, which I think most people in the world is a brand that they are familiar with, but for whatever reason in the past 2 years they have rebranded to be called Lotus's, which is a stupid name but as far as what is going on inside the store is concerned, nothing has really changed.  All of these shopping centers have a grocery store and they also tend to have some level of banking and ability to pay your bills such as internet, electric or water.   The one nearest my place is just 1.5 km away and most of the time I just take my bicycle.   

Of course we now have the option to just do online shopping and get all of that delivered as well, for the truly lazy.

All these suburb places have a bunch of local restaurants and you don't necessarily need to be able to speak Thai to go to them.  They tend to have picture menus at all of them or you could just learn the name of some sort of dish that you know you already like.

one of the best things about living in the suburbs is that most of Chiang Mai has a surplus of housing outside of the downtown area and therefore there isn't a lot of price gouging that is going on out here.  The people who own the property are not going to get some sort of wild notion that they can just double your rent after your first year in an attempt to fleece you.   

The downside of these places is that they can prove kind of difficult to find unless you have unlimited time and the desire to just drive around looking for \

signs that are unlikely to be in English anyway.  I can speak Thai on a very rudimentary level so I wouldn't want to be on the phone with the owner of my house.  Various apps such as Whatsapp or even more popular in Thailand and app called LINE, have built in AI translation tools so that can facilitate speaking to your landlord even if you don't share a language. 

The best thing to do though is to find a real-estate agent and just book a day to go and visit them and look at pictures.  I had an amazing agent that took time out of her day to drive me around in her car and show me a bunch of places and I ended up renting one of them in the same day.  My 2 bedroom, 2 bath, 2 story house that was mostly fully furnished costs me 9000 THB a month, and that is less than $300.   After electric, water, and internet charges are built in I pay less than $350 a month.   That's a pretty great deal and you are never going to find a deal like that in the city center.

I feel like I have really struck gold living out here in San Sai, and I think that other people that are considering moving to this part of the country would do well to follow suit.   Living downtown in Chiang Mai can be a bit of a drag because everything is always busy but out here in the suburbs I sometimes forget that I live in one of the most populated place in the country because if I don't leave my neighborhood, it is quiet and nice like a small city would be.  Yet giant shopping malls are just around the corner a few km's away!

body.title: Is travelling in India by motorcycle with little experience a good idea?
body.body:
![image](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/b731afc3b3a776b348c19b933a2643dd99935d3dd3e2f3eb8520f784380ea127)

Travelling to India by motorcycle sounds adventurous, but for beginners, it requires careful thought. India offers diverse terrains, unpredictable traffic, and varying road conditions. While the experience can be rewarding, limited riding skills may turn the journey challenging rather than enjoyable.

**What challenges should new riders expect?**

A motorbike tour india experience often includes:

*   Traffic congestion in cities that demands quick reflexes

*   Changing weather and road surfaces, especially in mountains

*   Long riding hours that test endurance

*   Limited familiarity with local driving behavior

For riders with little experience, these factors can increase risk and fatigue.

**Can beginners still enjoy an india motorbike tour?**

Yes, but preparation is key. Many [guided india motorbike tour](https://www.indiamotorbiketour.com/) options are designed for international travelers and provide support such as backup vehicles, route planning, and experienced guides. This makes a motorcycle tour in Asia more accessible even for less experienced riders.

What is the safest approach for first-time riders?

*   Choose organized tours instead of solo travel

*   Practice on similar terrain before arrival

*   Start with shorter routes before attempting long-distance rides

With the right support and realistic expectations, even beginners can enjoy the thrill of riding across India while staying safe and confident.

body.title: Gardening is Good for the Soul!
body.body: Today turned out to be a largely *\

* day — thanks to a variety of circumstances — and I must admit that I feel better for it!

![2904.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/denmarkguy/EoGxN6fYxmhcR2C3C8PexeBa45ZoNs7YDa664xMuvSoAXxsirDcwv9wBFS32eZEPEsJ.jpg)

Because it was a bright and sunny spring day, Mrs. Denmarkguy and I talked about the *possibility* of doing some gardening, even though we both had a lot of *\

* that needed attending to. 

Then our son randomly showed up around 10:00am — unannounced, from Seattle, a couple of hours away — to pick up a package he had had sent here and then wanted to take us to breakfast... and we decided on a place that just *happened* to be most of the way to the organic nursery we like, so we figured we might as well go get some plants...

Which led to us really needing to clean out the raised beds in our vegetable garden and doing some soil conditioning before planting... and before you knew it, we'd managed to spend a good 6-7 hours gardening... and that was really a very welcome break from the general noise of the external world. 

![2912.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/denmarkguy/Ep1Wrok3MwE5Z71p9qMYmwwreAfghN2MYwofFUXTgpzkDdaEofsvugfCmfbW2oogkb1.jpg)

The only time we even *touched* our phones was to occasionally snap a photo of our progress.

I can't say that I *missed* being constantly plugged in.

Maybe Mrs. Denmarkguy and I are *\
* where we remember a time before mobile devices and even Internet so unplugging is not as *\
* as it might be to somebody in their 20s... but, frankly, I could feel my general *\

* come down substantially. 

Of course, I have a sketchy relationship with phones in the first place... because of so many years spent where the *only* reason the phone would ring would be either because it was a bill collector, or someone needing help with something. 

![2794.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/denmarkguy/Eos2JSA6tEZKgQWamBHW3vUgQtTxBKDGFqNG9W9JS6UoedMLCihj1FVJmZ9knnoitcd.jpg)

As days go, today was a good one, and a poignant reminder of just *how much* time we spend with our noses pressed on glass!

Thanks for stopping by and have a great week ahead!

body.title: The 111th Anniversary of the Armenian Genocide
body.body:
![mem1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/namiks/23tbo36xEgMdBHoy5BXfF53kvusJcrfm8tGFrMEuRCBiUnMre2feTFFfvfC9yQdwgWyi3.jpg)

April 24th is the remembrance day to the Armenian Genocide which took place back in 1915 at the hands of the Ottoman Empire. In recent years the date has also grown to become a day of grieving for those who had lost friends and relatives in the more recent conflicts that had taken place, which were also against Turkey and Azerbaijan. This is a pretty tense day for Armenians, and thousands upon thousands go to a specific place in Yerevan dedicated to those who suffered during the Armenian Genocide. A monument built in the Soviet era that sits above a large hill. Within is an eternal flame. 

![mem2 1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/namiks/23tbyhzEL3p3486Q1cFNRBUzMcFLEmitzRCHrcSC7GHaYsUu84HcsUnF73P31nk3bPEGS.jpg)

People come and place flowers around it. One after the other. Some groups perform various types of music to pay their respects. On a relatively warm and cloudy day, I went and observed. As people crammed into such a small space and the flowers piled up. To shoot anything here was a great challenge. Many film crews, a directional line for people to walk to try to handle the sheer number of people coming and going. I entered from the wrong side it appears, having walked up against the crowds of people to the monument and entering from the exit. Once inside, I stood for a while.

![mem3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/namiks/23tbPcjZhyykYtaYVBm18iNdU7DEPbo7zvnfcQTG1hb53n8QGhzVjQEpJSdRq7mgTXL9w.jpg)

I could feel the emotion here. People still talked, laughed, and took photographs of their own. But the atmosphere was quite raw. You could see that this was a difficult subject for many. This wasn't just a ritual that took place every year. Many of those people attending would've directly lost people in those aforementioned recent conflicts and for them these two events were the same. That their struggles had never really ended a century later. That the pain remains more raw than ever.
![mem4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/namiks/48TK4PisC9CYB6HbxE3KCmargukRjvW4FM2uuX4RENaQShX33k1anmQEu4mewcY91G.jpg)

I shot the images mostly with Soviet glass. I wasn't happy with the clinical sharpness of the 35mm or the 85mm despite trying to photograph with both of those lenses. I wanted more separation, I wanted to capture the depth and interactions of people as they placed flowers, but I also didn't want to get too close to them, I wanted to give them that space. I opted for the 37mm Mir and the 58mm Helios, both performing wonderfully in that bokeh, that vintage look in the colours, and the background separation that it did offer when I could get it. I did want to photograph the people more, but again, I wanted to keep some distance and be respectful. As to not get into their faces with a lens as they pay respects to family members, friends, or distant relatives.
![mem6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/namiks/23xKtRNK5Qf8QTRfRcpCstgTSsop6grz8kSyYCZzv6x7jZFtWjE3eYpNWgm1Dqes18U9n.jpg)

I think that vintage look from the lenses also helped with the more emotional side of things. It's less about detail and sharpness and more about the emotion and colours present. I cropped these final images to give them a bit more of a tighter scene, focusing on specific people or objects to highlight some narrative.

![mem7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/namiks/EoEp3jhT8wwpT2S2pmhrEgpQQy3Kc3JBRhTBD1S22b4JNAHbwpLFTyotrQExoX4uyUh.jpg)

![mem5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/namiks/23wgQCo3txigx2hijkfoVB86xutjpTHwZ85q2YmLG67KZj85DZrAKnVzJd3GSHVZeZ8z4.jpg)

And this last one was shot on the 85mm. I tried to use it and just didn't like the feeling it gave. It didn't capture enough. A bit too tight. After all, it is more of a portrait focal length and less something that really captures enough to show emotion within space.

body.title: Cycling just doesn't feel intense:  But some experts suggest it is really good for you
body.body:
After a rather long run the other day that resulted in my phone actually temporarily switching off because of the amount of sweat that got into it, I had a bit of a pain in my right leg that to me suggested that maybe I shouldn't go on yet another run and aggravate the situation.  

Therefore I decided to go for a bike ride with no particular goal in mind.

It turns out that cycling area was going to make that decision for me because there were so many people out there that I couldn't really get up to a speed that I would consider to be good exercise.

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tGa4Gcg5VdJ4rbCmUFE8UJ5EuQkGB2m6AYByMUp8h9jDMqB26Vr5dj6DVev4S7Pdcun.png)
</center>

After an hour I wasn't tired, I hadn't really felt as though I was working very hard, and I had plenty of water remaining but I went home because of one big problem, my butt was sore from the seat.  

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tbEbodzqJ5BZjfA4sXMCbyJ9N2gA4noxZU3sVKXBkzCDuLCnrPVyZbyBMpLZPGU9hyL.png)
</center>

These are km/hr by the way, not a per km time like is displayed in running.  

For me, I was restricted by the masses and how we had a bunch of people that don’t seem to understand that the left lane is for passing, not hanging around and talking to your buddy, so I was never really able to push myself.   Another thing that kind of makes cycling feel as though it is too easy is the technology.   I have 21 gears and while my bike isn’t top-end, that does make almost any situation something where I don’t have to work very hard because where I live is almost entirely completely flat 

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tGTmRvhMEzb9a2Hr3gzDEJpNd76UVAyaB57zHYcSZ4EmKGYo8xovfJhbWpVttvf8PGH.png)
</center>

I have been listening to a couple of podcasts where there are certain trainers that have stated that zone 2 cardio can be very beneficial for your endurance and all I can say is that I hope they are correct, because even though I was trying to get into zone 3 it just didn’t seem like it was going to happen and is unlikely to ever happen where I live since there are 8 million people here and virtually no open spaces.  

In the end my phone's evaluation of this one hour of exercise was a disappointing one and if there is one thing I really don't like to do it is to disappoint my apps!

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tkfYAJigVRZsnMGb5BEPrJxC1B9bbg2c3acsnukbZx9wXxb2tPMyrXd39d52Brbao99.png)
</center>

While these apps are not meant to be the truth, I have to say that I agree with the assertion that this activity should be considered a \
level of effort and no real gains can be expected from it.  However, if someone was in less of a cardiovascular \

than I am, perhaps their readout would be different.  While the computations these things do is meant to be quite complicated, all it is really doing is comparing your heart rate with your weight, age, and height.  So someone who is particularly overweight (i'm only a few kg over) this would probably be considered a much more intense level of exercise. 

I suppose this is one of the downsides of getting into better shape, it becomes increasingly difficult to find things that are really going to push your boundaries.  This was one thing I liked about when I was just lifting... there is always a couple more plates you can throw on a lift.   

I will likely only go cycling on days where I have a pain in my legs from running because I don't really consider it to be real exercise.

body.title: Bullying Is Not Just Play , My Honest Take. LOH#286
body.body:
School bullying is something that I really dislike, It bothers me a lot because it can affect someone's confidence and mental health for for a very long time, Some people think that it is not a big deal and say it is just kids being kids,  but that is not true at all, Bullying can be very harmful, It is not kids or people joking around.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSHQeAd7baUW3uKiLdG5CSq5tsWwQ7QfsrAkA4Dof9Ldz/1777277902949.jpg)

For me, I feel like bullying is not just about the person doing it, but also about the environment that allows it to happen, If a school doesn’t take it seriously, it just keeps growing, that is why I believe schools need to be more active, not just reacting when something bad happens, but actually creating awareness, setting clear rules, and making students feel safe enough to speak up.

So if my child came to me and said they were being bullied, seriously I would listen to them carefully, I would not just tell them to be strong or ignore it, I would make sure they know I am on their side, because that I will help them, then I would tell them to report the bullying to a teacher , counselor or the principal in the school, My child should not have to deal with bullying of any sort.

I would not just wait for the school to fix the problem, I would go to the school, Talk to the teachers If necessary then I would also meet with the parents of the child who is bullying, I would be serious, I would make sure they understand that bullying is not acceptable, If anything happens to my child I would hold them responsible, sometimes people only listen when you are serious.

I would also teach my child to stand up for themselves but not by fighting, I would teach them to be confident and not to tolerate disrespect from anyone at all,  Bullies often pick on people who do not stand up for themselves, I would also remind my child that it is okay to ask for help, they do not have to handle everything

I think we should start teaching kids about kindness, respect and empathy when they're young, this can help reduce bullying,sometimes bullies are acting out because of things they have seen or that they have experienced.

At the end of the day bullying is something that should be taken seriously, No child deserves to feel unsafe or uncomfortable at school, As a parent I would do everything I can to make sure my child feels protected and heard, school bullying is a problem and we need to do something about it, We need to make sure our kids feel safe and supported, SchoolSchool bullying is not just a kids problem , it is a problem, for all of us. We need to work to stop any form of bullying whatsoever.

[Image Credit](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-red-sign-that-says-no-to-bullying-XUdthBA01CM)

body.title: Comensando la semana con un nbuen jugo de almendrasºººººStarting the week with a good almond juice
body.body:
Hola a todos, la verdad amigos siempre cuando se habla del comienzo de la semana, en lo personal lo concidero muy bueno, por el solo hecho de que se me hace que esa energia que obtenemos por ser lunes el primer dia de la semana, nos seguira durante toda la misma o sea la semana, con esto quiero decirles que estoy hablando de un buen jugo, el cual consiste en almendras, a las que una ves bien molidas, las llevo a la licuadora, donde agrego muy poca agua y la licuo durante unos minutos, para que la misma se disuelva muy bien.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/Eoc8wBoP7Q2G7g3RMDJDmncS1wM1agZsUeLjT2J8XL2pDP9apqqA96qmPjTQ6MWnpC1.png)

Luego una ves que tenemos dicha almendras en la licuadora y bien disuelta, como se ve parece leche, pero no lo es, es dicha almendra, la cual la paso por un colador de tela muy fino, para que de esa manera salga solamente el jugo, el resto que queda en el colador, una ves que pase todo, lo paso nuevamente por la licuadora, agregandole un poco de agua, asi no se desperdicia nada.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EowGCHUpBk9QRzvWYCNrebdygCDd72UcNJoN4cbLDA6CL6jdRZsgaLQXtXSJGFkVHgG.png)

Una ves que licuo y paso todo por el colador, queda de esta manera amigos, como lo vemos en esta fotografia, bueno siempre tiene un poco de espuma, la verdad salio excelente y muy sabroso.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoeGQCrXfQfEC5mmyMD69fmEQKAbxWHNFohoMnMSLeksnnzY4WAYm5aXn3XAzXToVzB.png)

Asi que dicho jugo, se lo puede tomar despues del desayuno o asimismo como desayuno, acompañandolo con una tostada y puede ser con una variedad de comidas.

MUCHAS GRACIAS POR SEGUIRME Y LEERME, QUE TENGAN BUEN COMIENZO DE SEAMANA.

ENGLISH


Hello everyone, the truth is that whenever we talk about the beginning of the week, I personally consider it very good, simply because I feel that the energy we get from Monday being the first day of the week will carry us thru the entire week. With this, I want to tell you that I am talking about a good juice, which consists of almonds. Once they are well ground, I put them in the blender, where I add very little water and blend it for a few minutes so that it dissolves very well.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/Eoc8wBoP7Q2G7g3RMDJDmncS1wM1agZsUeLjT2J8XL2pDP9apqqA96qmPjTQ6MWnpC1.png)

Then, once we have the almonds in the blender and well blended, it looks like milk, but it isn't, it's the almonds. I strain it thru a very fine cloth strainer so that only the juice comes out. The rest that remains in the strainer, once everything has passed thru, I put it back in the blender, adding a little water, so nothing goes to waste.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EowGCHUpBk9QRzvWYCNrebdygCDd72UcNJoN4cbLDA6CL6jdRZsgaLQXtXSJGFkVHgG.png)

Once I blended and strained everything, it looks like this, friends, as we see in this photograph. Well, it always has a bit of foam. Honestly, it turned out excellent and very tasty.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoeGQCrXfQfEC5mmyMD69fmEQKAbxWHNFohoMnMSLeksnnzY4WAYm5aXn3XAzXToVzB.png)

So, that juice can be taken after breakfast or even as breakfast, accompanied by a toast and it can be with a variety of foods.

Thank you very much for following and reading me, have a great start to the week.
